water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Drought harms the investment mainly by leaving it without water or unbuilt. In Kenya, a drought season's poor rainfall generated very little runoff and the earth dam barely held any water [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6]. In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in the governorate of Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Neither unit measures structural damage to built works: the Kenyan dam was intact but empty, a loss of function for that season, and the Tunisian figure comes from a single ex-post review of project completion data on works that were never built [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2]. Units about benefits shrinking in drought are effect units recording a benefit shortfall, not damage, and practitioner coping ratings are not counted here.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms overtop, breach or collapse works: storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope, tied ridges in a Kenyan trial collapsed in heavy rainfall events and had to be rebuilt within the season, and poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av, ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av]. In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av], and a check-dam review links failures worldwide to extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge zaï pits, contour stone bunds, semi-circular bunds, contour bunds and Vallerani trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1614_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1652_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1613_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm]. A review of farming terraces adds that soil saturation in very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and that with heavy rainfall shallow terrace landslides can become debris flows that affect the entire terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Compilers for jessour and gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dams and bench terraces in China, sand dams in Kenya, spate irrigation in Eritrea, stone-covered bench terraces in Yemen and vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti judge them to cope well with rainstorms, and those for terraces in Thailand and Bangladesh and marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan to cope very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1400_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm]; weirs in Ethiopia, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso are rated as coping moderately [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1528_2012_local_rainstorm]. The literature ties damage to upkeep and construction quality: the Algerian failures concern poorly maintained banquettes, the Spanish landslides poorly structured terraces, and the check-dam failures lack of maintenance as well as extreme rain [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Most units are compiler ratings or manual and review statements rather than damage records, the only field observation is from a single Kenyan trial, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, trenches) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure [ev_climate_shock_ndun23_1_av, ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7]. The terrace riser and debris-flow statements are general review findings with no damage count or location [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. In Morocco staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of rains below 50 mm, but in the biggest storms the excess overtops the bunds and gullies the slope [ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both are expert or survey statements without damage counts; the Algerian failure is explicitly tied to poor maintenance, and the Moroccan statement implies the bunds hold for ordinary rains and fail only in the largest storms [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_roos10_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau with few local funds to repair it, and WOCAT compilers judge pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, radical terraces in Rwanda, gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and ripper tillage in Zambia not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1219_2014_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1139_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers in Tunisia, Eritrea, Kenya, Yemen, Uganda, India, Madagascar and Ethiopia judge coping as good, and those in Burkina Faso, Bangladesh and Somalia as moderate; the Haiti and Bangladesh terrace sheets judge coping with landslides as very good [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_landslide]. All units except the Loess Plateau observation are practitioner judgements without damage records, and for field-level practices a not-well rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Heavy storms damage the structures themselves. A review of farming terraces finds that soil saturation from very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and that with heavy rainfall the shallow landslides normally confined to small parts of a terrace can become debris flows affecting the entire terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av]. A worldwide review of check dams notes that cases of check-dam inefficacy are common and often associated with structure failures in response to extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Both sources are reviews describing failure modes, not measurements of how often or how badly structures fail, so the strength is not quantified; the check-dam statement is the authors' assertion and couples extreme rainfall with lack of maintenance, so the causes are not separated [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Terrace riser failure is also tied to runoff accumulating behind the walls, which drainage and upkeep influence [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the WOCAT compiler for stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde judges them not to cope well with local rainstorms, and in Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Compilers judge check dams and progressive bench terraces in China to cope well, and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand and the marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan to cope very well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5860_2021_local_rainstorm]. The units are compiler ratings and a secondary statement from an Algerian evaluation that links the failure to poor maintenance, not measurements of damage [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with forest fire and well with land fire, and stone check walls and check dams in India as coping well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings from two technology sheets with no observed damage; earth and stone works offer little to burn, so any fire effect would fall on vegetation on or around them.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, check-dam failure releases stored sediment, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. On China's Loess Plateau, sediment-filled check dams are vulnerable to large floods: more than 200 mm of rain falling on 26 July 2017 in Suide and Zizhou counties produced a flood that damaged 20% of the main check dams [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, check dams in Tunisia, China and India, and spate or water-spreading systems in Eritrea and Sudan to cope well, those for marab and Vallerani systems in Jordan and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well, and those for weirs in Ethiopia and works in Somalia to cope moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]; these are practitioner judgements from technology sheets, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds, trenches) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure. Literature failures are tied to maintenance and design: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees, the Moroccan earth check dams need frequent upkeep, and on the Loess Plateau it was the dams already filled with sediment that were vulnerable, the authors recommending side spillways [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av, ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. The boulder-impact and sediment-release statements are secondary citations or come from a USA study, and the Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Intense runoff overwhelms or breaks structures: floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, large floods could wash out traditional spate diversions in Yemen, banquettes in Niger lack capacity for erosive rains and overflow, in Rwanda a very rainy week can carry away all the small terraces on a slope without trees in a mass movement, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are fragile during major floods [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge jessour in Tunisia, zaï pits, bunds and Nardi/Vallerani trenches in Niger, the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, check dam ponds in Ethiopia, radical terraces in Rwanda, and gully-plugging check dams in Nepal not to cope well with river or flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1219_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1613_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1528_2012_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers judge water spreading in Sudan, spate irrigation in Eritrea, a gabion check dam and stone lines in Tunisia, sand dams in Kenya, stone check walls and check dams in India and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan to cope well, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia and haffir and gabion works in Somalia to cope moderately, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia to cope very well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1400_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5210_2019_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6715_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7778_2026_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood]. Most units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets or manuals, not measurements, and for field-level practices (pits, bunds) a not-well rating describes exposure of fields to floodwater rather than damage to a structure; the Moroccan statement ties fragility to maintenance, the Yemen statement describes diversions before project improvements, and the Ethiopian log-dam failure rate is reported second-hand in a review [ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: A review of terraces names torrential rain, together with the collapse of walls and vegetation strips and use after abandonment, among the conditions that degrade terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3]. WOCAT compilers judge a check dam for land in China and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde to cope well with river floods, and marab floodplain agriculture and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchments in Jordan to cope very well with flash floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1455_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5860_2021_flash_flood]. On China's Loess Plateau, sediment-filled check dams are vulnerable to large floods: heavy rain on 26 July 2017 in Suide and Zizhou counties caused a large flood that damaged 20% of the main check dams [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The pool is small: apart from the review and the Loess Plateau damage count, it consists of practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets rather than measured damage, and the review ties damage to abandonment as much as to rainfall. The Loess Plateau damage hit dams already filled with sediment, so it is partly a design-life and maintenance effect [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3]. The Jordanian ratings carry no damage signal at all.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan records that the technology copes very well with extreme winter conditions [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a frost sensitivity: one practitioner rating from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band, with no observed damage and no frost event described, so it does not show the works go undamaged elsewhere [ev_asset_frost_wocat_5860_2021_extreme_winter_conditions]. What is missing is a second independent source or one observed account of frost damage or its absence.

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage, for a structure of stone and wire that heat would affect mainly through the vegetation around it [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av]. Among WOCAT compilers, stone check walls and check dams in India are rated as coping only moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Other compilers rate stone lines in Tunisia, a masonry check dam in Ethiopia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand as coping well, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh as coping very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment, not to maintained terraces, and the ratings come from a small set of technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. In Tigray, Gebremeskel et al. cite Berhane et al. (2016) for siltation threatening the benefits of 61% of surveyed micro-dams, ahead of leakage and structural damage [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5]. On China's Loess Plateau high sediment loads fill check dams rapidly, so their trapping gives only short-term erosion-control benefit [ev_climate_shock_shi19_4]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime, and an Indian review cites Gunnell and Krishnamurthy (2003) that all rainwater-harvesting structures need regular silt clearing to stay functional and maximise recharge [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av]. On Ethiopian highland bunds, a filled drainage ditch quickly lowers sediment-trapping efficiency and adds pressure that can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. In Burkina Faso the 2- and 3-m half-moon plots showed lower infiltration than the control plots, likely due to suspended matter that clogs the soil during sedimentation [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units, including the Tigray and Indian maintenance statements, are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. The half-moon clogging is a loss of infiltration in the larger basins, with a likely cause the authors name but do not test, not a structural failure [ev_soil_permeability_zour25h1_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.mechanism: No unit describes how wind damages the works; the row rests on WOCAT compiler judgements of how terraces, bunds, pits, check dams, sand dams and spate systems cope with local windstorms and tropical storms. Most are judged to cope well, while progressive bench terraces in China and fascine vegetative check dams in Madagascar are judged not to cope well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__asset_thr.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements from documented technology sheets, not measurements; compilers for bench terraces in Bangladesh and gabion works in Somalia judge coping as moderate, and the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso is judged to cope very well [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1528_2012_local_windstorm]. For field-level practices such as pits and bunds a rating describes exposure of fields rather than damage to a structure.

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: In Burkina Faso the proximity of zai pits on bare, crusted land raises germination and seed dispersal, so herbaceous and woody species re-establish on formerly barren fields, and users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. WOCAT compilers give a mechanism with each rating: in Somalia improved soil moisture and reduced erosion supported more plant and grass species, and restored vegetation and water availability improved habitat for livestock and small wildlife; in Bhutan the soil became suitable for more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: The class is set by the sub-practice vote: the in-field and runoff-storage rows are slight, and the terracing row is conflicting, because a Bhutan compiler rating of more diverse crops stands against an Israeli finding of lost herbaceous species on machine-built terraces; the pooled evidence alone would read stronger [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9]. The WOCAT units are compiler ratings from technology sheets in Somalia and Bhutan, not measurements, and the Somali sheet supplies separate plant, animal and habitat ratings; the Bhutan rating refers to more diverse crops rather than wild species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. The literature units are descriptive species counts or user perceptions with no untreated comparison, and the zai counts partly restate the same earlier observation [ev_biodiversity_outcome_kabo04_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_zoug14_1, ev_biodiversity_outcome_roose93_1]. The barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, and the gain comes through the gardens and orchards on the humid fringe rather than the basin itself [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3]. The harm comes from how the works are built: in Israel, earthen contour bench terraces built with heavy machinery strip the soil's A-horizon, and these earthworks have been suggested to reduce herbaceous species richness (Stavi et al., 2015, cited in the later Stavi et al. review) [ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9].

water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.mechanism: Consecutive years of zai planting pits on formerly bare, barren soil in central Burkina Faso were followed by the re-establishment of herbaceous species and of trees and shrubs.
water_harvesting_conservation__biodivers.conditionality: Both units are secondary citations of earlier zai field observations from Burkina Faso, probably overlapping, reporting species counts on treated land without an untreated comparison or a biodiversity index; the strength of the effect is not quantified.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: Carbon removals come from more vegetation and more soil organic matter on treated land. WOCAT compilers attribute storage gains to vegetation: the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso raises biomass production many times over nearby unploughed soil, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase biomass and, through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, soil organic matter, a haffir in Somalia allows vegetation cover to regenerate, and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan add below-ground organic matter through expanding roots [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_1528_2012_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The Somali compiler adds that vegetation recovery and increased biomass store more carbon in plants and soils by absorbing carbon dioxide from the atmosphere [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases]. In the literature zai fields in Burkina Faso treated for several years had higher organic matter while trenches combined with vegetation raised soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. In Burkina Faso, soils on farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3], and a review cites climate-smart packages of soil and water conservation structures with biological measures boosting soil carbon stock by three to seven times over business-as-usual [ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The WOCAT units are compiler ratings from technology sheets in Burkina Faso, Somalia, Uzbekistan and Bhutan, not measurements, and soil organic matter and emission ratings are proxies rather than measured carbon storage; the Bhutan sheet describes organic matter moving downslope within each terrace, a redistribution rather than a net removal [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. The literature is mixed: trenches in Mexico lowered soil nitrogen and carbon, and a zai trial in Burkina Faso found no significant change in organic matter by the end of the experiment even though biomass rose [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_roose93_1]. The Loess Plateau check-dam finding is a secondary citation in a review, with no magnitude in the quoted passage [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. The Chinese figures come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country. Several are the values for the duration window with the greatest increase rather than a pooled estimate, and the duration subsets overlap the regional ones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. The Burkina Faso result is a carbon content on farm soils, not a stock change, and the three-to-sevenfold stock gain is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures, very large for structures and to be read with caution [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3]. Paired soil samples from Zambian fields under planting basins or ripping (bundled with reduced tillage), with crop residues hardly retained, showed no significant difference in organic carbon from conventional fields [ev_soil_organic_carbon_umar11_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In semi-arid settings the practices add carbon removals mainly through soil storage: organic matter concentrated in zaï pits raised soil organic matter content from 1 to 1.4 percent on soils treated 3 and 5 years earlier in Burkina Faso, and farms using zaï and/or rock bunds there had more soil carbon than a control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau store carbon in the sediment trapped behind them, and that storage increases with time at both check dam and watershed levels [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit states how large the carbon removal is per hectare or per year: the zaï figure is an organic-matter content change cited second-hand from an earlier study, the Burkina Faso farm comparison is a soil-fertility test against a single control farm, and the Loess Plateau statement is a review citation [ev_soil_organic_carbon_kabo04_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. Soil organic matter and trapped sediment stand in for a measured carbon stock change, and carbon in check-dam sediment partly moves carbon eroded from upslope rather than removing new carbon from the air.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: Soil carbon storage is the carbon removal at stake here, and in-field works can add to it by returning more crop residue and organic matter to the soil. In Kenya, soil organic carbon at the end of the fallow stage under plastic-film ridge-furrow rainwater harvesting was on average 7.5% (transparent film) and 13.7% (black film) greater than under flat planting [ev_soil_organic_carbon_mo17_5]. In Burkina Faso, farms using zaï and rock bunds with compost had higher soil carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Studies disagree on whether the stock grows. On the storage side are the Kenyan end-of-fallow measurements and the Burkina Faso farm comparison [ev_soil_organic_carbon_mo17_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3]; on the loss side, the same Kenyan trial found soil organic carbon consumption during the growing seasons 61.6% (transparent film) and 4.0% (black film) greater than under flat planting [ev_soil_organic_carbon_mo17_6]. What separates them is when and what is measured: the film-mulched ridges speed up the draw-down of soil carbon while the crop grows, and the gain appears only after the fallow, so whether the soil ends up storing more carbon depends on the balance across the full year and on the film type. The Burkina Faso contrast bundles the structures with compost, against a single control farm, so it does not isolate the water-harvesting works, and no unit measures carbon over more than a few seasons.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: In low-income settings the pathway is zai pits building soil organic matter over time, with organic matter and nitrogen higher on fields treated for several years.
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: Both units are zai in Burkina Faso and measure soil organic matter, a proxy for carbon; one is a secondary citation of an earlier study and the other, a controlled trial, found no significant change in organic matter after two years.

water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.mechanism: Carbon removal here is soil storage, plus carbon held in trapped sediment: a review of infiltration trenches reports that trenches combined with vegetation raised soil nutrients including soil organic carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. A meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures, available as a preprint, finds soil organic carbon 10.74% to 22.63% above the initial level after straw mulching across regions, and 3.36% and 75.77% higher after contour tillage in two regions within 5 to 10 years [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_1, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_2, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_4]. The same preprint meta-analysis finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. A Chinese meta-analysis, available as a preprint, reports fish-scale pits raising soil organic carbon storage by 79.86% on the Loess Plateau in years 11~30 [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__carbon_se.conditionality: The trench review also reports that trenches in Mexico actually decreased soil nitrogen and carbon, so the trench evidence is split [ev_soil_organic_carbon_locat20_2]. Soil organic carbon gains stand in for carbon removal; none of the units reports a net greenhouse-gas balance. The Loess Plateau check-dam result is a secondary citation without a magnitude in the quoted passage [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1]. The Chinese figures come from a preprint that has not been peer reviewed, in an upper-middle-income country. Several are the values for the duration window with the greatest increase rather than a pooled estimate, and the duration subsets overlap the regional ones [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_12]. In this scope the preprint carries most of the measured signal.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Groundwater recharge now counts as a component of catchment water yield, so this row holds two kinds of evidence. Most units report recharge and rising water tables at or near capture structures: the proportion of runoff infiltrated through check dams can reach more than 50%, with recharge linked to episodic storm events [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1]; groundwater tables rise in the vicinity of filled check dams, and sand dams can raise the local groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, groundwater levels rose in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters, and a state survey found levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], and ISRO survey data record increased recharge in treated areas [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, and modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]; stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level, and in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; communities in Mauritania, spate beneficiaries in Yemen and an Ethiopian public-works assessment report rising well levels, increased groundwater or water-table improvements [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]; and a review lists aquifer recharge among benefits cited for water harvesting [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_saru19_1]. Reductions are measured on flow leaving the treated land: On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], and in the Maghreb mechanised bund systems, built with large machines that scrape a 4 to 10 m strip to raise bunds 1.5 to 2 m high every 30 to 50 m, considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs and cost 10 to 25% of the cultivable area [ev_water_yield_roos10_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6]. Reviews of Indian studies add recharge figures: about 3–8% of rainfall from well measurements near structures (Badiger et al. 2002), 11% of annual rainfall per structure in Gujarat (Sharda et al. 2006) and around 7% in the Arvari watershed (Glendenning and Vervoort 2010), and an overall 16% increase in recharge across 16 observation wells in Maharashtra, equal to 2% of local annual rainfall (Gore et al. 1998) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_4]; in Ethiopia's Mendae catchment recharge rose from 8 mm before water-harvesting interventions to 107.7 mm after (Negusse et al. 2013) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]; sand dams in Kenya enhance groundwater recharge (Hut et al. 2008) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27]; and seepage from a Burkina Faso farm pond is described as recharging the groundwater [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8]. The reductions are now more numerous, mostly modelled and mostly Indian: watershed development including more rainwater harvesting was estimated to cut runoff by approximately 60% while raising recharge by only 5% (Sharma and Thakur 2007), rainwater harvesting was suggested to close a basin in Andhra Pradesh so that no more water flowed downstream (Calder et al. 2008), it reduced streamflow in the Arvari model (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011), a global model put the average reduction in annual river flows at 18% with up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al. 2010), water outflows from treated catchments were halved against untreated ones (Garg et al. 2012; Gates et al. 2011), and investment in water harvesting upstream is cited as cutting runoff generation for downstream users [ev_water_yield_glen12_2, ev_water_yield_glen12_5, ev_water_yield_glen12_7, ev_water_yield_glen12_10, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The studies found real effects in both directions, and what separates them is where and at what scale they measure. The gains are recharge and well levels at or near the structures; the losses are streamflow, runoff and reservoir inflow below large-scale or basin-wide works — a check-dam campaign built to retain floodwater, mechanised bunds, and Indian watershed development modelled at catchment scale, where the main change in the water balance was more evapotranspiration [ev_water_yield_glen12_2]. Both can hold at once: the Arvari model found rainwater harvesting reduced streamflow while making groundwater more reliable [ev_water_yield_glen12_7], and the global model that cut river flows also raised crop production [ev_water_yield_glen12_10]. Scale matters on the recharge side too: a theoretical model found the impact on water levels minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of a structure (Neumann et al. 2004) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8], and other catchment studies found intensified small-scale upstream water management had limited or no downstream impact on stream flows (Schreider et al. 2002; De Winnaar and Jewitt 2010; Andersson et al. 2011) [ev_water_yield_dile13_10], as did a water-harvesting review for widely implemented small-scale storage [ev_water_yield_rock10_1]; trenches in the Peruvian Andes had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. For a Task Team Leader the practical reading is that dispersed small structures mainly recharge local aquifers, while basin-wide intensification can take water from downstream users and calls for a basin water balance before scaling up. The recharge side has limits in its own sources: the sand-dam effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]; in India, pumping from tube wells that land-owning farmers sank as the water table rose has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge from the watershed treatments, and without data from untreated sites the project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]; and catchment-level recharge gains in the Andes are plausible but cannot be generalised [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. Most recharge units are secondary citations, programme reports or modelling, the Mendae figure is a before-and-after water balance cited in a review, and the Burkina Faso pond recharge is inferred from seepage losses rather than measured [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8]. On the loss side, the 39% is a figure the check-dam review cites from another study (Shi et al., 2015) for one Chinese region [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], the Maghreb reduction is a narrative from a Moroccan expert manual with no figure for the water lost downstream, the 10 to 25% being cultivable area rather than water [ev_water_yield_roos10_1], and the Indian reductions are model results cited in reviews, including a basin closure that later reversed as the structures silted up [ev_water_yield_glen12_5]. The digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. The barraginha recharge statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement behind it [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In the Sahel, stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1], and in Burkina Faso levels of water in wells have improved, which the source links not to higher rainfall but to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Both sides are real findings in semi-arid land, and what separates them is the outcome measured, the place and the scale of the works. The gain is groundwater and well levels on and around treated Sahelian fields and watersheds [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; the loss is streamflow below a campaign of check dams built at very large scale in China to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. For a downstream user the Chinese finding is the relevant one; for a farmer near the works the Sahelian one is. Neither side compares with and without the works at catchment scale: the Sahelian units are cited statements, the 39% is cited by a review from another study, and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly since SWC began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. A further Burkina Faso statement, cited from another study with no figures, also sits on the gain side [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Water held on the land seeps down to the groundwater that villages draw on. In Burkina Faso, Fox and Rockström observe that seepage from a farm pond need not be lost to the household because it recharges the groundwater, at a time when some village wells run dry during parts of the year [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8]. Sawadogo cites studies such as Reij and Thombiano (2003) showing that soil and water conservation techniques, especially the large permeable rock dams known as digues filtrantes, improve groundwater availability in many villages [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Neither unit measures recharge or water yield: the farm-pond statement is the authors' inference from measured seepage losses, and the rock-dam finding is cited without figures, so the strength is not quantified [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. Both come from Burkina Faso and describe recharge near the works; neither says what happens to flow reaching streams or users further downstream.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock settings the evidence is thin and points both ways. On the recharge side, recharge in Ethiopia's Mendae catchment rose from 8 mm before water-harvesting interventions to 107.7 mm after, by water balance (Negusse et al. 2013, cited in a review) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11], and Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6]. On the other side, studies cited in the same review (Garg et al. 2012; Gates et al. 2011) found water outflows from treated catchments halved against untreated ones, a potential loss for downstream users [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: What separates the sides is where the water is measured: the gains are recharge within the treated catchment, the loss is outflow leaving it, so both can hold at once and the row cannot say whether downstream users gain or lose. Every unit is a second-hand citation or an agency's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Capturing runoff upstream moves water from the stream into the ground. On the recharge side, works that hold water on the land let it infiltrate and raise local water tables: in Maharashtra a groundwater model of 16 observation wells found an overall increase in recharge from rainwater harvesting of 16% (Gore et al., 1998, cited by Glendenning et al.), well measurements near structures put recharge at about 3–8% of rainfall (Badiger et al., 2002), and in Ethiopia's Mendae catchment a water balance gave groundwater recharge of 107.7 mm after water harvesting against 8 mm before (Negusse et al., 2013, cited by Gebremeskel et al.) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]. Terraces in the Mandara mountains are reported to recharge the water table by 15 to 25% of rainfall (Hiol Hiol and Mietton, cited by Roose), modelling of contour ridges in Morocco estimates a 50% rise in recharge (cited by Willems et al.), and check dams and other structures in Saurashtra were estimated to add 480 million cubic meters of recharge per annum (Jain, 2012, cited by Verma and Shah) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1]. In Rajasthan piezometers recorded groundwater rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts by an average of 1.42 meters, and after tank desilting in Telangana a state survey found levels up in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]; a water budget for Uttarakhand's watershed project put aquifer recharge 3.3 percent above baseline [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]. Rising well levels are also reported around stone bunds, zaï and half-moons in Burkina Faso, earth and stone bunds in Mauritania, spate and conservation structures in Yemen, filled check dams (Frankl et al., 2016; Lucas-Borja et al., 2018), sand dams (Hut et al., 2008), and Ethiopian public-works watersheds where a better water table allowed small-scale irrigation [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mrt14_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7], and a Burkina Faso farm-pond study treats seepage from the reservoir as recharge rather than lost water [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8]. On the outflow side, the same capture reduces the water that leaves the catchment: a GIS and water-balance study estimated that watershed development including more rainwater harvesting would cut runoff by approximately 60% while raising recharge by only 5% (Sharma and Thakur, 2007), a global model suggested rainwater harvesting would reduce annual river flows by 18% on average and by up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al., 2010), and in Andhra Pradesh it was suggested to cause basin closure (Calder et al., 2008), all cited by Glendenning et al. [ev_water_yield_glen12_2, ev_water_yield_glen12_10, ev_water_yield_glen12_5]. Outflows from treated catchments have been found halved compared with untreated ones (Garg et al., 2012; Gates et al., 2011, cited by Gebremeskel et al.), reviews cite decreased runoff generation harming downstream systems, a Rajasthan model found rainwater harvesting reducing streamflow, and in Morocco mechanised bunds considerably reduce the water collected in downstream hill reservoirs (Albergel et al., 2004, cited by Roose et al.) [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9, ev_water_yield_glen12_7, ev_water_yield_roos10_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: Studies disagree on the direction because they measure different water. The recharge side counts water entering the ground near the works; the outflow side counts water leaving the catchment for downstream users, and the same capture can raise the first while lowering the second, as in the watershed where runoff fell by about 60% and recharge rose by only 5%, with most of the change going to evapotranspiration [ev_water_yield_glen12_2]. Scale and intensity separate them too: several studies find limited or no downstream impact from small-scale water storage even when implemented widely (Evenari et al., 1971; Schreider et al., 2002; Sreedevi et al., 2006; De Winnaar and Jewitt, 2010; Andersson et al., 2011) [ev_water_yield_rock10_1, ev_water_yield_dile13_10], a theoretical model found the effect on water levels minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of a structure (Neumann et al., 2004) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8], while the large flow reductions come from intensive watershed development, basin-wide models and mechanised bunds. Siltation of the structures can also reverse basin closure by letting downstream flows rise again [ev_water_yield_glen12_5]. The recharge gains are not secure: in Burkina Faso a reconnaissance of 59 villages found that the number of wells with water year-round had not increased significantly since soil and water conservation began [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]; in India the survey data showed more recharge in treated areas but had no untreated sites, and tube-well pumping encouraged by subsidised electricity has possibly wiped out the gains [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4]. Most units on both sides are second-hand citations, models or self-reported project results (the Uttarakhand, Mauritania and Yemen figures come from World Bank completion reports), and few measure both recharge and downstream flow in the same catchment. This row is for downstream users and basin planners; spring and stream discharge gains near treated watersheds are local supply and are reported in the water stress rows, not here.

water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.mechanism: Upstream capture can both add to and take from downstream water. On China's Loess Plateau, a large campaign of check-dam construction carried out since the 1970s to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1]. On the other side, Embrapa says its barraginhas in Brazil help recharge groundwater by raising the water table and revitalise springs and rivers [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6], and in the Peruvian Andes a few studies have observed catchment-level changes such as reduced quick runoff or increased aquifer recharge, which the source calls plausible but not generalisable [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__catchment.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. The sides now conflict, and what separates them is what is measured and at what scale: the loss is streamflow below a check-dam campaign at very large scale built to retain floodwater [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], while the gains are recharge and water-table statements for small dispersed basins and trenches [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1]. In the Peruvian Andes trenches had little effect on increasing baseflow, with hydrogeological characteristics key to explaining their impact [ev_water_regulation_locat20_1]. None of this is a measured project comparison: the 39% is a secondary citation in a global review, the Peruvian statements are a review's summary, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_water_yield_luca21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_locat20_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In a Kenyan catchment, low-cost water measures built around sand dams are estimated to have given more than 100,000 people better access to water within 10 years at an investment of about 35 USD per capita [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: This is a single estimate from a single study, with no stated currency year, expressed per person gaining water access rather than per farmer or household, so it covers the water-access benefit only [ev_project_cost_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: The pooled costs are up-front establishment or treatment costs per hectare. In Ethiopia, the initial investment in terracing was equivalent to US$ 46.51 per hectare in the first year of construction, with about US$ 48.8 per hectare needed to maintain it over the first three years [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]. Indian watershed projects treated sub-watersheds at US$261 and US$217 per hectare [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11], and spate systems in Yemen averaged USD 800-1200 per hectare to build, of which farmers paid 15-20% [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. WOCAT compilers report establishment costs per hectare of 147.30 USD for gully works in Somalia, 345 and 1293 USD for technologies in Jordan and 2000 USD in Uzbekistan [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment]. At the high end, rehabilitating pre-Columbian andenes in Peru cost USD 2,200 per hectare, and a review tabulates terracing costs in China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare, rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The small cost class reflects the lower figures from Ethiopia, India, Yemen and Somalia; the Peru and China costs come from upper-middle-income settings, and the Jordan, Uzbekistan, Peru and China figures sit well above the rest [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1]. These are establishment costs, not costs per hectare restored, and the spread is wide because the technologies differ from hand-built terraces to engineered spate systems; the Ethiopian terracing figure is for terraces built with unpaid community labour decades ago [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]. WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables converted to USD with the sheet's exchange rate, not market prices. The India costs are described by the evaluator as high by national norms, the Peru figure is a 1994 assessment cited secondhand, and the Chinese terracing costs are a secondary table showing that steeper land costs more to terrace [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In low- and lower-middle-income settings the pooled per-hectare costs are up-front establishment and treatment costs. An independent evaluation of two World Bank-supported India watershed projects reports treatment unit costs of US$261 per hectare in the Integrated Watershed Development Project and US$217/ha in the Karnataka project [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11]. A Yemen completion report gives average investment costs for spate systems of USD 800- 1200/ha, of which the farmer's 15-20% share comes to US$ 150-200/ha [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. Two WOCAT technology sheets add compiler-reported establishment costs: 2000.00 USD per hectare for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan, a total spread over 1.6 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment], and 147.30 USD per hectare for gabion and rock check-dam gully control in Somalia, a total spread over 160 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The figures measure different things: watershed treatment cost per hectare treated in India, spate-system investment in Yemen, and WOCAT compilers' own cost tables converted with each sheet's exchange rate, which are not market prices; none is a cost per hectare of degraded land restored, and no price-year adjustment is made across them. The India evaluator calls the US$261 per hectare cost high by Indian standards, and the US$217/ha cost below the central government norm [ev_project_cost_iegind11_10, ev_project_cost_iegind11_11]; the Yemen report calls the farmer contribution comparatively high [ev_project_cost_yem12_8]. The Somali figure spreads a whole gully-control package over the treated area, which keeps it low per hectare, while the Uzbek terrace figure is a small orchard plot, so the spread from 147.30 to 2000.00 USD per hectare reflects practice and denominator as much as cost. All four countries are in the low- or lower-middle-income target band.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings the pooled per-hectare costs are a 1994 rehabilitation cost for Andean terraces in Peru from an FAO manual and Jordanian WOCAT sheets for a floodplain marab system costed over its ten hectares and mechanised Vallerani micro-catchment trenching costed per hectare [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. A review adds terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare, rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_per_.conditionality: The Peruvian figure is a nominal 1994 cost for rehabilitating existing terraces rather than building new ones, and the Jordanian figures are the compilers' own cost tables converted at the sheets' stated rates, not market prices; all three sit outside the low- and lower-middle-income target band [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_establishment, ev_project_cost_wocat_5860_2021_establishment]. The Chinese figures are a secondary table and include socioeconomic costs alongside machinery and labour [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Water harvesting changes farm and programme costs in both directions. Practices that remove a step save money: in Mozambique labour costs were $153 per hectare for basins against $173 for conventional tillage, and in Ethiopia mulching reduced weed density and labour costs for weeding [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. Better siting saves on construction: in Karnataka, land-resource-inventory planning avoided unnecessary structures, so works cost INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the conventional programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]. Practices that add earthworks raise costs: switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, increased the cost of production in Ghana's Nandom area [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. In Ghana, the share of small dams rehabilitated for less than USD 5,000 per irrigated hectare was 25% under government and 12% under development partners [ev_project_cost_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: Studies disagree because they cost different practices. The savings come where the practice removes a step, such as tillage or hand weeding, or where planning avoids building structures; the increase comes where the practice adds ridging [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1, ev_project_cost_kar20_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The Karnataka saving is against another conservation programme, not against doing nothing, and comes from a World Bank completion report [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; the Ghana dam figures describe a spread of rehabilitation costs between implementers rather than a saving or an overrun [ev_project_cost_veno12_1]; the Mozambique basins also carry residue retention and herbicide weed control, and the Ethiopian statement gives no figure [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. Cost evidence is ordinal here: read the row as which practices tend to cut or add costs, not as a price.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: In-field water-harvesting practices both cut and raise the cost of production, depending on what they replace. Basins in Mozambique cost $153 per hectare in labour against $173 for conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]. Switching from flat-land production to tied ridges, with or without grass strips, raised the cost of production at Nandom in Ghana [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: What separates the two is whether the practice replaces tillage work or adds construction on top of it [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The Mozambique basins bundle basin digging with residue retention and herbicide weed control, and the Ghana cost rise is stated without a figure [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]. The row rests on two units from two sources; more costed comparisons for rainfed cropping are missing.

water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.mechanism: Studies disagree on whether the practices lower or raise what farmers and projects pay. On the saving side: in Karnataka, planning structures from a land-resource inventory cut construction cost to INR 14,228 per hectare against INR 18,739 under the comparison programme, a drop of 30 percent [ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; in Mozambique, labour for the basin practice averaged $153 against $173 per hectare under conventional tillage [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]; and in Ethiopia mulching reduced labour costs for weeding [ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1]. On the cost side: in Ghanaian trials, switching from flat-land production to tied ridges with or without grass strips increased the cost of production [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2]; and in Ghana most rehabilitated small dams cost USD 5,000 or more per irrigated hectare, with only 25% of government and 12% of donor-rehabilitated dams below that [ev_project_cost_veno12_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__cost_redu.conditionality: What separates the sides is whether the practice removes work or adds a structure. The savings come from basins that replace conventional tillage, mulch that suppresses weeds and better siting of structures, which save labour or construction cost [ev_project_cost_kida19_5, ev_project_cost_sime15h2_1, ev_project_cost_kar20_5]; the cost increases come from building ridges or rehabilitating dams [ev_project_cost_dalt14_2, ev_project_cost_veno12_1]. The Mozambique saving is bundled with reduced tillage, residue retention and herbicide weed control, so it is not a pure capture effect [ev_project_cost_kida19_5]. The Karnataka saving is a planning-efficiency comparison between programmes rather than a with-and-without contrast, and the Ghana dam costs are thresholds from a review rather than a comparison with an alternative [ev_project_cost_kar20_5, ev_project_cost_veno12_1]. For scoping, expect labour savings from in-field moisture practices and added establishment costs for built structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field pits and bunds let more rain infiltrate and stay in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years, and chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to conserve soil moisture and mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, and cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4]. Studies cited in conservation agriculture meta-analyses report yields 10–100% higher than conventional tillage in relatively dry years, a review notes soil and water conservation is particularly useful where rainfall is low or variable, and WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Somalia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_4, ev_crop_yield_rusin11_6, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies found yield improvements significantly higher in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter study years, and yield gains, though not significant, in below-average rainfall years [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. Second-hand citations add that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season (De Graaff, 2005, cited by Adgo et al.), that rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells (Kahinda et al., 2007, cited by Biazin et al.), and that a conceptual watershed model for the Arvari watershed in Rajasthan showed rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years (Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The class stops at moderate because the benefit fades as drought deepens and few of the supporting units say how big the gain is: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage reaches 50 mm, and a water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Storage runs out: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001 and small dams cannot sustain long dry spells, and four consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. In a semi-arid Kenyan season with a failed start, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize yields [ev_crop_yield_boil19_3]; in Ethiopia vegetation greenness in treated watersheds still tracked local drought severity [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Part of the pool is WOCAT compiler ratings, statements cited second-hand inside meta-analyses and reviews, an expert review, and bundled programmes in Rwanda and Ethiopia; the Brazilian cistern statement on livestock mortality in severe drought is a potential effect, not a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. The Zimbabwe water-productivity gain and the Rajasthan drought buffer are modelling results cited second-hand, the terracing statement gives no size, and the meta-analysis compares rainfall classes rather than drought and normal years on the same fields [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6, ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In semi-arid fields, pits and bunds raise infiltration and soil water retention so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1]. In semi-arid Brazil, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years, and production-cistern water is described as able to reduce animal mortality in more severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001 and small dams cannot sustain long dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]; and in a Kenyan season with a failed start and a long dry spell, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize yields, though the authors caution the yield data were aggregated [ev_crop_yield_boil19_3]. The positive units are field observations and secondary citations from West Africa, while the Brazilian statements are institutional assertions without data, the cistern statement framed as a potential effect [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Pits and bunds let more rain infiltrate and stay in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land where the without-zaï yield was 0, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years, and chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7].
