A water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, Rwandan project households proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought, and physical structures were reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Somalia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced and name the route: water stored in the soil profile, a pond that still holds water during drought, and more water captured and infiltrated [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage reaches 50 mm, and a water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Four consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits, conservation agriculture pillars had no detectable effect on maize in a Kenyan season with a failed start, and in Ethiopia vegetation greenness in treated watersheds still tracked local drought severity [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_crop_yield_boil19_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. The benefit holds against dry spells; at severe or extreme drought the measured results mostly show no benefit.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss during critical drought periods, and in Mediterranean long-term experiments cited in a no-till meta-analysis, wheat yields under no-till tended to be higher than under conventional tillage in years when water stress occurred [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The same experiments show no-till wheat yields lower than conventional tillage in years with little water stress [ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5]. Both units are secondary citations inside a review and a meta-analysis drawn from several countries, with no magnitude, so they show direction only [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Water-harvesting yield gains hold up in dry years: a meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia found significantly higher yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and yield gains also in below-average rainfall years, though not significant there [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid Brazil, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and production-cistern water is described as able to reduce animal mortality in more severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Adgo et al. cite Posthumus and De Graaff (2005), a Peruvian bench-terrace study, for terracing reducing the risk of crop failure during rainy-season dry spells through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Storage runs out in long droughts: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry up in the rainless year 2001, and small manually built dams cannot sustain long dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The meta-analysis compares drier against average rainfall years, pools in-soil and reservoir techniques, and its China-dominated upper-middle-income sample sets this row's scope while the African sub-sample is lower income; many of its observations also carried soil fertility treatment, which the authors control for [ev_crop_yield_boum16_3, ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. The Brazilian benefit units are institutional statements without data (the cistern statement framed as a potential effect), the Peruvian terrace finding is a secondary citation, and the dry-up findings come from field observation and family interviews [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The zaï and stone-bund yield figures come from one study, Kaboré and Reij, the stone-bund figure as restated by Zougmoré and colleagues, so they are not independent confirmations [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In Malawi's El Niño drought season ground cover (a soil-cover mulch, modelled separately from the other practices) raised maize from 247 kg per hectare on control plots to 432 kg per hectare and raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement [ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Storage works carry water into dry periods: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. The Vallerani-system compiler in Burkina Faso credits water storage in the soil profile, and the Uzbek orchard-terrace compiler notes that more water is captured and infiltrated [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. Sand dams carry water into drought years: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. Farmers practising basins in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Limpopo reported maize and sorghum yields of >1 tonnes per hectare even in seasons with poor rainfall (<450 mm), against total crop failure under conventional ploughing [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields too [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. In a Burkina Faso farm-pond trial, sorghum given supplemental irrigation from the harvested runoff yielded 680 against 443 kg per hectare in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per hectare in 2000, both seasons with serious dry spells [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial (Barron and Okwach), supplemental irrigation from a runoff-fed earth dam plus fertiliser raised maize yields over fertilised plots without irrigation in low-rainfall seasons (<300 mm) but not in seasons above 300 mm, and in a dry long-rains season only the irrigated plots produced any grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid north-east Nigeria, tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised sorghum grain yield by 67% over a flat bed in 1999, a season that ended in drought at grain filling [ev_crop_yield_chir06_6]. In southern Malawi's 2015/16 El Niño season, maize hybrids under conservation agriculture (planting in small holes with residue cover) yielded 700 kg per hectare more on average than under conventional ridge tillage [ev_crop_yield_seti18_1]. A terracing study citing De Graaff (2005) states that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A risk model of a Burkina Faso farm reservoir, built on field experience, finds all mild dry spells mitigated by supplemental irrigation and severe late dry spells reduced to mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A watershed model of the Arvari in Rajasthan (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011, cited in a review) found rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores, despite reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. A survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe (Kahinda et al. 2007, cited in a review) found rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The benefit shrinks or vanishes in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage is sufficient, and in Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment in a season heavily affected by drought [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. A water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through water management but crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Storage also runs out, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. The pool includes on-farm or trial measurements from Malawi, Kenya, Zimbabwe and Mozambique, alongside WOCAT compiler ratings and institutional assertions; the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, the Indian pond figures come from a preprint farmer survey, the sand-dam figures rest on recall interviews, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian programme results come from bundled programmes [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. Not every in-field practice helped in that Malawi El Nino season: banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare and lowered the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. In the Zimbabwe panel conservation agriculture had no specific impact in mitigating rainfall-shortfall losses for millet and groundnut [ev_crop_yield_mich19_6]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. The farmer-reported basin yields compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author warns makes those datasets too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. In Zimbabwe first-year planting-basin farmers obtained 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 368 kg on conventional plots in the 2006/07 season, which the source calls a drought year [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 2.53 against 1.82 t per hectare without inputs (not significant) and 4.10 against 3.15 t per hectare with manure and fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3]. Storage practices — ponds, cisterns, sand and subsurface dams — work instead through water kept for later use: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells, Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without, production-cistern water for livestock can reduce animal deaths in severe drought and pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Cambodia, Somalia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced, the Burkina Faso compiler noting that in years of extreme drought most plants survived and were used to feed animals [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Chololo pits in Tanzania are reported to mitigate drought effects [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_7]. Against the fertilised conventional arm in the same Zimbabwe budget the contrast was 1520 against 400 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In on-farm conservation-farming trials in Kenya, Tanzania and Ethiopia the largest yield difference over conventional ploughing came in rainy seasons with low rainfall, when the practice maximises rainfall infiltration so the crop can bridge short periods of dry spell [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season of very scattered rainfall, maize in hand-hoe conservation-farming basins yielded 3,054 kg per hectare against 1,339 kg under ploughing, which the authors say showcased the water-harvesting benefits of the basins [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. At landscape scale, Ethiopia's Sustainable Land Management Project, which combined surface water-harvesting systems with hillside grazing control and other works in degraded highland watersheds, reduced vulnerability to severe drought: where droughts were severe (SPI below –2) the programme effects were three times larger than its average, with increases of 16.71% in EVI and 13.48% in GOSIF-GPP, and significant buffering was also found in moderate droughts [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies found yield improvements significantly higher in study years with rainfall below 330 mm, and yield gains, though not significant, in below-average rainfall years [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. Second-hand citations add that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season (De Graaff, 2005, cited by Adgo et al.), that rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells (Kahinda et al., 2007, cited by Biazin et al.), and that a Rajasthan watershed model showed rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years (Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The storage pool still rests largely on compiler ratings, programme assertions and surveys, and includes the subsurface dams in Brazil that dried out in a rainless year [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. The benefit shrinks in severe drought: stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985), Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and zaï only buffers a dry spell of two to three weeks [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. In the Kenyan trial's short rains with meteorological droughts, tied ridging gave no advantage (0.52 against 0.53 t per hectare without inputs, 1.17 against 1.27 with manure and fertiliser) because there was little or no rainwater to hold in the basins [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5, ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. A water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through water management but crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Storage also runs out, with subsurface dams in Brazil drying out in a rainless year and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limiting soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Many units are compiler ratings or institutional assertions; the Zimbabwe planting-basin gain also carries manure and fertiliser, the Kenyan tied-ridging result is a single-site trial, the Indian pond figures come from a preprint farmer survey, the sand-dam figure rests on recall interviews, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian results come from bundled programmes [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. Water harvesting is not irrigation, and the new primaries mark the limit: at the more arid Kenyan sites of Laikipia and Machakos each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, with 0 kg per hectare of maize harvested at Machakos due to meteorological drought, and the conservation-farming treatments did not avert it [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The East African low-rainfall gain is for the best system per site, ripping or pitting usually with fertiliser, so it is bundled with reduced tillage and fertiliser, and the authors read it as a trend from their own figure [ev_crop_yield_rock09_15]. The Zambia 2001/2 basin contrast is a raw comparison in a single season with no normal-year reference, and most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit, so part of the gap is the input package [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Ethiopian landscape result is for a bundled programme measured as vegetation greenness and productivity, not crop yield; in mild droughts the EVI model still detected a small buffering effect but the GOSIF-GPP model showed none [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4]. The Zimbabwe water-productivity gain and the Rajasthan drought buffer are modelling results cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave sorghum in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that otherwise yielded nothing, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. In semi-arid Brazil, pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall and production-cistern water for livestock can reduce animal deaths in severe drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells, a benefit shortfall rather than damage [ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The large zaï, tassa and stone-bund contrasts are author estimates or secondary citations and the Brazilian statements are institutional assertions or potential effects without data [ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. The pool mixes low-income Sahelian evidence from Burkina Faso and Niger with upper-middle-income Brazil.

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: In-field practices let more rain infiltrate and hold water in the soil, so crops suffer less from dry spells: zaï pits gave 300–400 kg of sorghum per hectare in a low-rainfall year on degraded land that yielded 0 kg/ha without them, zaï trials in Burkina Faso gave honourable cereal yields on degraded crusted soils in periods of deficient rainfall, only tassa fields produced a harvest in the 1990 drought in Niger, and crops behind stone bunds could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_kabo04_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_1_s, ev_crop_yield_roose93_3, ev_crop_yield_kabo04_6_s, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. A meta-analysis of catchment restoration in Ethiopia cites physical soil and water conservation structures buffering crop growth against the 2015 severe drought [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. Stored water carries supply into dry periods: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, some 24,000 cisterns on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, households in Rwanda's land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster, and Ethiopian public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. WOCAT compilers for terraces, ponds, check dams, stone lines, weirs and gabions in Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ethiopia, Haiti, India, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate drought impacts as reduced through captured and infiltrated water and better soil moisture, and the Burkina Faso compiler for the Vallerani system notes that in years of extreme drought most plants survived and were used to feed animals [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The meta-analytic evidence also records failure under drought: a conservation agriculture meta-analysis reports that in long-term Zimbabwe trials conventional tillage yielded considerably more maize than mulched and reduced-tillage treatments in extreme seasons, and that mulch gave no water-conservation benefit in the 1991/1992 drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield gain in the driest year (1985) and do not reduce famine risk in a particularly dry year, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in years with low rainfall, zaï only reduces the impact of a dry spell of two to three weeks where soil water storage reaches the 50 mm minimum, and four consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. The Ethiopian public-works study notes vegetation greenness was still affected by local drought severity [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. The meta-analysis findings rest on cited trials and a secondary citation, most of the positive units are WOCAT compiler ratings (the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured) or institutional assertions without measurement such as the Loess Plateau cisterns, the sand-dam figure rests on recall interviews, and the Rwandan and Ethiopian results come from bundled programmes [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: Rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss during critical drought periods, and in Mediterranean long-term experiments cited in a no-till meta-analysis, wheat yields under no-till tended to be higher than under conventional tillage in years when water stress occurred [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: The same experiments show no-till wheat yields lower than conventional tillage in years with little water stress [ev_crop_yield_pitt15_5]. Both units are secondary citations inside a review and a meta-analysis drawn from several countries, with no magnitude, so they show direction only [ev_crop_yield_silv26_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.mechanism: A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia found significantly higher yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and yield gains also in below-average rainfall years, though not significant there [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In semi-arid Brazil, water from small earth reservoirs applied as supplemental irrigation during the dry spells that commonly interrupt the rainy season has reduced farming risk in years of irregular rainfall, so the crop does not suffer water stress or die [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. Water stored in production cisterns can serve to reduce animal deaths in periods of more severe drought, which matters to semi-arid farm families because small herds are a key household asset [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Adgo et al. cite Posthumus and De Graaff (2005), a Peruvian bench-terrace study, for terracing reducing the risk of crop failure during rainy-season dry spells through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought__.conditionality: Storage runs out in long droughts: subsurface dams at Mutuca (Pesqueira) tended to dry up through 2001, a year without rain, and at Ouricuri the small dams do not withstand long droughts, so fruit availability depends on the length and intensity of each year's rains; these units record no benefit at that point rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The meta-analysis compares drier against average rainfall years and pools in-soil and reservoir techniques; its China-dominated sample sets this upper-middle-income scope while its African sub-sample is lower income, and many of its observations also carried soil fertility treatment, which the authors control for [ev_crop_yield_boum16_3, ev_crop_yield_boum16_4]. The Peruvian terrace finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. The Brazilian benefit units are institutional statements without data: the Embrapa passages assess technologies the institute itself promotes, with no measured drought contrast or normal-year reference, and the cistern passage describes a potential effect, while the dry-up findings come from field observation and interviews with a few families [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Water harvesting buffers dry periods by storing or infiltrating water, but the storage practices show the clearest effect: zai pits reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, runoff ponds in semi-arid Brazil supply supplemental irrigation and production cisterns supply livestock water, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works interventions in Ethiopia raised water availability [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4]. WOCAT compilers for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, a farm pond in Cambodia, gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan and gabion check dams in Somalia judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6]. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the dry spells of the season [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. A terracing study citing De Graaff (2005) states that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A risk model of a Burkina Faso farm reservoir, built on field experience, finds all mild dry spells mitigated by supplemental irrigation and severe late dry spells reduced to mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A watershed model of the Arvari in Rajasthan (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011, cited in a review) found rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores, despite reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result. Only the storage family (sand dams, ponds, cisterns, check dams) holds a moderate result, resting on the Kenyan sand-dam catchment table and the Burkina Faso reservoir model [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7]. The in-field row (zaï, mulch), the terracing row (the Rwandan programme and the Uzbek terrace sheet) and the cross-family row (Ethiopian public works, Brazilian production cisterns, the Tunisian programme, the Burkina Faso review) each hold a slight gain, so the roll-up is slight rather than the pooled moderate [ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1, ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. Much of the pool is practitioner judgement from technology sheets or expert assertion (Brazilian research and programme authors, a lender evaluation in China without measurement); the comparisons against controls are the Rwanda unit, reported second-hand in a completion report, the Kenyan sand-dam catchment table, whose values are likely interview-derived, and the Ethiopian Sustainable Land Management Programme, measured on vegetation rather than yields [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. The Ethiopian study notes vegetation greenness still tracked local drought severity, and the zaï effect depends on soil storage capacity [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_roose93_1]. Storage itself runs short in prolonged drought: subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year, and consecutive drought years in Tunisia limited soil-conservation benefits; these units record no benefit at that point, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. The Ethiopian dry-spell finding is a field observation of which plots wilted, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Burkina Faso reservoir model marks the limit: a meteorological drought cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and severe late dry spells at flowering and grain filling are only partly mitigated because the reservoir supports two supplemental irrigations where at least three are needed [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, water from runoff-harvesting ponds applied as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced crop-loss risk in years of irregular rainfall, and water stored in production cisterns can reduce livestock mortality in severe droughts [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Against this, subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells; these units record no benefit when storage is exhausted, a shortfall rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. All units come from Brazilian research and programme authors, an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target, and none gives a drought-impact metric. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Ethiopia's Sustainable Land Management Project, whose measures include surface water-harvesting systems in degraded highland watersheds, reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds compared with control watersheds, with effects where severe droughts occurred three times larger than the average programme effect (increases of 16.71% in EVI and 13.48% in GOSIF-GPP), and significant buffering under moderate drought [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley maize trial the plots without mulch were the ones particularly affected by the season's dry spells [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1], and in Brazil Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: The measured effect is on satellite greenness and productivity indices over whole watersheds, not on yields or household outcomes, and comes from a programme bundling water harvesting with other land-management works, so its share is not isolated and the strength is not stated as a size for the practice [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1]. At the mild end the buffering thins: the EVI model still detects a small significant effect but the GOSIF-GPP model shows none [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4]. The Rift Valley finding is a field observation of which plots wilted during mild dry spells, not a tested yield contrast [ev_drought_hazard_sime15h2_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no normal-year reference, from a Brazilian setting rather than the East African zones this row covers [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Zai pits in Burkina Faso reduce the impact of dry spells of a few weeks when soil water storage is sufficient, cisterns in China are reported to mitigate frequent droughts, and public-works watershed interventions in Ethiopia improved drought resilience by raising water availability. WOCAT compilers for Vallerani micro-catchments, ponds, check dams, terraces, stone lines and water-spreading weirs judge drought impacts reduced through stored water, infiltration and soil moisture retention, and households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster.
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Most units are practitioner judgements or assertions without a drought metric, including a lender evaluation in China with no measurement; the Rwanda comparison against controls is reported second-hand in a completion report. In Ethiopia vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, and the Haiti compiler notes the impact has not yet been measured. In Tunisia, consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits, a unit recording no benefit rather than damage [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.mechanism: Storage carries water into dry periods: in semi-arid Brazil water from small earth reservoirs used as supplemental irrigation during in-season dry spells has reduced farming risk in years of irregular rainfall, and water in production cisterns can serve to reduce animal deaths in periods of more severe drought, protecting the small herds that are a key asset for semi-arid farm families [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Terracing is also cited as reducing the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season, through its water-conserving effect (De Graaff, 2005, cited by Adgo et al.) [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__drought_h.conditionality: Small storage works fail in prolonged drought: subsurface dams at Mutuca (Pesqueira) tended to dry up through 2001, a year without rain, and those at Ouricuri do not withstand long droughts because of their small size; this records a shortfall in benefit rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The benefit side rests on institutional statements with no data in the passage (an Embrapa assessment of technologies it promotes and a cistern statement of potential), while the dry-up evidence is field observation and family interviews; apart from a second-hand terracing statement with no measurement, the pool covers only Brazil [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3, ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. With the benefit side unmeasured and the measured side showing storage running dry, the class is slight.

water_harvesting_conservation__establish.mechanism: Pooled costs are up-front construction costs per structure: village ponds or tanks and dry-stone check dams (the latter per cubic metre of masonry) from a World Bank watershed project in Himachal Pradesh, India, and compiler-reported WOCAT establishment costs for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, a set of check dams and walls in India, a 200 m vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia.
water_harvesting_conservation__establish.conditionality: The WOCAT figures are each compiler's own cost table summed and converted with the sheet's exchange rate, and the India project figures are self-reported from project monitoring in rupees converted at one rate; none are market prices. A structure means very different things across the pool, from a fascine line of a few metres to a haffir of about 5100 square metres, and the per-cubic-metre check-dam figure is per volume of masonry, so the pooled cost class is a loose summary rather than a comparable unit cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.mechanism: The only unit argues that terraces limit fire by removing fuel: on intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little to spread on [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__fire__all.conditionality: Data deficient: the row rests on a single expert estimate whose authors say there is no experimental work on terraces behind it [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1]. What is missing is a second independent source or any measured fire outcome (burnt area, fire frequency or spread) on treated against untreated land. The argued effect depends on grazing keeping biomass down rather than on the structures themselves, so it says nothing about practices without that management.

water_harvesting_conservation__flood__al.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and infiltration trenches slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, trenches significantly reduced plot runoff across the reviewed studies, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_runoff_reduction_locat20_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Catchment-level terrace evidence is scarce, most measured results are at plot or hillslope scale, the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, and the Italian check-dam cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting rather than farm water harvesting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. Catchment-level evidence is scarce, and the Tunisian catchment result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Most units are WOCAT compiler ratings rather than measurements: the Indian farm-pond sheet rates downstream flooding as unchanged, the Zambian compiler says the benefit holds only at large scale, and a Somali sheet scores downstream flooding in the worsening direction although its comment says flooding was reduced [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1139_2013_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_flooding]. The Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported, and the Ghana finding is user perception [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Terraces, contour stone bunds, check dams and small dams slow and spread runoff and retain water and sediment, lowering peak discharges: terraces lowered flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower peak discharges at the foot of the slope, and in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50% [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. WOCAT compilers in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Somalia, Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced and say how: rain retained where it falls, a dam or series of dams acting as a downstream buffer, stone lines and walls cutting peak flows, and structures slowing runoff velocity [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods, spate and diversion structures in Yemen are said to control floods, and compacted hill terraces in Uttarakhand, India are credited with limiting flood and landslide damage [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: The sub-practices disagree, and the split runs through terracing: bunds and terraces that slow and spread runoff on the slope lowered peak discharges, while structures that divert runoff did the opposite — diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Runoff-catchment and spate rows each show a moderate benefit on their own, so whether the practice eases or worsens flood hazard depends on whether it holds water in place or concentrates it. Size and extremes matter too: larger sand dams increase flooding risk, and check dams have a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where ill-designed or poorly maintained [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Catchment-scale measurement is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, the Yemen and Uttarakhand statements are lender self-reported, the review's supporting cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.mechanism: Structures that hold runoff on the slope or in the channel lower flood peaks: a check-dam review cites check dams in Iran mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow, a review of Andean terraces reports that hydrological modelling and field measurements indicate a reduction in peak flow, and Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, as mitigating floods while recharging groundwater by infiltration [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__flood_haz.conditionality: None of the units says how large the reduction is, so the strength is not quantified. The terrace review itself calls the impact on peak flow uncertain given the scarcity of catchment-level studies, the Iranian result is a secondary citation in a review, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology; all are catchment or downstream effects rather than flood losses avoided on the adopting farm, and the row covers upper-middle-income settings only [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Water harvesting and soil and water conservation reduce food insecurity mainly by raising and steadying harvests and by putting stored water on gardens. In the Brazilian semi-arid, subsurface dams gave families more fruit and vegetables and, by most interviewees' account, more food overall, and production cisterns allow daily irrigation of gardens in households that had not grown or eaten vegetables before [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6]; in Burkina Faso, runoff cisterns irrigate small gardens and water livestock, improving food security in the lean season [ev_food_security_roose94_1]. In the field, planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a Kenyan plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, and ground cover raised those odds in Malawi's El Nino season [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_boil19_1]. Household food security rises in proportion to the area of a farm improved with bunds, and beneficiaries of Rwanda's terracing project showed drastically improved food consumption scores against a comparison group [ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. WOCAT compilers rate food self-sufficiency as improved and the risk of production failure as lowered, and say why: enough stored water to irrigate during drought in Cambodia, better soil moisture in Ethiopia, more cultivable land and crop diversity in Bhutan, more productive fodder and crops in Burkina Faso, and rehabilitated gullies and farmland in Somalia [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, farmers recalled that before terracing the community was highly food insecure and migrated in search of food even in minor droughts, and that terraces improved crop production and reduced seasonal migration [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. Ethiopian farmers who adopted rainwater-harvesting irrigation properly improved their dietary status (Desta 2004, cited in a review) [ev_food_security_biaz12_26].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gains depend on the rainfall year, on where the works are built and on practice choice. In Niger, farm families with soil and water conservation produced an estimated surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]; in Malawi's El Nino season, banking lowered the odds of meeting the maize requirement from 0.19 to 0.054 [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. Independent evaluations of Ethiopian programmes found communal, mostly off-farm watershed works did not raise food security, possibly because the programmes were short [ev_food_security_abate21_4, ev_food_security_arega24_1], and compilers record no change for vetiver terraces in Haiti, where land users must wait for degraded soil to recover [ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. Much of the literature is cited second-hand or qualitative, and the Brazilian findings include Embrapa's assessment of its own technology and programme reviews [ev_food_security_mira19_2, ev_food_security_castro22_3]. The class is moderate because the sub-practices differ, from slight for cross-family evidence to strong for in-field practices. A gain in a good season does not by itself show the practice protects food supply through drought. The Anjene account rests on farmer recall and group discussions, and the dietary finding is second-hand with no magnitude [ev_food_security_adgo13_11, ev_food_security_biaz12_26].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Harvested water and held soil moisture raise harvests and diversify diets: in semi-arid Kenya planting basins (zai pits) raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement to 421.75 against 1.67 in the control, bunds improve household food security in proportion to the farm area they cover, and Burkina Faso farms applying manure or soil and water conservation techniques on over half their plots are cited as more food secure [ev_food_security_boil19_2, ev_food_security_zoug14_1, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. In semi-arid Brazil stored production water allows daily irrigation of vegetable gardens and fruit trees for families who previously did not grow or eat vegetables, subsurface dams gave families more access to fruit and vegetables and more food overall, reviews of production-cistern experiments stress their importance for food security, and a systematic review cites significant improvements in food security indicators among adopters of rainwater-harvesting ponds in Burkina Faso [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_silv26_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gain depends on rain: Niger farm families with soil and water conservation produced an estimated surplus of 70 percent in years of good rainfall but still had an estimated deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years, so the practice does not secure food in dry years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1]. The only sized result is the Kenyan odds ratio, which has a wide confidence interval and comes from an above-average rainfall season [ev_food_security_boil19_2]. The Brazilian units are implementer perceptions, a seven-family interview study and a review of experiments run by the technology's developer, the Burkina Faso farm statement bundles manure with the conservation works, and the systematic review's citation is contradicted by its own table [ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5, ev_food_security_silv26_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: In rainfed cropping, in-field water capture and higher yields reduce food insecurity by helping plots meet household staple needs. In Malawi's El Nino season, adding ground cover raised the odds of a plot meeting the household maize requirement from 0.12 to 0.475 [ev_food_security_boil19_1, ev_food_security_boil19_3]. In Burkina Faso, higher yields are cited as improving household food security, especially on farms that apply manure or some kind of soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The strong class rests on a single odds-ratio study, and the same study shows practice choice can reverse the result: in that El Nino season banking reduced the odds of meeting the maize requirement to 0.054 against 0.19 in the control [ev_food_security_boil19_3]. The Burkina Faso statement is cited second-hand and does not separate manure from soil and water conservation [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5]. The evidence is thin and both studies are from semi-arid African settings, so the size of the effect elsewhere in rainfed cropping is uncertain.

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: Works that raise and steady crop output reduce the times a household runs short of food. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, which two decades earlier was highly eroded and highly food insecure, with people migrating in search of food in times of even minor droughts, the introduction of fanya juu terraces improved crop production and so reduced seasonal migration of farmers [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. In Brazil, adopters of Embrapa's barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins, identified food security as the technology's greatest impact, because it guarantees quantity, quality and diversity of food [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: Both units say food security improved but neither says by how much: the Ethiopian finding rests on farmer recall and group discussions about the period before and after terracing, and the terraces were maintained for decades with community labour alongside fertiliser use on cereals [ev_food_security_adgo13_11]. The Brazilian finding is an adopter rating in Embrapa's own impact assessment of its technology, not a measured food-security indicator [ev_food_security_mira19_2]. A measured household food-security comparison with untreated farms is needed to state a size.

water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.mechanism: In upper-middle-income semi-arid Brazil, stored water lets families grow food close to home: once production water is stored it allows daily irrigation of gardens, beds and fruit trees, and most families had not even been in the habit of growing and eating vegetables before [ev_food_security_arsky20_6]. Families with subsurface dams gained more varied diets, mainly through more access to fruit and vegetables, and most of those interviewed reported more food available [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6]; a review of Embrapa experiments judges irrigation of small beds from production cisterns important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3], and adopters of barraginha runoff basins identified food security, in quantity, quality and diversity, as the technology's greatest impact [ev_food_security_mira19_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__food_inse.conditionality: The gain is rated slight because no unit gives a size of effect: the evidence is qualitative interviews, an expert account of a cistern programme, a review of the research institute's own experiments, and an adopter-rated indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_castro22_3, ev_food_security_mira19_2]. All of it comes from semi-arid Brazil and works through garden irrigation and diet diversity rather than staple-crop supply, so it describes household storage for home production, not field-scale harvesting.

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: The review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall and names no specific practice or magnitude, so it does not isolate heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The row rests on this one secondary statement; a measured heat-stress contrast with a no-practice comparison is what is missing.

water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.mechanism: A maize meta-regression finds conservation agriculture performs better relative to conventional practice under drought and/or heat stress, and a review of quasi-experimental studies reports that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__heat_stre.conditionality: Neither unit separates heat from drought: the meta-regression frames them together and the review groups temperature shocks with low rainfall, without naming specific practices or giving a magnitude, so no unit isolates heat-stress losses [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. The meta-regression is restricted to maize under conservation agriculture, so it speaks to in-field residue and tillage practices rather than to storage structures [ev_crop_yield_stew18_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Water harvesting and conservation structures capture runoff and raise soil moisture so rainfed crops yield more, especially in dry years and low-rainfall areas; stored water allows supplemental irrigation and extra crops, and sediment and organic matter trapped behind structures add fertility. Meta-analyses now carry much of the evidence: A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 142% for infiltration pits, 91% for mulching, 69% for soil and stone bunds, 48% for terraces and 74% for tied ridging [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_2, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_3, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_5, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_6]; a synthesis of Ethiopian studies gives mean grain-yield differences of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds biomass on terraces about 1.94 times that on slopes [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1], and 2 to 4-year old bench terraces in Peru gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In Burkina Faso stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% and by about 142% with compost, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded plots, in Malawi's El Niño season ground cover raised maize from 247 to 432 kg per hectare, and silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_boil19_2, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. Stored water stabilises output: Indian farmers reported crop-failure chances falling from 20% to 6% in the rainy season and from 100% to 5–10% in winter with a farm pond, sand dams cut crop failure against a control catchment in Kenya, and WOCAT compilers across many technology sheets judge crop, fodder and animal production increased [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1]. In a Zimbabwe enterprise budget first-year planting-basin conservation farming yielded 1520 kg of maize per hectare against 400 kg on the fertilised conventional arm [ev_crop_yield_mazv09_2]. Newer field trials point the same way: In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, maize stalk mulch raised maize yield over no mulch at both sites in both seasons, and planting basins did so in 2012 [ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_1, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_2, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_3, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_4, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_6, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_8]. In Rwanda, vetiver mulch raised maize to 8089 kg per hectare against 4755 on flat rainfed plots [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_1], and in the same trial runoff from the terrace waterways, collected in a dug, lined pond and applied by a gravity drip kit as supplementary irrigation, gave 11982 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. In Burkina Faso, crop yields in years of average rainfall rose by 63–74 per cent on farms using rock bunds and by over 100 per cent on farms using zaï [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_1, ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 30-cm zaï and 1-m half-moons with compost gave 408 and 1372 kg of millet per hectare where direct seeding gave none [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_1, ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. Primary trials and surveys from eastern and southern Africa now stand in for second-hand Zambia readings. In on-farm trials in Ethiopia, ripper plus tied ridging with fertiliser gave 1775 kg of maize per hectare against 1458 under conventional maresha ploughing with the same fertiliser, and 1076 against 945 kg of tef [ev_crop_yield_rock09_1, ev_crop_yield_rock09_4]; in Tanzania, ripping and pitting combined with fertilisation gave yields 1.5–2.2 times those of conventional ploughing with the same fertilisation [ev_crop_yield_rock09_11]; and at Chipata, Zambia, basins with fertiliser gave 6660 kg of maize per hectare against 3153 under conventional practice [ev_crop_yield_rock09_13]. In Zambia's 2001/2 season hand-hoe conservation-farming basins gave 3,054 kg of maize per hectare against 1,339 under ploughing, and a regression controlling for planting date, hybrid seed and fertiliser puts the gain from the basins themselves closer to 700 kg per hectare for maize and 400 to 500 kg for cotton [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_2, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_3]; a later survey of Zambian conservation-agriculture households reports 5.2 t of maize per hectare in basins against 1.8 under the hand hoe [ev_crop_yield_umar11_1]. A meta-analysis of tied-ridge-furrow experiments finds tied ridges without fertiliser or mulch yielded 17% more sorghum grain than flat planting [ev_crop_yield_makm21_1]. In a Zimbabwe household panel, conservation agriculture (mostly planting basins, with residue mulch and rotation on some plots) improved maize yields both when rainfall was above average and during times of drought, and sorghum and cowpea yields during drought [ev_crop_yield_mich19_3, ev_crop_yield_mich19_4, ev_crop_yield_mich19_5]. A review of conservation agriculture in Zambia also cites planting basins plus lime raising yields by 68% [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_1] and a simulated gain of around 40% for the whole conservation farming package [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_6]. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, raised maize grain to 4457 kg per hectare with NPK and urea against 2157 kg under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea, and to 3768 kg averaged over the fertility options, and lifted rain water productivity from 3.10 to 6.61 kg per hectare per mm [ev_crop_yield_koro17_1, ev_crop_yield_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. Primary studies acquired in the latest round add to this. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia finds that water harvesting increases crop yields by 78% on average, with a large spread, and puts the average maize gain at almost 3000 kg/ha in Asia against 400 kg/ha in Africa [ev_crop_yield_boum16_1, ev_crop_yield_boum16_5, ev_crop_yield_boum16_6]. Stored runoff used for supplemental irrigation raises yields where rain is short: in Burkina Faso a farm pond lifted the 3-year mean sorghum yield from 455 kg per hectare under the farmer's normal practice to 712 with irrigation alone and 1403 with fertiliser as well [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_1, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_2], and a risk analysis puts the long-term average gain at 150% [ev_crop_yield_fox05_1]; in Kenya irrigation from a runoff dam with fertilizer gave 1796 kg of maize per hectare against 1375 on fertilised non-irrigated plots [ev_crop_yield_barr05_1]; and in Pakistan supplemental irrigation from harvested rainwater raised wheat yield by 146%, mustard by 101%, maize by 118% and pearl millet by 101% over rainfed fields [ev_crop_yield_waqa25_1, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_2, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_3, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_4]. In-field works raise yields by holding rain where it falls: terraced fields in Ethiopia's Anjene catchment gave 0.95, 1.86 and 1.73 t of teff, barley and maize per hectare against 0.49, 0.61 and 0.77 t on un-terraced farms [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_3]; in Nigeria tied ridging raised four-year mean sorghum yield by 25% and tied ridging with mulch by 57% [ev_crop_yield_chir06_1, ev_crop_yield_chir06_3]; Zambian basins averaged 4.4 t of maize per hectare against 1.7 under the hand hoe [ev_crop_yield_umar12_1], and in Malawi conservation agriculture (planting in small holes under residue cover) gave 600 kg per hectare more grain than conventional ridge tillage in 2016/17 [ev_crop_yield_seti18_2]. Plot-level econometrics in Ethiopia agree for drier areas: conserved plots in low-rainfall Tigray carry a yield premium of ETB 412 or 299 per hectare depending on the estimator, and all the soil and water conservation technologies studied had robust impacts on crop output in low-rainfall areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_kato11_1]. Output also steadies: in Kenya the coefficient of variation of maize yield was 5% with irrigation and fertilizer against 11% in the control, Nigerian sorghum under tied ridging with mulch fell below 1000 kg per hectare once in four years against three times on the flat bed, and in Malawi yield variation was lower under conservation agriculture [ev_yield_stability_barr05_8, ev_yield_stability_chir06_12, ev_yield_stability_seti18_3]. Reviews add second-hand gains: tied ridges improving barley grain yield by at least 44% in northern Ethiopia (Araya and Stroosnijder, 2010), stone rows or grass strips raising sorghum yield by 12–58% in Burkina Faso (Zougmore et al., 2004), basin tillage with mulching raising maize yields by 30–50% on a South African clay (Hensley et al., 2000; Walker et al., 2005), soil bunds giving at least 30% more lowland rice in Tanzania in normal years (Raes et al., 2007), and stone bunds and terraces raising crop yield by up to 53% in Ethiopia (Nyssen et al., 2007) [ev_crop_yield_biaz12_9, ev_crop_yield_dile13_3, ev_crop_yield_biaz12_23, ev_crop_yield_biaz12_12, ev_crop_yield_biaz12_16, ev_crop_yield_gebr18_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Held out of the class, as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: where rainfall is heavy the practice can lower yields through waterlogging, and the authors say so. Annual rainfall above 1000 mm lowered the performance of Ethiopian soil and water conservation practices, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, and fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]; and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rain exceeds 80 mm a day and 1,200 mm a year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than flat-cultivated fields because of frequent waterlogging and the risk of nutrient leaching [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In a wetter sub-humid Kenyan site, ridged plots with fertiliser gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. Read these as a siting limit: the practice should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. Other measured losses do count against the class: bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years in Ethiopia, and stone bunds in semi-arid Tanzania reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_9]. In a drought-affected season in Mozambique no cowpea yield was obtained on any treatment [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2]. In Algeria farmers lost 5 to 15% of their cropped area to banquettes without seeing yields improve, legume yields between banquettes showed no significant gain, and a Moroccan farmer saw no yield improvement between banquettes imposed by technicians [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2, ev_crop_yield_roos10_2]. Other nulls and negatives: conservation promoted mostly off-farm had no yield effect, benefits in Ethiopia appeared only once structures were maintained for at least seven years, diversion banquettes in Niger cut yields, and soil salinisation can appear on check-dam farmland [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1].
