Outside the meta-analyses the pool mixes independent evaluations with lender completion-report figures, bundled watershed programmes, reviews quoting ranges from earlier studies, a farmer survey reported in a preprint and many practitioner judgements; much of the zai and planting-basin gain rides on added manure, compost or fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_crop_yield_mazv09_1]. In the Malawi El Nino survey banking, the reinforcement of ridges while the crop is growing, cut maize from 245 to 153 kg per hectare, so some in-field practices lowered yield in that season [ev_crop_yield_boil19_5]. Planting basins gave no significant gain over no mulch in 2011 at either Ethiopian site (4239 against 4171 and 4265 against 4131 kg per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_5, ev_crop_yield_sime15h2_7]. Rwandan contour ridges were not significantly different from flat rainfed plots (5937 against 4755 kg per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_2]. The Burkina Faso zaï and half-moon contrasts are against land where direct seeding produced no grain, with compost added to the pits, so they measure bringing degraded land into production rather than an improvement on a cropped field. The Burkina Faso farm gains are for years the authors call average rainfall, with compost on the bunded fields. The wheat figure is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. The Rwandan pond result is a bundle — terrace runoff capture, a lined storage pond and drip irrigation — so the yield is delivered through irrigation hardware and cannot be read as a pure capture effect; it is one season of a randomised trial in which every plot received farmyard manure and mineral fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. The East African and Zambian trial gains are bundles. In Ethiopia the comparator carried the same fertiliser, but without fertiliser neither improved tillage nor fertiliser alone raised maize significantly, and the 20–50% tef gain without fertiliser was not significant [ev_crop_yield_rock09_2, ev_crop_yield_rock09_3]; the Tanzanian ripping-or-pitting arms are bundled with reduced tillage [ev_crop_yield_rock09_11]; and the Chipata basins carried improved seed against a conventional practice with extremely low fertiliser, in seasons of well-above-average rainfall, a gain the authors say cannot be fully explained [ev_crop_yield_rock09_13]. Some trial arms lost: pitting with fertiliser was the lowest-yielding treatment at Machakos, at 1.2 against 1.6 t per hectare under conventional practice [ev_crop_yield_rock09_9], and at the more arid Kenyan sites each site recorded complete crop failures in two out of three and four seasons, which the treatments did not avert; water harvesting is not irrigation [ev_crop_yield_rock09_10]. The Zambian 2001/2 raw contrast is one season with no normal-year reference and mixes the basin effect with higher input use, since most basin farmers received hybrid seed, fertiliser and lime on credit; the regression figure is the cleaner estimate, and even its basin dummy also picks up extra weeding labour and lime [ev_crop_yield_hagg03_1, ev_crop_yield_hagg03_2]. The later Zambian survey yields are farmer self-reports with large spreads, and the basin gain over ploughing (5.2 against 3.8 t per hectare) was not significant [ev_crop_yield_umar11_1, ev_crop_yield_umar11_2]; a national Zambian smallholder panel finds no significant maize yield effect of planting basins under any of its estimators [ev_crop_yield_burk12_1]; and paired soil samples on Zambian fields under basins or ripping (bundled with reduced tillage), with residues hardly retained, showed no significant difference in nitrogen [ev_soil_nitrogen_umar11_6]. The Zimbabwe panel keeps drought-season and normal-season results apart: in average rainfall periods conservation agriculture had no significant impact on any crop, in another specification it decreased maize yields by itself, and it did not mitigate rainfall-shortfall or surplus losses for millet and groundnut, so its gains appear only in seasons away from the average [ev_crop_yield_mich19_1, ev_crop_yield_mich19_2, ev_crop_yield_mich19_6, ev_crop_yield_mich19_7]. The tied-ridge meta-analysis finds no significant millet gain over flat planting and no significant difference when grass mulch was added to the ridges, and its sorghum observation count is internally inconsistent [ev_crop_yield_makm21_3, ev_crop_yield_makm21_2, ev_crop_yield_makm21_1]. Farmer reports of basin yields of >1 tonnes per hectare in poor-rainfall seasons, against total failure under ploughing, compare fertilised basins with unfertilised ploughing, which the author calls too confounded [ev_crop_yield_faocr11_9]. The remaining Zambia and global figures are cited secondhand in Arslan and colleagues' literature review, and none has a normal-year comparison: the 68% gain is for planting basins plus lime application, with timely conventional farming giving 50% in the same trials [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_1]; and the roughly 40% gain is a simulation of the whole conservation farming package, through early planting and improved soil quality [ev_crop_yield_arsl15_6]. Readings in that review that misread their primaries were dropped, and the primaries themselves are now in the pool directly. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers the 2014 season only, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gains belong to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_crop_yield_koro17_1, ev_crop_yield_koro17_7]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (3507 kg per hectare with NPK and urea, 3065 kg averaged, against 2157 kg) were not significantly different from the control in yield, nor in rain water productivity (4.84 against 3.10) [ev_crop_yield_koro17_2, ev_crop_yield_koro17_4, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2]. At Péni no conservation arm differed significantly from the control in yield or water productivity, grass strips with zaï giving 4192 kg and earth bunds with contour ploughing 4067 kg against 3317 kg per hectare; the authors attribute this to rainfall, saying water was not a limiting factor at Péni [ev_crop_yield_koro17_5, ev_crop_yield_koro17_6, ev_crop_yield_koro17_7, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO cross-slope barrier mark is a compiler judgement, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The newer primaries also mark where the gain stops. Supplemental irrigation pays mainly in dry seasons and with fertiliser: in Kenya it left yield unchanged or slightly lower in good rainfall seasons (>350 mm), and irrigation alone did not increase grain yield [ev_crop_yield_barr05_7, ev_crop_yield_barr05_2]; in Burkina Faso irrigated and non-irrigated plots did not differ significantly at the same fertiliser level, so fertiliser was the main reason for the higher yields, and the gain from irrigation alone does not cover the heavy investment of labour and capital [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_3, ev_crop_yield_fox05_1]. In Ethiopia's high-rainfall Amhara, conserved plots showed no significant yield difference, the point estimate lying ETB 179 or 145 per hectare below non-conserved plots, and only waterways and trees had robust impacts in high-rainfall areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_kato11_2]; soil bunds raised production risk in Tigray, the driest region studied, and irrigation alone did so too unless combined with improved seed and fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_kato11_6, ev_yield_stability_kato11_8]. Nigerian ridging without mulch yielded 9 and 3% less than the flat bed in 2000, when rain failed at flowering and grain filling [ev_crop_yield_chir06_5]; in Ghana tied ridges made no significant difference to maize yield [ev_crop_yield_dalt14_1]; in Mozambique basin and direct-seeded maize yields did not differ [ev_crop_yield_kida19_1]; and in the meta-analysis most of the 21 observations with a lower yield were in-soil storage techniques [ev_crop_yield_boum16_2]. Rodents sheltering in narrowly spaced stone bunds can damage up to 225 kg of crop per hectare (Meheretu et al., 2014) [ev_crop_yield_gebr18_4]. The larger Nigerian gain comes with mulch [ev_crop_yield_chir06_3], and the meta-analysis's Asian maize gain far exceeds the African average [ev_crop_yield_boum16_6], so the size of the gain depends heavily on the package and the region.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In the tropical highlands, soil and water conservation has measured yield gains and measured yield losses, depending on the practice. Gains: an Ethiopian synthesis finds mean grain-yield gains of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds, 554.3 for tied ridges and 629.2 for mulching, stone and soil bunds raising yields by up to 10% in Tigray, and stone bunds raising soil total nitrogen from 0.16 to 0.20% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_4, ev_crop_yield_adim16_8, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1]; in a Kenyan highland trial, tied ridges in long rains with dry spells gave 4.10 against 3.15 t of maize per hectare with manure and fertiliser, and 2.53 against 1.82 t without inputs (not significant), and tended to give less variable yields [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_3, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1]; in Peru, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]. In the Ethiopian highlands, fields with long-established fanya juu terraces and grass strips yielded 0.95 against 0.49 t of teff, 1.86 against 0.61 t of barley and 1.73 against 0.77 t of maize per hectare on adjacent un-terraced farms, and the terraces improved the water productivity of the three crops by at least 100% [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. Losses: in the same Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the authors suggest may be waterlogging in the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The fanya juu and soil bund losses and the finding that annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively are held out of it, because the synthesis puts that effect down to excessive water availability (water logging) on the furrows of structures [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]: they are logged as a performance caveat — these structures should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy — rather than as production evidence. The evidence points to three things that separate gains from losses. Practice type: stone bunds, tied ridges and mulching gained, while graded and level fanya juu, soil bunds and grass strips lost yield in the Ethiopian table [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Rainfall: the gaining practices were studied at lower average rainfall (695.1 mm for tied ridges, 876.7 mm for mulching) than the losing bunds (1030.2 to 1454.3 mm), and rainfall above 1000 mm reduced performance [ev_crop_yield_adim16_3, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]; practice and rainfall travel together in that table, so the two cannot be fully separated. Time: bunds lose yield in the first few years, while the long-established fanya juu terraces of the Ethiopian with-and-without survey yielded more than un-terraced fields, so fanya juu is not a losing practice everywhere [ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1]. Against those terrace gains, the same paper cites Herweg and Ludi (1999) and Kassie et al. (2008) finding that fanya juu, soil and stone bunds and grass strips did not increase crop yield or biomass in the highlands of Ethiopia and Eritrea [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_12]. For a Task Team Leader the actionable reading is to match the structure to the rainfall regime, favouring in-field moisture capture in drier highlands and avoiding fanya juu and soil bunds where waterlogging is likely, and to budget for an early yield dip. At the dry end, tied ridging gave no advantage in the Kenyan short rains with meteorological droughts, since there was little rain to hold [ev_crop_yield_ndun23_2, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_4, ev_crop_yield_ndun23_5]. On quality, both sides rest mainly on the same Ethiopian synthesis of unweighted means pooled across studies; the Kenyan result is a single-site trial whose lower-variability finding was not tested, the Peruvian figure is cited in a review, and the Ethiopian terrace gains are descriptive statistics from a comparison of terraced and adjacent un-terraced farms, not a controlled trial [ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_yield_stability_ndun23_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_4, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In semi-arid settings, pits (zai, tassa), stone bunds, tied furrows and subsurface dams concentrate scarce rainfall in the root zone or store it for later use, raising cereal yields and enabling harvests in drought years when untreated fields fail.
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Evidence mixes Sahelian field results (Burkina Faso, Niger) with Embrapa and cistern-programme sources from semi-arid Brazil, several of them self-assessments or expert statements; the Brazilian programme effects are on value of production, a proxy, and some yield gains depend on manure added to the pits.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: In rainfed hill and watershed systems, in-situ rainwater conservation, terracing and soil and water conservation works combined with crop packages raise yields: average rainfed crop yields rose 24% and 26% against controls in Karnataka watershed phases, rainfed crop productivity rose 20.8 percent by difference-in-difference in Uttarakhand, and maize on terraced Rwandan hillsides rose from 1.5 to 2.8 tons per hectare [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. The DIME evaluation reported for Rwanda found the value of harvests 36 percent higher than in the control group [ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3]. Outside these programmes, on-farm trials in Mozambique gave maize gains of 504 to 800 kg per hectare on planting basins and direct-seeded conservation agriculture over conventional ridge-and-furrow plots, and farmers in a Kenyan sand-dam catchment had less crop failure than in a control catchment [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_3, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: The Indian and Rwandan units are bundled programmes in which conservation works came with improved seed, vermicompost, crop packages or life-saving irrigation, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated, and they are drawn from Bank completion reports or IEG reviews of them; the Rwanda maize figure is project monitoring without a control and the Uttarakhand terrace figure compares with- and without-project models [ev_crop_yield_hp17_2, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7]. In Mozambique conservation agriculture and control plots alike gave no maize or cowpea harvest in a drought season, and the Kenyan crop-failure finding comes from interviews [ev_crop_yield_thierf15_1, ev_crop_yield_thierf15_2, ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Sand dams in Zimbabwe improved water availability, and livestock health improved at eight sites where cattle had been driven up to 20 km to the nearest water point before construction [ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Against this, long-term Zimbabwe trials found conventional tillage yielding considerably more maize than mulched and reduced-tillage treatments in extreme seasons, with no water-conservation benefit from mulch in the 1991/1992 drought [ev_crop_yield_rusin11_7]. The livestock finding rests on respondent statements, and both findings come from Zimbabwe only.

water_harvesting_conservation__productio.mechanism: Stored or concentrated water raises yields and adds harvests. In the Brazilian semi-arid, tied furrows gave 606 kg of maize per hectare against 302 kg under traditional planting, soil management in subsurface dams raised crop productivity over 22 years without salinisation, larger subsurface dams let some owners take up to 4 consecutive harvests in 12 months, and runoff retention with rescue irrigation is credited with securing fruit production in a 550 mm rainfall zone [ev_crop_yield_brito07_8, ev_crop_yield_brito07_5, ev_crop_yield_cirilo03_4, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2]. A quasi-experimental study of a Brazilian cistern programme found a raised value of family production, and programme authors describe wider water access letting families expand and diversify production [ev_agricultural_production_value_casag22_7, ev_agricultural_production_value_arsky20_7]. Beyond Brazil, 2 to 4-year old bench terraces in Peru gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields, silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland, and the Jordanian compiler rates fodder production up because the barley crop and its stubble feed animals [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__productio.conditionality: Results are not uniform. A review of infiltration trenches reports yield gains on some plots and losses on others [ev_crop_yield_locat20_1, ev_crop_yield_locat20_2]; in Algeria, farmers who lost 5 to 15% of their farmland to banquettes saw no yield improvement, and legumes grown between banquettes showed no significant gain [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2]. A Brazilian farmer's subsurface dam produced no harvest in one season of adverse weather [ev_crop_yield_brito07_6]. Much of the Brazilian evidence is Embrapa or programme self-assessment, the cistern-programme author states there are no quantitative impact evaluations, and the value-of-production finding is a proxy for yield [ev_agricultural_production_value_arsky20_7, ev_agricultural_production_value_casag22_7]. The Chinese check-dam figure is a secondary citation that also notes soil salinisation on check-dam farmland, and a South African farmer's account of stable harvests concerns a residue-cover system with no capture structure [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_yield_stability_faocr11_10].

water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets, per hectare for sheets in Tunisia, India, Ethiopia, Yemen, Uganda, Jordan and Somalia and per structure for a farm pond in Cambodia, check dams in India, a vetiver line in Haiti, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia; the cost class is set from the per-hectare sheets.
water_harvesting_conservation__recurrent.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. Older sheets treat every costed item as per hectare, and the per-hectare values run from a cent to several hundred USD per hectare per year, so the sub-dollar Uganda and India figures look like entry or conversion problems; the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: Water harvesting and soil and water conservation raise household income and returns through higher and steadier yields, dry-season irrigation of higher-value crops and better fodder and livestock, but the evidence also shows them failing to pay. On the gain side, a quasi-experimental study cited in a review found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]; in Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3]; Zambian crop budgets give hand-hoe conservation-farming basins returns per hectare 70 percent higher than conventional hand hoe cultivation for cotton [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6]; first-year Zimbabwean planting-basin farmers earned a maize gross margin of 473.36 USD per hectare against 70.60 on conventional plots [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1]; and Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In the Ethiopian highlands, teff, barley and maize on long-established terraces earned incremental income of US$ 159, 275 and 141 per hectare per year over un-terraced farms, and terrace investment for barley had an average net present value of US$ 1542 over 50 years at a 10% discount rate [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4, ev_economic_return_adgo13_5, ev_economic_return_adgo13_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_10]. A risk and cost-benefit analysis of farm ponds for supplemental irrigation, combined with fertiliser and an off-season tomato crop, gives net profits of 151–626 USD per hectare per year in Burkina Faso and 109–477 in Kenya, depending on labour opportunity cost [ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_fox05_4]. In a Kenyan trial, unmulched and straw-mulched ridge-furrow rain harvesting raised wheat net income by 82% and 117% over flat planting [ev_economic_return_wang16_3, ev_economic_return_wang16_4]. Switching to conservation-agriculture basins in Zambia gave a marginal rate of return of 860% over hand hoeing and 360% over ploughing, and in Mozambique basin net returns were $148 against $104 per hectare under conventional tillage [ev_economic_return_umar12_2, ev_economic_return_umar12_3, ev_economic_return_kida19_2, ev_economic_return_kida19_4]. Reviews cite more: Hatibu et al. (2006) found road-catchment rainwater harvesting for paddy in Tanzania returning more than US$ 12 per person-day against US$ 3.7 for rainfed sorghum, Ngigi et al. (2005) farm ponds in Kenya raising annual maize returns by 150%, Senkondo et al. (2004) rainwater harvesting in Tanzania profitable in the long term, Awulachew et al. (2008) users of water-management techniques earning significantly more agricultural income than non-users, and Gebremedhin et al. (1999) stone bunds returning 50% [ev_economic_return_biaz12_21, ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_biaz12_19, ev_household_income_biaz12_18, ev_economic_return_gebr18_3]. In Apurímac, Peru, Cárdenas et al. cite a study by Tafur for a benefit of 1.96 soles per sol invested in building cochas [ev_economic_return_card22_1]; in Pakistan, farmers earned a net income of US$ 1799 from fish farming in a rainwater-harvesting farm pond, and maize irrigated from harvested rainwater had a cumulative benefit-cost ratio of 2.02 by the second year [ev_household_income_waqa25_7, ev_economic_return_waqa25_5]. A meta-analysis puts the payback of water-harvesting investment at 4–5 years at the pooled-average maize yield gain [ev_economic_return_boum16_8]. WOCAT compilers mostly rate farm income as increased [ev_household_income_wocat_1528_2012_farm_income, ev_household_income_wocat_2844_2017_farm_income]. On the loss side, Ethiopian graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds had net present values below zero of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], single soil and water conservation measures in Burkina Faso did not cover their annual costs [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3], Brazil's production-cistern programme returned a benefit-cost ratio of 0.0858 over its evaluation window [ev_economic_return_casag22_9], and in a Nigerian trial tied and open ridging, with or without mulch, made net economic losses of about 1, 0.5, 11 and 12% because of high production costs [ev_economic_return_chir06_10]. Zougmoré et al. (2004), cited by Biazin et al., found stone rows and grass strips in Burkina Faso not cost-effective without added nutrients despite sorghum yield gains of 12–58% [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24], and in Pakistan pearl millet irrigated from harvested rainwater had a benefit-cost ratio of −0.49 in its first year, still 0.53 by the third [ev_economic_return_waqa25_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The roll-up states conflicting evidence because the sub-practice rows disagree: the runoff-catchment, micro-catchment and terracing rows lean towards gains, while the in-field and cross-family rows are each split. What separates the sides is how the gain is valued and against what. Crop budgets built on bundled input packages put basins well ahead [ev_economic_return_hagg03_6, ev_economic_return_mazv09_1], but a Zimbabwe household panel that holds inputs constant finds conservation agriculture generates less revenue than traditional cultivation over a large portion of the rainfall distribution [ev_economic_return_mich19_8]; in a Kenyan drought season net benefits were higher without tied ridging [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]. Complementary inputs and crop value separate them too: in Burkina Faso, supplemental irrigation from a farm pond alone did not repay the heavy labour and capital invested, and paid only with fertiliser and a high-value tomato crop [ev_economic_return_fox05_2, ev_economic_return_fox05_3]; stone rows and grass strips paid only with nutrients added [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24]; in Pakistan stored water paid on maize but not on pearl millet [ev_economic_return_waqa25_5, ev_economic_return_waqa25_6]; and the Tanzanian paddy return is high because paddy cannot be grown there without rainwater harvesting at all [ev_economic_return_biaz12_21]. Region matters: the meta-analysis puts payback at 2 years for the average Asian farmer but more than 15 years for the average African farmer, at world maize prices [ev_economic_return_boum16_7]. In Mozambique basins did not differ significantly in net return from conventional tillage at intermediate elevation [ev_economic_return_kida19_3], while in Ghana tied ridges with grass strips returned more than flat land in 2010 but not in 2011 [ev_economic_return_dalt14_3]. Farm size also matters: the Brazilian cistern income effect was confined to small farms and reversed on farms larger than 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5, ev_household_income_casag22_6]. Much of the literature comes from bundled programmes, lender reports and secondary citations, the Fox and meta-analysis returns are modelled, the Kenyan ridge-furrow net-income gains are from a single field trial, and the Tanzanian, Kenyan pond and stone-bund figures are cited in reviews [ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_boum16_8, ev_economic_return_wang16_3, ev_economic_return_biaz12_20]; the Indian pond returns are cross-sectional and confounded by farm size, and sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient [ev_economic_return_pals23_1, ev_economic_return_ritc21_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty, and few studies follow households over time.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In semi-arid areas, production cisterns and subsurface dams let families irrigate gardens and fruit, diversifying diets and raising farm income, while zai and stone bunds raise cereal output and return to labour; food security rises with the area of farm under bunds.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Income gains from the Brazilian production-cistern programme are small and turned negative for larger farms, its benefit-cost ratio is well below one, and subsurface dams yielded little cash income in stagnant local economies; a Sahelian study found SWC families still in deficit in low-rainfall years, and single SWC measures did not repay annual costs.

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock systems, farm budgets show water capture both paying and not paying. In Zimbabwe, planting-basin conservation farming earned a first-year maize gross margin of 473.36 against 70.6 US dollars per hectare for conventional practice without fertiliser and 48.19 with fertiliser, and experienced households could earn US$866.84 per hectare against US$357.16 for a farmer using chemical fertilizer in higher rainfall [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. In semi-arid India, net returns rose with livestock and trees to US$ 586 per hectare and to US$ 857 once a farm pond was added [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In a Kenyan highland trial, by contrast, net benefits in the short-rains season were higher without tied ridging than with it, except under one soil treatment [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: The sides differ in season, in what is compared and in how cleanly water capture is isolated. The Kenyan loss is from a short-rains season of meteorological droughts, in a trial that compares tied ridging with and without under the same soil inputs [ev_economic_return_ndun23_1]; it is the cleanest single comparison here. The Zimbabwean gains set a package of basins, manure, fertiliser and residue against conventional practice, so the water-capture effect is mixed with nutrient supply, and the higher-rainfall figure is a sensitivity scenario with assumed yields [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2]. The Indian figure comes from a farmer survey in which few farms had a pond, the pond water was also used for irrigation, and the compared farms differ in other ways [ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. The evidence therefore cannot say whether water capture alone pays in this farming system; the gains belong to packages, and the one isolated test found a loss in a drought season. All of these are farm budgets rather than measures of household poverty, and none follows households over time [ev_economic_return_mazv09_1, ev_economic_return_mazv09_2, ev_economic_return_mazv09_3, ev_economic_return_ndun23_1, ev_economic_return_pals23_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.mechanism: In the Brazilian semi-arid, cisterns and subsurface dams supply water for gardens, fruit and livestock, improving diets and raising family farm income, with the largest income effects on small farms; Andean terrace rehabilitation is judged to pay back through long durability.
water_harvesting_conservation__rural_pov.conditionality: Evidence is from upper-middle-income Brazil and Peru, outside the LIC/LMIC target band. A quasi-experimental study found modest income gains, no effect outside the Northeast, a negative effect on larger farms and a benefit-cost ratio far below one; several units are Embrapa or programme self-assessments and household self-reports.

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: Terraces, stone bunds and lines, banquettes, trenches, pits and check dams slow overland flow and spread it behind barriers, so less runoff leaves the slope and less soil is detached and carried away; check dams and gabions trap sediment in channels. Measured reductions are large: terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, Burundi terrace plots cut erosion by 50% to 90%, trenches reduced soil loss by 73.0% on average, and check dams cut catchment sediment export by 20 to 98% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1]. WOCAT compilers across many countries rate soil loss, surface runoff and downstream siltation as reduced, explaining that micro-catchments cut the kinetic energy of rain by trapping runoff that check dams slow runoff so soil accumulates upstream, and that gabion walls and check dams trap sediment that would otherwise travel downstream [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation]. Meta-analyses confirm the direction: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil-loss reductions of 68.67% for mulching, 54.97% for ridging, 55.06% for soil and stone bunds and 60.21% for terraces [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_2, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5]; an Ethiopian synthesis reports soil loss down 59% under graded soil bunds, 88% under level soil bunds, 38% under stone bunds, 98% under mulch and 62% under tied ridging [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_5]; and a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1]. Reviews add further cited figures: Nyssen et al. (2007) found stone bunds cutting soil erosion by 68%, Gebremichael et al. (2005) recorded soil loss on cropland in Dogu'a Tembien falling from 57 to 20 t per hectare a year after physical conservation works, Lanckriet et al. (2012) measured 14.4 against 35.4 t per hectare a year under conservation agriculture compared with plain tillage, Al-Seekh and Mohammad (2009) found stone-terraced hillslopes reducing runoff by 65–85% and soil erosion by 58–69%, Araya and Stroosnijder (2010) found tied ridges cutting runoff by about 60%, Hulugalle (1990) recorded 0% to 15% of seasonal rainfall lost as runoff with tied ridging against 20–40% with open ridging or flat planting, and Lal (1982) found runoff and erosion 2.7 and 15.3 times higher in non-terraced than terraced catchments [ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_13, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_6, ev_runoff_reduction_stav20_1, ev_runoff_reduction_biaz12_7, ev_runoff_reduction_biaz12_11, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_1]; a terracing review concludes that soil loss from cultivated slopes is much higher without terraces, which increase infiltration and interrupt hydrological connectivity [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_4, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5]. At catchment scale, stone bunds, check dams and regrowth in Ethiopia cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year, and check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1]; there, a watershed model shows check dams reducing runoff by 12% and sediment by 11.7%, and studies cited by Shi et al. report check dams cutting sediment load by 51.9% in the Huangfuchuan catchment and rainy-season runoff by 15.5%–28.9% in the Yanhe watershed [ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_6]. In Tigray, physical conservation works are cited as decreasing runoff by up to 88%, and integrated catchment management at May Zeg Zeg cut surface runoff volume by 81% [ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_7, ev_runoff_reduction_gebr18_8]; well-designed check dams reduce stream power and channel erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_11]. A meta-analysis of mulching finds runoff reduced by 47.4% and soil loss by 76.2% against controls, soil loss by 70.9% on cropland, and reductions of 45.9% and 75.1% at rainfall intensities above 90 mm/h [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_1, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_2, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_3, ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_5, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings, and several literature sources are lender self-reports with before/after designs, perception surveys or catchment numbers that barely changed: the Rwanda sediment drop from 54 to 2.6 tons/ha a year has no control, and Indian sediment yield moved only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5]; runoff reduction and sediment retention enter as component proxies. Contrary findings: check dams can cause downstream channel incision, diversion banquettes increased gully and bank erosion in Niger, trenches raised sediment in the first years, Maghreb banquettes were often erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_locat20_2, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. A rangeland review adds that, about 30 years after abandonment, many channel runoff-control structures in southern Arizona had failed and some accelerated headcut retreat and scouring, that collapsing stone terraces across dry channel beds in the Israeli Negev induced rill and gully erosion, and that Nyssen et al. (2007) suggest excessive removal of surface stones to build terraces led to a threefold increase in sheet and rill erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12, ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13, ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_3]. Most harm is tied to failed upkeep or poor construction rather than to working structures. Terraces also pass on part of what they catch: a review puts the delivery ratio at about 20%–30% for sediment and 50%–60% for runoff, and in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel; one cited Chinese catchment estimate is only 25.04 against 28.97 t per hectare a year [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6, ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3]. A catchment-restoration meta-analysis in Ethiopia finds minimal effect of catchment treatment on runoff in drought-prone areas with annual rainfall below 500 mm [ev_runoff_reduction_meaza22_3]. In Tunisia gullied area on banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]; and USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2]. Many of the added figures are citations within reviews rather than primary measurements, and the Loess Plateau watershed effect is modelled [ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_1, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1]. The meta-analyses pool unweighted study means and are dominated by plot-scale East African studies, so catchment-scale effects remain less certain [ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_1, ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1]. The mulching meta-analysis pools land uses including post-fire forest and bare land; cropland and tree crops were less effective in reducing runoff, both below 40%, and the mulching benefits decreased with increasing rainfall intensity under heavy rainfall [ev_runoff_reduction_fan23h1_4, ev_erosion_hazard_fan23h1_6]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In the Maghreb, contour structures have been reported both to hold runoff and to accelerate erosion. Staggered earth bunds (tabia) in Morocco store the runoff of all rains below 50 mm on the field [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. In Algeria, a poorly maintained banquette becomes a factor accelerating erosion, because the smallest unrepaired breach triggers a chain reaction through the whole network in torrential and prolonged rains [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: Two conditions separate the sides in the sources. Maintenance: the acceleration is tied explicitly to unrepaired breaches in state-built banquettes [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2]. Storm size: the tabia hold runoff only up to rains of 50 mm, and in bigger storms the excess overtops them and gullies the whole slope [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1]. The actionable reading is to plan and fund upkeep and spillways, not only construction. Elsewhere banquettes simply did not stop gullying: gullied areas on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, and over 1947-1968 Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam [ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. Neither side is measured on plots: the protective statement is from an expert manual and the harmful ones are secondary citations within a national evaluation, and the two concern different structures, tabia and banquettes [ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.mechanism: In high-income settings check dams and ponds trap sediment: loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland watersheds retained 48.4% and 82.4% of total sediment yield and produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, four field-edge ponds in southern Germany trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years, and a typical Belgian pond had a long-term trapping efficiency of 68% [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Bench terracing in a small USA watershed reduced runoff by 9% and sediment yield by 58% [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1]. In Spain, terrace maintenance slowed runoff for events with a return period shorter than 8–10 years, and terraces in general interrupt flows, shrinking the runoff-contributing area and peak discharges (Bellin et al. 2009, cited in a review) [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__soil_eros.conditionality: The studies found real effects in both directions, and what separates them is whether the structures hold and where erosion is measured. The gains are sediment trapped behind working dams, ponds and terraces; the harms are erosion triggered by the structures themselves or by their failure: channel incision was observed below 81% of surveyed check dams in a Spanish catchment through the clear-water effect [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1], about 30 years after channel runoff-control structures on semi-arid Arizona rangelands were abandoned a large share had failed and some accelerated headcut retreat and scouring (Nichols et al. 2018) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12], and in the Israeli Negev traditional stone terraces across dry channels proved highly vulnerable to collapse, their failure inducing rill and gully erosion, so they need frequent maintenance [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. For a Task Team Leader the separators are maintenance over decades and design for the channel below the structure. Even working check dams had no statistically significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms, reducing only the number of runoff events from small storms by 60%, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Most units are secondary citations in reviews, and the high-income settings (rangeland, arable fields with ponds, Mediterranean terraces) differ from smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Tunisia, drought caused a shortfall in the spate-irrigation and water-recharge works established in Medenine, where only 15 were built against a target of 95 [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The single unit comes from an ex-post review drawing on project completion data and describes an establishment-phase shortfall of works, not physical damage to structures already built.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On Ethiopian soil and water conservation structures, a review reports second-hand that when the drainage ditch behind a structure fills with sediment, trapping efficiency quickly decreases and the extra pressure on the structure can lead to structural failure [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: a single statement cited second-hand in a review, with no rate or frequency of failure; it does describe a damage pathway, and implies the damage depends on whether ditches are cleared [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1_av]. What is missing is a second independent source or one measured finding on how often silted structures fail.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Burkina Faso, soils on farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher carbon and nitrogen contents than the control farm [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3], and a review cites climate-smart packages of soil and water conservation structures with biological measures boosting soil carbon stock by three to seven times over business-as-usual [ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only two units, neither a measured stock change against a matched control: the Burkina Faso figure is a carbon content on farms using several techniques with compost, and the three-to-sevenfold gain is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures, very large for structures and to be read with caution [ev_soil_organic_carbon_sawa11h1_3, ev_soil_organic_carbon_tade23h1_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed-scale soil and water conservation is reported to raise groundwater, used here as a component of catchment water yield: stone bunds, zaï and half-moons applied at watershed scale increase ground water level [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_zoug14_1]; in Burkina Faso improved well levels are linked to SWC measures that control surface runoff and improve infiltration [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_1]; ISRO survey data record an increase in groundwater recharge in treated areas in India [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3]; piezometers recorded groundwater levels rising in 16 of 21 non-desert districts with an average increase of 1.42 meters [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_3]; the Uttarakhand water budget shows aquifer recharge up 3.3 percent and water yield from catchment areas up 4.9 percent [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5]; and in Ethiopia improvements in the water table made small-scale irrigation possible [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_eth16_7]. In Burkina Faso, cited studies show soil and water conservation techniques improving the availability of ground water in many villages, especially large rock bunds known as digues filtrantes [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6]. In Ethiopia's Mendae catchment a water balance gave groundwater recharge of 107.7 mm after water harvesting against 8 mm before (Negusse et al., 2013, cited by Gebremeskel et al.) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_gebr18_11]. On the other side, the same capture reduces what leaves the catchment: water outflows from treated catchments have been found halved compared with untreated catchments (Garg et al., 2012; Gates et al., 2011, cited by Gebremeskel et al.), reviews cite a decrease in runoff generation harming downstream social–ecological systems (Batchelor et al., 2003; Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011; Garg et al., 2012, cited by Dile et al.), and a global model suggested rainwater harvesting would reduce annual river flows by 18% on average and by up to 80% in a single basin (Wisser et al., 2010, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_water_yield_gebr18_9, ev_water_yield_dile13_9, ev_water_yield_glen12_10].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is for downstream users and basin planners: it asks what capturing water upstream does to the water that reaches streams and reservoirs below, not whether the farm that captures it has more. Studies disagree because the recharge side counts water entering the ground near treated land, while the outflow side counts water leaving the catchment, and the same works can raise the first and lower the second [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5, ev_water_yield_gebr18_9]. Scale and intensity also separate them: the outflow losses come from large-scale implementation and basin-wide models, while other studies find limited or no downstream impact on stream flows from small-scale storage, even when implemented widely (Schreider et al., 2002; De Winnaar and Jewitt, 2010; Andersson et al., 2011) [ev_water_yield_dile13_10, ev_water_yield_rock10_1]. The recharge gains have limits in their own sources: without data from untreated sites the Indian project impact is unclear [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_3], subsidised tube-well pumping has possibly wiped out any increases in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4], and in Burkina Faso the number of wells with water year round has not increased significantly [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2]. The Uttarakhand figures are a modelled water budget [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_utk22_5], the outflow findings are all cited second-hand, and most other units are programme reports or cited statements; the digues filtrantes finding is cited from another study, with no figures [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_sawa11h1_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Costs are the per-hectare unit cost of watershed treatments (bunds, check dams and other soil and water conservation works) across treated area in two World Bank-supported India watershed projects.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both figures come from one evaluation of bundled watershed programmes in India and are treatment costs per hectare treated, not per hectare of degraded land restored; the evaluator compares them with national budget norms rather than with outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Better-sited planning based on a land resource inventory avoided unnecessary structures, so construction of soil and water conservation works cost less per hectare than under the conventional integrated watershed programme.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Single lender completion-report figure from Karnataka, India, in local currency at stated price terms; the comparison is against another watershed programme, so it shows a saving from planning rather than the cost of SWC versus no SWC.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. In Ethiopia's Sustainable Land Management Project, whose measures include surface water-harvesting systems, a satellite difference-in-differences comparison of treated and control watersheds found that the programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought, with effects in areas that had severe droughts three times larger than the average programme effect (increases of 16.71% in EVI and 13.48% in GOSIF-GPP), and significant buffering under moderate drought [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies found significantly higher yield improvements in years with rainfall below 330 mm [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks, and a Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The buffering weakens at the mild end and fails at the extreme end. Under mild drought the Ethiopian programme's EVI model still detects a small significant effect but the GOSIF-GPP model shows none [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4]. A water-harvesting review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years (the measured harm in this row), and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Almost every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated: water harvesting is one of several listed Ethiopian programme measures, and many meta-analysis observations also carried soil fertility treatment [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. The Brazilian statement describes potential without data, the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation, the Burkina Faso moisture finding is for pits filled with compost, and the Burkina Faso review conclusion has no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm and 1-m half-moon plots mitigated the impact of dry spells by retaining moisture for 2-3 weeks [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Apart from the water-harvesting meta-analysis, every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data and the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The Burkina Faso half-moon and zaï moisture finding is the authors' statement about dry spells, for pits filled with compost [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In mixed crop–livestock settings the evidence is the same as for rainfed cropping, with an Ethiopian watershed programme evaluation added. These are programme-scale or unspecified soil and water conservation packages. A review of impact studies finds such methods particularly useful in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability, Ethiopia's PSNP public works improved watershed drought resilience by increasing water availability, and in semi-arid Brazil production cisterns can reduce animal mortality in severe drought [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. Physical soil and water conservation structures were also reported to buffer crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia, and a water-harvesting review states that dry spells can be bridged through investments in water management [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1, ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia (Bouma and colleagues) found significantly larger yield improvements in study years with rainfall below 330 mm than in wetter years, and gains in below-average rainfall years that were higher but not significant [ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same review states that crop yields cannot be sustained during a meteorological drought and different coping mechanisms are required [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. The PSNP note adds that vegetation greenness still followed local drought severity, Niger families with soil and water conservation still had an estimated 28 percent deficit in low-rainfall years, and in Tunisia four consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_food_security_kabo04_1, ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. Apart from the water-harvesting meta-analysis, every unit is a bundled programme, pooled soil and water conservation or an expert review, so the share due to water harvesting is not isolated; the Brazilian statement describes potential without data and the Ethiopian 2015 finding is a secondary citation [ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed works and production cisterns increase stored water, which improved watershed drought resilience in Ethiopia and can reduce livestock deaths in severe droughts in Brazil [ev_drought_hazard_arega24_4, ev_drought_hazard_castro22_2]. A Burkina Faso review concludes that soil and water conservation techniques helped reduce vulnerability to drought and famine [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. In Ethiopia, the Sustainable Land Management Programme reduced vulnerability to severe drought in treated watersheds against control watersheds, with programme effects three times larger where severe droughts occurred, and buffered moderate droughts significantly on both vegetation measures used [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Ethiopian public-works study bundles area closures, small-scale irrigation and soil and water conservation, the Brazilian cistern statement is framed as a potential effect, and in Tunisia consecutive drought years limited soil-conservation benefits (no benefit rather than damage) [ev_drought_hazard_iegtun13_1]. That Burkina Faso conclusion is the author's overall judgement, with no measured drought-year contrast behind it [ev_drought_hazard_sawa11h1_7]. The Ethiopian programme result is measured on remotely sensed vegetation greenness and productivity rather than crop yields, comes from a programme that bundles surface water harvesting with small-scale irrigation, gully rehabilitation, grazing control and reforestation, and under mild drought the buffering showed on the greenness index but not on the productivity measure [ev_drought_hazard_cons22_1, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_3, ev_drought_hazard_cons22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Watershed programmes combining physical and vegetative barriers, bunds, check dams and terraces reduce runoff and soil loss: runoff dropped by 5 to 18 percent across Indian states, downstream runoff in the Karnataka catchments examined fell by 10 to 22 percent, and Ethiopian public works cut soil loss by 32.2% [ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_6, ev_runoff_reduction_iegind11_5, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_erosion_hazard_arega24_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are bundled programme results measuring runoff or soil loss as proxies for flood impact, several from Bank completion reports or perception surveys, such as 84 percent of Ethiopian respondents reporting reduced run-off [ev_runoff_reduction_eth16_2, ev_erosion_hazard_eth16_4, ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1]. Effects at watershed scale are small or absent: Karnataka project watersheds cut runoff by 3.2 percent against conventional sites, Uttarakhand sediment yield fell only from 71.6 to 69.3 tons per ha per year, and its water-budget model showed overall surface runoff up 1.5 percent [ev_runoff_reduction_kar20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_utk22_3, ev_runoff_reduction_utk22_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Across mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes, the reported route to lower food insecurity is higher yields and irrigated gardens. A review tabulates significantly increased food security from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi [ev_food_security_ngur26_1]; Brazilian studies judge production-cistern irrigation of small beds feasible and important for household food security [ev_food_security_castro22_3]; and higher yields are cited as improving food security in Burkina Faso, especially on farms with soil and water conservation on over half of their plots [ev_food_security_sawa11h1_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gain is only slight because the supporting findings are qualitative, cited second-hand and give no size, while the independent evaluations point the other way. In Ethiopia, an impact evaluation of a bundled watershed project found no significant food-security effect for treated households at any participation level [ev_food_security_abate21_4], and public-works participation in communal soil and water investments did not translate into increased food security, possibly because of the short programme [ev_food_security_arega24_1]; both concern mostly off-farm community works. In Niger, families with soil and water conservation produced a surplus of 70 percent in good rainfall years but a deficit of 28 percent in low-rainfall years [ev_food_security_kabo04_1], so benefits may not hold in the dry years that matter most.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A review reports, second-hand from three cited studies, that the impact of soil and water conservation is especially significant in areas with temperature shocks or lower rainfall [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one narrative statement read second-hand from a review, which does not name specific practices, does not separate heat shocks from low rainfall, gives no magnitude and states no country; no unit measures heat-stress losses directly [ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Soil and water conservation and water harvesting have been found both to raise and to lower production. Gains come from retaining moisture and soil: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a pooled yield gain of 71% over controls, with 69% for soil and stone bunds and gains of 71.7% for maize and 68.2% for sorghum without fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_1, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_4, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_7, ev_crop_yield_tefe24_8]; four studies in a systematic review find 20–24 per cent gains in crop yield or value of production, particularly in regions with low rainfall or high climatic variability [ev_crop_yield_mala24_1, ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_mala24_5]; zai pits combined with stone lines in Burkina Faso are reported to raise sorghum yields by over 100% [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_3]; Ethiopian early adopters had a 15.2 percent higher value of production and invested plots 20.6 percent higher [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_4]; physical structures buffered crop growth against the 2015 severe drought in Ethiopia [ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]; and dry spells can be bridged through water management [ev_crop_yield_rock10_1]. Programme reports add rainfed yield gains of 24% to 26% in Karnataka and 20.8% in Uttarakhand, yields rising from 0.5 to more than 1.2 t per hectare in wetter Mauritanian watersheds, and crop diversification from water harvesting with irrigation [ev_crop_yield_iegind11_1, ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_arega24_2]. Losses come from structures taking cropland and from excess water: in an Ethiopian synthesis fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare, bunds cut yields by up to 7% in the first few years, and rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, possibly through waterlogging [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]. A review cites soil and water conservation structures combined with biological measures raising wheat production by 30–45% over business-as-usual [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. Soils on Burkina Faso farms using soil and water conservation techniques had higher nitrogen contents than the control farm, used here as a component [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. A meta-analysis of water-harvesting studies across semi-arid Africa and Asia finds crop yields 78% higher on average, with a large standard deviation and range; average maize gains were almost 3000 kg/ha in Asian studies against 400 kg/ha in African ones, and gains were significantly larger in study years with rainfall below 330 mm [ev_crop_yield_boum16_1, ev_crop_yield_boum16_6, ev_crop_yield_boum16_5, ev_crop_yield_boum16_4, ev_crop_yield_boum16_3]. In Burkina Faso stone rows or grass strips gave sorghum yield increases of 12–58%, particularly under poor rainfall (Zougmoré et al. 2004, cited in a review) [ev_crop_yield_biaz12_23]; in Ethiopia's upper Agula watershed integrated catchment management combined with fertiliser and in-situ moisture conservation raised rainfed crop productivity by 50% (Alemayehu et al. 2009, cited in a review) [ev_crop_yield_gebr18_10]; and a global hydrology–crop model suggested rainwater harvesting would raise overall crop production by 35% (Wisser et al. 2010) [ev_crop_yield_glen12_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The class is set by the gains. The excess-water losses are held out of it as a caveat on where the practice performs rather than as production evidence: annual rainfall above 1000 mm affected performance negatively, which the synthesis puts down to water logging on the furrows of structures, fanya juu and soil bunds were associated with yield losses of 54 to 193 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_adim16_6, ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. Bunds should not be applied where rainfall is that heavy. The evidence itself names what separates gains from losses. Rainfall: gains concentrate in low-rainfall or variable areas and in drier periods, while bunds lose yield in high-rainfall areas, and in Tigray bunds slightly raised productivity in drier periods but reduced it in moist seasons because cropped area was lost to the bunds [ev_crop_yield_mala24_3, ev_crop_yield_schmidt12_8, ev_crop_yield_adim16_6]. Time and maintenance: value of production rose only after structures had been maintained for at least 7 years, later adopters saw no significant gain, and bunds cut yields in the first few years [ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_5, ev_agricultural_production_value_schmidt12_2, ev_crop_yield_adim16_7]. Who decides: imposed structures often reduced cultivable area by 3 to 20% without improving productivity, and structures promoted mostly off-farm for community resource protection gave no gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_5, ev_crop_yield_abate21_1]. Severity: dry spells can be bridged but yields cannot be sustained in a meteorological drought [ev_crop_yield_rock10_2]. Practice: fanya juu and soil bunds account for the measured losses [ev_crop_yield_adim16_2]. The actionable distinctions are therefore siting by rainfall regime, farmer-owned rather than imposed structures, and a maintenance horizon of years. On quality, many of the largest gains are from bundled programmes or lender completion reports (Ethiopia public works, India watershed projects, Mauritania), with value of production and forage biomass used as proxies, while the losses come from an Ethiopian synthesis and a matched study; the drought finding is a secondary citation in a review [ev_crop_yield_utk22_1, ev_crop_yield_mrt14_2, ev_forage_productivity_mrt14_3, ev_crop_yield_meaza22_1]. The wheat figure is a review's citation of a package that includes biological measures [ev_crop_yield_tade23h1_2]. The nitrogen finding is a content on farm soils, not a yield [ev_soil_nitrogen_sawa11h1_4]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The meta-analysis also holds losses: 21 of its observations show lower yields with water harvesting, most of them in-soil storage techniques [ev_crop_yield_boum16_2]. Without added nutrients, water-conservation measures in the Sahel had little influence on yields in years with well-distributed rainfall (Zougmoré et al. 2003b, cited in a review) [ev_crop_yield_biaz12_17]. The Agula gain is bundled with fertiliser and measured before and after over decades, and the global figure is a model result that also projects reduced river flows [ev_crop_yield_gebr18_10, ev_crop_yield_glen12_9].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Household income and returns from mixed soil and water conservation and water-harvesting programmes have been found to rise, to stay flat and to fall. Gains run through higher yields, irrigation and diversification: a quasi-experimental study found soil and water conservation raised net rice profit in Ghana by a significant 16 per cent [ev_economic_return_mala24_1]; Brazil's production-cistern programme raised family income by about 4.6%, nearly 11% when the top of the income distribution is excluded, with larger effects on farms of 0 to 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_1, ev_household_income_casag22_2, ev_household_income_casag22_5]; a review of 311 Indian watershed case studies found a mean benefit-cost ratio of 2.14 and an internal rate of return of 22 percent [ev_economic_return_josh05_1, ev_economic_return_josh05_2]; Mauritanian dikes returned a financial IRR of 24% [ev_economic_return_mrt14_4]; and programme evaluations report income gains of 54% in Karnataka and 58% on the Loess Plateau over control areas [ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_iegchn07_6]. Losses come from costs exceeding gains: in Burkina Faso the yield increase did not cover the annual costs of single SWC measures [ev_economic_return_zoug14_3]; Ethiopian graded fanya juu and graded soil bunds had net present values of −148 and −708 ETB per hectare [ev_economic_return_adim16_4]; and the Brazilian cistern programme's benefit-cost ratio over its evaluation window was 0.0858 [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. In Ethiopia, agricultural income from crops and livestock was significantly higher for users than non-users of micro- and macro-catchment techniques (cited in a review) [ev_household_income_biaz12_18], and in Tanzania investment in rainwater harvesting for maize, paddy rice and onion was profitable in the long term as long as farmers could afford the initial investment (Senkondo et al. 2004) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_19]. A meta-analysis valuing average maize gains at world prices puts payback of the water-harvesting investment at 4–5 years at the pooled-average gain, not accounting for capital interest [ev_economic_return_boum16_8]. On the loss side, stone rows and grass strips in Burkina Faso were not cost-effective without added nutrients because of high labour, transport and material costs (Zougmoré et al. 2004) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: What separates the sides, where the evidence says it: farm size, since the Brazilian income effect was a gain on small farms but a loss on farms larger than 10 ha [ev_household_income_casag22_5, ev_household_income_casag22_6]; labour costing and the size of the initial investment, since Ethiopian household benefit-cost ratios were 0.42 to 0.78 at market wages and exceeded one only with a shadow wage and a low initial investment [ev_economic_return_schmidt12_6]; and how long benefits are counted, since the Brazilian ratio covers a short window against a long-lived asset and counts income only [ev_economic_return_casag22_9]. For a Task Team Leader, the practical points are targeting smallholders, costing household labour honestly and expecting returns to arrive over years. The largest gains are from bundled programmes with weak attribution, and the Brazilian income effects are for a cistern bundled with a productive grant and training [ev_household_income_casag22_1]; IEG calls the China income estimate not robust and notes the India gains may partly be construction wages, and a Karnataka completion report doubts its own before/after figures [ev_household_income_iegchn07_6, ev_household_income_iegind11_2, ev_household_income_kar20_3]. The losses and nulls come mostly from independent evaluations, though the Ethiopian values may omit off-site benefits [ev_economic_return_adim16_4], and a Kenyan bundle showed no effect on per capita income [ev_household_income_mala24_2]. A review's report of increased incomes from check dams and infiltration pits in Malawi is qualitative and cited second-hand [ev_household_income_ngur26_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty. Location and up-front cost add to the separators: the same meta-analysis puts payback at 2 years for the average Asian farmer but more than 15 years for the average African farmer, whose average maize gain is far smaller [ev_economic_return_boum16_7], the Tanzanian profitability holds only where farmers can afford the initial investment [ev_economic_return_biaz12_19], and the Burkina Faso structures paid only with nutrients added [ev_economic_return_biaz12_24]. The payback periods are modelled from average yields, and the Ethiopian and Tanzanian findings are cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_boum16_8, ev_household_income_biaz12_18].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Physical SWC works under public-works and watershed programmes reduce soil loss and downstream runoff, and sediment-control dams with terraces and vegetation trap sediment in the catchment. A meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds soil loss cut by 58.66% and runoff by 53% on average, with soil and stone bunds reducing soil loss by 55.06% and runoff by 49.2% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_1, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_1, ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_4, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_5]; in Ethiopian catchments, stone bunds, check dams and vegetation regrowth cut sediment yield from 8.5 to 1.9 t per hectare a year [ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_meko14_2].
