In a randomised field experiment in semi-arid Kenya, a micro-field rain-harvesting system of ridges shedding rain into planted furrows significantly improved wheat grain yield and soil water storage over flat planting, with both growing seasons classed as dry years [ev_crop_yield_wang16_5]. A WOCAT compiler for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso rates drought impacts as reduced, crediting more vegetation cover, soil fertility and water storage in the soil profile, and reports that in years of extreme drought most plants reduced their growth but survived [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Kenyan result comes from research-station plots in dry, not failed, seasons, and the pooled claim includes plastic-film mulch arms, which are not a nature-based component [ev_crop_yield_wang16_5]. The Burkina Faso unit is a practitioner rating, not a measured drought-year contrast [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts]. No measured result covers severe or extreme drought, so whether the gain holds when a season fails is unknown.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of the WOCAT sheet on the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso judges that greater biodiversity, vegetation cover and soil fertility, deep root systems and water stored in the soil profile increase resilience to drought, and that in years of extreme drought most plants survived though their growth fell [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single practitioner judgement from one technology sheet, not a measured drought outcome [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_drought_impacts]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Vallerani compiler in Burkina Faso keeps the treated area open to regulated grazing to reduce the grass growth that could favour the spread of fire, and herders monitor the area [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one compiler rating, not a measurement, and the reduction it describes comes from grazing management and community monitoring alongside the micro-catchments, so it is a bundled effect rather than one of the basins themselves [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_fire_risk]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-catchments retain rain where it falls; the Burkina Faso compiler for the micro-basins reports that through water harvesting the rain is retained in the precipitation area and flood risk decreases [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Data deficient: the row rests on one WOCAT compiler rating, not a measurement, and the same compiler adds that a flood in the ploughed area before vegetation is well established can wash out the micro basins [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts]. What is missing is a second independent source or a measured runoff, peak-flow or flood-damage contrast for micro-catchments; until then no class is stated, which is not the same as no effect.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Through water harvesting the rain is retained in the precipitation area and flood risk decreases, as the compiler of the Vallerani System sheet in Burkina Faso puts it [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Data deficient: the row rests on a single practitioner judgement from a technology sheet with no hydrological measurement, and the same compiler cautions that a flood on ploughed land before vegetation is established can wash out the micro basins [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_flood_impacts]. What is missing is a second independent source or a measured runoff or peak-flow contrast for micro-catchments; the absence of a class does not mean the practice has no effect on flooding.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Vallerani tractor-ploughed micro-catchments collect runoff for fodder and crops. The Burkina Faso compiler writes that food security improves with increased and diversified productivity and income, and that even in severe drought some sown plants can serve as emergency food for people and animals, while the deep root system of the sown plants and higher soil moisture and fertility reduce the risk of production failure [ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: both units come from a single WOCAT technology sheet for Burkina Faso and are practitioner ratings, and no study measures household food security for micro-catchment practices. A second independent source, or any measured result on food security or production-failure risk, would let the cell state a class [ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_1528_2012_risk_of_production_failure].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Semi-circular bunds, Vallerani micro-catchments and half-moons harvest runoff for crops and grasses. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost gave 1372 kg of millet per hectare where direct seeding gave none [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. A review tabulates crop yield increases of 50–200% from half-moons in Burkina Faso and Niger, and cites micro-basin water harvesting in Zambia doubling maize yields to 3 t per hectare [ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5]. Negarim micro-catchments with supplementary irrigation supported fruit production at Embrapa Semi-Arid in Brazil, and semi-circular bunds raised millet grain production under African conditions [ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_1]. For the Vallerani System in Burkina Faso the WOCAT compiler reports more fodder in quantity and quality, a surplus of 22–106 grazing days per tropical cattle unit per hectare [ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1528_2012_animal_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Animal production was rated lower on the Niger sheets because treated rangeland must be protected from grazing for the first years while vegetation establishes [ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1613_2014_animal_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_1614_2014_animal_production]. The Burkina Faso half-moon contrast is against land where direct seeding produced no grain, with compost added to the pits, so it measures bringing degraded land into production rather than an improvement on a cropped field [ev_crop_yield_zour25h1_2]. The FAO manual cites earlier work, the review figures are ranges and single citations rather than pooled estimates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements [ev_crop_yield_fao13c_1, ev_crop_yield_fao13c_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_2, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Vallerani tractor-ploughed micro-catchments, half-moons and ridge-furrow systems collect runoff for crops and sown fodder. In a Kenyan field trial, ridge-furrow rain harvesting raised wheat net income by 82% without mulch and 117% with straw mulch over flat planting [ev_economic_return_wang16_3, ev_economic_return_wang16_4]. On crusted degraded soil in Burkina Faso, 1-m half-moons with compost were profitable at 377 275 FCFA per hectare after the investment [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3]. The Burkina Faso compiler for the Vallerani system links more and better fodder to improved animal health, productivity and market price, and so to higher farm income [ev_household_income_wocat_1528_2012_farm_income].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gains are per-hectare net incomes from field trials, not measured changes in household income or poverty, which they stand in for. The Kenyan figures come from one trial, and the larger wheat gain also carries a straw mulch [ev_economic_return_wang16_4]. The row rests on three sources, one of them a technology-sheet rating; measured household income for micro-catchments is missing. The half-moon profit comes from a trial on degraded land where the authors count the experiment's own investment, and compost was added to the pits [ev_economic_return_zour25h1_3]. The Vallerani unit is a technology-sheet rating [ev_household_income_wocat_1528_2012_farm_income].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-catchments trap runoff in small basins, which the Kenyan compiler says cuts the kinetic energy of rainwater and so reduces soil loss; for the Vallerani tractor-ploughed basins in Burkina Faso the compiler adds that ploughing along the contour collects the runoff flowing between the tilled lines, and that soil loss falls through runoff reduction and less wind erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1528_2012_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Confidence is only medium because the row rests on practitioner ratings from the Burkina Faso and Kenyan WOCAT technology sheets; no literature measurement of soil loss covers this family, and the rated reduction says nothing about how much sediment leaves the treated area [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_1528_2012_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2895_2017_soil_loss].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Jordan sheet for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting rates downstream siltation as reduced, consistent with runoff and sediment being held in the micro-basins [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5860_2021_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner ratings support this cell, and the semi-circular bund sheet for Niger rates downstream siltation unchanged [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1614_2014_downstream_siltation]. Siltation is a component proxy for water quality; no water-quality measurement exists for this family.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Micro-catchments concentrate runoff from the bare ground between basins into the planted area, so more water stays in the root zone. In the eastern drylands of Ethiopia, a study by Abdulkadir and Schultz cited by Biazin et al. found mean soil moisture 31% higher in the wet season and 24% higher in the dry season in tree-and-grass plots fed by micro-catchments [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1]. For the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, the WOCAT compiler states that the micro-basins collect up to 95% of rainfall and relays local reports that well levels rose after implementation [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Ethiopian figure is a secondary citation, and the Vallerani units are practitioner ratings with the well-level rise a community report. The evidence measures soil water in the field, not household water supply. No measured in-field soil-water contrast for micro-catchments is in the pool apart from the secondary Ethiopian citation; that is what is missing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as decreased, with no comment explaining why [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single compiler rating with no comment or measurement, from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band, and it concerns rain-storm impacts rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop storage depends on rain to refill: in great multi-year droughts the domestic cistern runs dry and households fall back on water trucks, and WOCAT compilers for rooftop systems in Nepal and Uganda rate the technology as not coping well with drought [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1497_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1595_2013_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a functional failure of storage rather than structural damage; the Brazilian unit is an implementer interview and the others are practitioner ratings, none quantified [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1497_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1595_2013_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with river floods [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1497_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1595_2013_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without damage records or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate rooftop rainwater systems in Nepal and Uganda as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1497_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1595_2013_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on Rubagano rooftop rainwater harvesting with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda rated plant diversity slightly increased; the sheet gives no mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single practitioner judgement without comment or measurement; the link from roof-water storage to wider plant diversity is not explained in the source, so the row is indicative only.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry period, giving households basic drinking and cooking water near the home, cutting the time spent fetching water and postponing or avoiding the shortages that send families to water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. In a survey of beneficiary families, 57.8% said the cistern fully met drinking, cooking and personal hygiene needs, and the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop tank system in Uganda rates water quantity and availability as improved [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The benefit is set by storage per person: a 16 thousand-litre cistern gives a family of four 16.6 litres per person-day, larger households stay dependent on water trucks, and only 19.1% of surveyed families named the cistern as their main source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. In great multi-year droughts the cisterns run dry and households fall back on water trucks, which records no benefit at that point rather than damage to the tank [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3]. The survey used recall with no control group, the other Brazilian units are implementer or author statements, and the Ugandan units are practitioner ratings; all describe domestic water access as a component proxy, not crop or livestock losses [ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic cisterns in semi-arid Brazil store rainwater for the dry season, but in great multi-year droughts they run dry and households fall back on water trucks, leaving them very vulnerable [ev_drought_hazard_arsky20_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single expert statement from a Brazilian programme account, upper-middle-income and adjacent to the target; it records no drought benefit once storage is exhausted, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the tank, and says nothing about shorter droughts.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The pooled cost is the average construction cost of a roof rainwater-harvesting tank under the Himachal Pradesh mid-Himalayan watershed project in India, reported per structure from the project's output table.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single lender completion report, self-reported from physical and financial monitoring; the figure is a nominal rupee average over the project years converted at one exchange rate, so it indicates the order of cost of a household tank rather than a transferable unit rate.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop tanks capture part of the rain falling on roofs; the WOCAT compiler for a rooftop system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda rates surface runoff and downstream flooding as reduced [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1595_2013_downstream_flooding].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both sheets are practitioner ratings, and the Nepal compiler rates downstream flooding as unchanged because only a little portion of rainfall is trapped from the roof [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Rooftop systems trap part of the rainfall from roofs, and the compiler for Rubagano rooftop harvesting with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda judged downstream flooding slightly reduced.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets; the Nepal compiler rated the effect neutral because only a little rainfall is trapped from the roof, so any flood benefit is marginal.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler's rating on the WOCAT sheet for the Rubagano rooftop rainwater harvesting system with a concrete or brick tank in Uganda, which records crop production as increased; the sheet gives no comment on how the stored roof water reaches crops [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, not a measured yield, and no literature unit supports it; whether the rating holds beyond this single Ugandan technology is untested [ev_crop_yield_wocat_1595_2013_crop_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Ugandan Rubagano rooftop system's WOCAT sheet rates farm income and food self-sufficiency as increased [ev_household_income_wocat_1595_2013_farm_income, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_food_security_selfsufficiency]. In Brazil, domestic cisterns fully met family drinking and household needs for many households and improved quality of life and health, but did not influence income [ev_household_income_silva09_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The signals point in different directions: a Brazilian household survey from an upper-middle-income setting finds no income effect, while the Ugandan input is a single compiler's ratings that also record the risk of production failure as unchanged [ev_household_income_silva09_3, ev_food_security_wocat_1595_2013_risk_of_production_failure]. Neither source measures income change, and the Brazilian null concerns cash income rather than other welfare outcomes.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Capturing roof runoff in a tank keeps it off the ground around the homestead: the Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates surface runoff as reduced, and the Nepali compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_1595_2013_surface_runoff, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings, and the Nepali sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged despite its comment, so any effect is confined to the homestead and is not measured [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation]. Runoff reduction and sediment retention enter only as component proxies for soil erosion.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The Nepali rooftop rainwater harvesting sheet rates downstream siltation unchanged, while its compiler notes less eroded material from the courtyard [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating of downstream siltation, a component proxy; it says nothing about the quality of the stored water itself [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1497_2011_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Domestic rooftop cisterns store rainwater beside the house, giving households basic drinking and cooking water through the dry season, sharply reducing time spent fetching water and dependence on water trucks [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_4]. The Ugandan Rubagano sheet rates water quantity as greatly increased [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_quantity].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most units come from cistern programmes in Brazil (upper-middle income), largely programme authors and household surveys. A standard cistern covers basic needs only for small households, larger families remain dependent on water trucks, and most households still use other sources as their main supply [ev_water_access_deficit_brito07_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_2, ev_water_access_deficit_silva09_2]. The Ugandan sheet rates overall water availability only slightly improved [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1595_2013_water_availability].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In a Kenyan supplemental-irrigation trial, the poor rainfall of the SR98 season generated very little runoff, and the tarpaulin-lined earth dam that fed the irrigation barely contained any water [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6]. Drought disables a runoff store by leaving it empty: with nothing to harvest, the work cannot deliver water when the crop needs it.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row rests on that Kenyan observation alone. It records the reservoir running dry, not physical damage to the dam, and gives no measure of how often or how badly storage works fail in drought; records of drought-season performance or damage at further sites are needed before the row can say how sensitive runoff storage is [ev_climate_shock_barr05_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A check-dam review notes that examples of check dams failing to meet their objectives are common worldwide and are often associated with structure failure in extreme rainfall events or lack of maintenance [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av]. Among runoff-catchment works, the WOCAT compiler for gully-plugging check dams in Nepal judges them not to cope well with local rainstorms, and gabions and rock check dams in Somalia are rated as coping only moderately with rainstorms and thunderstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1493_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_7778_2026_local_thunderstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Gabion check dams in Tunisia, check dams in China, sand dams in Kenya and stone check walls and check dams in India are judged to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1400_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1455_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1537_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5210_2019_local_rainstorm]; vegetative check dams (fascines) in Madagascar cope well with rainstorms and thunderstorms but moderately with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6478_2022_local_hailstorm]. The review statement does not separate rainfall damage from neglect, and the rest are WOCAT compiler ratings, not measured damage [ev_climate_shock_luca21_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India records that the technology copes well with forest fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state how sensitive these structures are to fire: one practitioner rating, with no observed damage, no stated reasoning and no fire event described [ev_asset_fire_wocat_5210_2019_forest_fire]. It does not show the works go undamaged. What is missing is a second independent source or one observed account of fire damage or its absence.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floods washed away scores of small dams in northern Ghana, 37.9% of boulder-faced log check dams in Ethiopia still failed after a high-magnitude runoff event, and when peak flows break check dams the stored sediment is released rapidly [ev_flood_damage_veno12_1, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_2, ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1]. A check-dam review cites structural failure from the impact of large boulders in extreme floods, and grassed earth gully check dams in Morocco are described as fragile during major floods and needing frequent winter maintenance [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. WOCAT compilers rate gully-plugging check dams in Nepal and check-dam ponds in Ethiopia as not coping well with floods and a haffir and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1493_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1547_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7777_2026_flash_flood]. On China's Loess Plateau, sediment-filled check dams are vulnerable to large floods: on 26 July 2017 more than 200 mm of rain in Suide and Zizhou Counties produced a flood that damaged 20% of the main check dams [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other compilers rate check dams in Tunisia, China and India and sand dams in Kenya as coping well, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia as coping very well with flash floods, so sensitivity varies with construction, and the Moroccan earth check dams depend on frequent maintenance [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1400_2011_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1537_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6716_2023_flash_flood, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1_av]. The check-dam failure and boulder-impact evidence is cited from other studies, the sediment-release statement comes from a USA study, the Ghana finding gives no count of dams lost, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_check_dam_failure_fran21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1_av, ev_flood_damage_veno12_1]. The Loess Plateau figure is a damage count from a single storm event, for dams already filled with sediment [ev_climate_shock_shi19_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rates the technology as coping moderately with heatwaves [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a single practitioner rating with no stated reason or observed damage [ev_asset_heat_stress_wocat_7778_2026_heatwave].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone check walls and check dams in India are rated by their WOCAT compiler as coping moderately with landslides [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide], and a double-basin masonry check dam in Ethiopia as coping well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This rests on just these compiler ratings from technology sheets; neither reports how a landslide would damage the structure, so there is no measured evidence on landslide damage to runoff-catchment works [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_5210_2019_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6716_2023_landslide].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Reservoirs, tanks and dams trap the sediment that runoff carries, so storage fills and function declines: Tigray dams with a 30-year design life were set to run their cycle in 4.4 to 5.7 years, eight of ten Zambian reservoirs lost storage to siltation, 31 percent of earthen dams in Haryana silted up within five years, Moroccan gabions had nearly lost their original function, and small hill dams in Morocco lose 0.5 to 1% of capacity each year to catchment erosion [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_1, ev_asset_siltation_saru19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_iegind11_12, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. Loose-rock check dams on semi-arid rangeland watersheds in the USA were filled to more than 80% of capacity within four years, and a review notes the sediment-control effect of check dams diminishes as they fill and becomes marginal a few years to a few decades after installation [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1_av]. Sedimentation is described as perhaps the primary reason for sand dam failure, and tanks desilted in an Indian programme need desilting again within its lifetime [ev_asset_failure_ritc21_3, ev_asset_siltation_verm19_1]. In Tigray, a survey cited in a review (Berhane et al. 2016) found siltation threatening the benefits of 61% of water-harvesting structures, ahead of leakage and structural damage [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5]; on China's Loess Plateau high sediment loads fill check dams rapidly, so trapping gives only short-term erosion-control benefit [ev_climate_shock_shi19_4]; and in India rainwater-harvesting structures need regular clearing of accumulated silt to stay functional and maximise recharge (Gunnell and Krishnamurthy 2003, cited in a review) [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Severity varies: a Kenyan sand-dam assessment estimates siltation cut storage by 10-25% and judges it neither an inherent limitation nor the main reason dams go unused [ev_asset_siltation_neuf17_1]. Most units are review citations or narrative observations without a common metric, the only directly measured fill rate comes from a high-income rangeland study, and losses depend on upkeep, as the Moroccan structures failed where no maintenance system had been put in place and small hill dams were forgotten once built [ev_asset_siltation_saru19_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1_av, ev_erosion_hazard_iegmar09_2, ev_sediment_retention_roos10_1_av]. The Tigray share and the Indian maintenance point are second-hand citations [ev_climate_shock_gebr18_5, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_11_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate check dams in China and Nepal and sand dams in Kenya as coping well with local windstorms and gabion check dams in Somalia as coping moderately, while fascine (vegetative) check dams in Madagascar are rated as not coping well with tropical storms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1455_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1537_2012_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_7778_2026_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage; the Madagascar sheet alone rates tropical storms, and it concerns a vegetative structure rather than stone or concrete [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_6478_2022_tropical_storm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Water held by runoff structures supports plant growth and habitat around them: the WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia reports that improved soil moisture and reduced erosion supported the growth of different plant and grass species, and that the restored vegetation and water created better conditions for livestock and small wildlife [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_habitat_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity]. Users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive greener surroundings and improved biodiversity [ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. Embrapa reports that crops, vegetable gardens and orchards on the humid fringes of its barraginhas in Brazil bring back fauna that had disappeared for lack of food [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gain is slight: the compiler units all come from a single Somali technology sheet and are mostly rated as slight change, the Ghana unit is a user perception, and no unit measures species or habitat [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_7778_2026_animal_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_veno12_1]. The Brazilian barraginha fauna finding is an adopter-reported indicator in Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no species measured [ev_biodiversity_outcome_mira19_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Carbon removal here runs through vegetation and soil: WOCAT compilers judge that gabions and rock check dams in Somalia increase above-ground biomass and soil organic matter through vegetation recovery and sediment accumulation, storing more carbon in plants and soils, and a second Somali sheet reports some soil organic matter gain as vegetation and soil cover regenerate [ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_emission_of_carbon_and_greenhouse_gases, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7778_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7777_2026_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C]. A check-dam review cites check dams on China's Loess Plateau contributing to carbon sequestration, an effect that grows with time at both dam and watershed level as sediment accumulates [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Apart from the Loess Plateau check-dam finding, which is a secondary citation in a review with no magnitude in the quoted passage, all units are practitioner judgements from Somali technology sheets, all rated slight, with no measured carbon; biomass, soil organic matter and avoided-emission ratings are proxies for carbon removal, and most units come from the same Somali sheet [ev_carbon_sequestration_luca21_1, ev_carbon_sequestration_wocat_7778_2026_biomass_above_ground_C].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Storage structures recharge groundwater around them. Check dams can infiltrate more than 50% of runoff, with recharge linked to episodic storm events, and groundwater tables rise near filled check dams [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_luca21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_fran21_1]. Sand dams can raise the local groundwater, and Biazin et al. cite Hut et al. (2008) for sand dams in Kenya enhancing groundwater recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_biaz12_27]. In India additional recharge from check dams and other water harvesting structures was estimated at 480 million cubic meters per annum, and a state survey found groundwater levels increased in 22 of the 31 districts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_2]. An Indian review cites Badiger et al. (2002) inferring recharge of about 3–8% of rainfall near structures and Sharda et al. (2006) estimating that 11% of annual rainfall could recharge from a structure, and Gore et al. (1998) modelling an overall 16% increase in groundwater recharge from rainwater harvesting in Maharashtra [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_4]. A farm-pond study in Burkina Faso treats seepage as groundwater recharge, a review lists aquifer recharge among cited benefits, and Embrapa says its barraginhas raise the water table and revitalise springs [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_saru19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates them is where the water is counted. Recharge is measured or modelled at or near the structures, while the harm side is flow leaving the watershed: on China's Loess Plateau the check-dam campaign reduced streamflow by approximately 39% [ev_water_yield_luca21_1], and the Indian review cites Sharma and Thakur (2007) estimating that watershed development including more rainwater harvesting would cut runoff by approximately 60% while raising recharge by only 5%, mostly through more evapotranspiration from irrigation, Calder et al. (2008) suggesting rainwater harvesting could close a basin in Andhra Pradesh so no water flows further downstream, and Glendenning and Vervoort (2011) modelling reduced streamflow in Rajasthan [ev_water_yield_glen12_2, ev_water_yield_glen12_5, ev_water_yield_glen12_7]. A theoretical study cited there, Neumann et al. (2004), found the effect on watershed water levels may be minimal beyond the immediate vicinity of a structure, and the sand-dam effect is often limited in space and time [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_glen12_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_ritc21_1]. So local recharge gains for wells near the works can coexist with less water for downstream users and basin planners. Almost every unit is a secondary citation, an estimate or a model; the Burkina Faso recharge is the authors' inference from seepage, and the barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_verm19_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_foxr03_8, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_mira19_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The runoff-catchment per-hectare cost comes from one Somali WOCAT sheet on gully erosion control with gabions and rock structures, whose costed items total 23568.70 USD spread over a treated area of 160 ha [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single compiler cost table for a project-built gully-control package, spread over the whole treated area rather than the structures alone and converted at the sheet's own rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_7778_2026_establishment]. A second independent cost source is needed before the per-hectare figure can be read as typical.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The unit reports how often rehabilitated small dams in Ghana came in under per-irrigated-hectare cost thresholds, comparing the government irrigation authority with donor and NGO implementers.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This is a cost distribution by implementer for reservoir rehabilitation, not a measured cost reduction from water harvesting; treat it as context on rehabilitation cost variability.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Runoff stored in a farm pond and applied as supplemental irrigation carries crops through dry spells. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, supplemental irrigation from a lined earth dam fed by surface runoff, with fertilizer, raised maize yields over fertilised non-irrigated plots in seasons below 300 mm of rain, and in the LR00 drought season only the irrigated plots yielded grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. In a Burkina Faso randomised trial with a hand-dug farm pond, irrigated sorghum yielded 680 against 443 kg per ha in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per ha in 2000 [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]; the companion risk analysis finds all mild dry spells mitigated and severe late-season dry spells only partly mitigated, turned into mild stress [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. Pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers in Cambodia and Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. A water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Biazin et al. cite Kahinda et al. (2007) in semi-arid Zimbabwe for rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raising water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per m3 by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% without one, and Glendenning et al. cite Glendenning and Vervoort (2011), a Rajasthan watershed model in which rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. Sand dams extend supply into drought: in Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after, and in a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins, as easing the effects of droughts on lowland crops [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: There has to be runoff to store. In the Kenyan SR98 season the dam barely filled, so there was no harvested runoff for irrigation and no treatment differed in yield; the Burkina Faso risk analysis puts the probability of drought at 0.1 and finds it cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and the reservoir supports only two irrigation applications where a severe late dry spell needs at least three [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. So the strong effect is a dry-spell effect within a season that still produces runoff, not a defence against a failed season. The Kenyan and Burkina Faso trial gains also depend on fertilizer: in the Kenyan high-rainfall seasons above 300 mm irrigation added no yield, and in Burkina Faso nutrients were the primary limiting factor [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. These trials apply stored water as supplemental irrigation, at the boundary between water harvesting and irrigation. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count, the Brazilian pond and barraginha statements institutional assertions without data, and the WOCAT units compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The supplemental-irrigation, crop-loss, Zimbabwe water-productivity and Rajasthan findings are secondary citations in reviews, the Indian pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint, and the sand-dam results rest on recall-based interviews and a catchment indicator table [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stored runoff applied as supplemental irrigation is where the largest drought-season gains are measured. Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In a Burkina Faso farm-pond trial, sorghum given supplemental irrigation from the harvested runoff yielded 680 against 443 kg per hectare in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per hectare in 2000, both seasons with serious dry spells [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial (Barron and Okwach), supplemental irrigation from a runoff-fed earth dam plus fertiliser raised maize yields over fertilised plots without irrigation in low-rainfall seasons (<300 mm) but not in seasons above 300 mm, and in a dry long-rains season only the irrigated plots produced any grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4]. A risk model of a Burkina Faso farm reservoir, built on field experience, finds all mild dry spells mitigated by supplemental irrigation and severe late dry spells reduced to mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A watershed model of the Arvari in Rajasthan (Glendenning and Vervoort 2011, cited in a review) found rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores, despite reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6]. A survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe (Kahinda et al. 2007, cited in a review) found rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gains hold for dry spells within a season, not for a failed season: where the catchment produces no runoff the store has nothing to give. Storage is exhausted in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional assertion without data, and the Cambodian and Somali units are compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. The supplemental-irrigation and crop-loss statements are secondary citations in reviews, and the Kenyan sand-dam figures come from a catchment indicator table whose values are likely interview-derived [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In the Kenyan dam trial's drought season the catchment yielded no runoff to irrigate with, both biomass and grain were strongly hit by the lack of water, and no treatment differed from another [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5]. The Burkina Faso reservoir model marks the limit: a meteorological drought cannot be mitigated because there is too little water to harvest, and severe late dry spells at flowering and grain filling are only partly mitigated because the reservoir supports two supplemental irrigations where at least three are needed [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The Burkina Faso and Kenyan farm-pond trials, the Burkina Faso reservoir model and the Zimbabwe macro-catchment finding are tagged as bundles: runoff capture and storage are the water-harvesting part, but the yield is delivered through supplemental irrigation, so these units are discounted rather than credited in full to water harvesting [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Runoff-fed storage carries water into dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns catching runoff on China's Loess Plateau are credited with mitigating frequent drought, and a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers for a pond in Cambodia and check dams in Somalia rate drought impacts as reduced, the Cambodian sheet noting the pond provides enough water even during drought and the Somali sheet crediting improved soil moisture retention and infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. Stored water bridges dry spells: a water-harvesting review cites supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells and stabilising yields, and rainwater management is cited as letting producers avoid total crop loss in critical drought periods [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2]. Indian farmers reported a 6% chance of rainy-season crop failure from aberrant rains with a farm pond against 20% in the same crop–tree–livestock system without a pond [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1]. In Zimbabwe the months water could be collected at sand-dam sites in a drought year rose from 5.8 before construction to 9.7 after [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths, as easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. Stored runoff used as irrigation raises the return on scarce water: a survey and modelling study in semi-arid Zimbabwe, cited by Biazin et al., found that rainwater irrigation from macro-catchments raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre by mitigating intra-seasonal dry spells (Kahinda et al., 2007), and a conceptual watershed model for Rajasthan showed that rainwater harvesting structures recharging groundwater gave a slight buffer in drought years (Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Storage is exhausted in prolonged drought: Brazilian subsurface dams tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long droughts, a benefit shortfall rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The Loess Plateau claim is a qualitative assertion, the reservoir finding a vote count and the Brazilian pond statement an institutional assertion without data, and the Cambodian and Somali units are compiler ratings [ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10]. The supplemental-irrigation and crop-loss statements are secondary citations in reviews, the Indian pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint, and the Zimbabwe sand-dam figure rests on recall-based before-and-after interviews [ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_2, ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Zimbabwe and Rajasthan findings are modelling results cited second-hand, and the Rajasthan model also showed the structures reducing streamflow, a downstream cost of the same recharge [ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5, ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Ponds, cisterns and check dams store runoff for use in dry periods: pond water used as supplemental irrigation reduces crop-loss risk in irregular years in semi-arid Brazil, cisterns in China are reported to be mitigating frequent periods of drought, a review of small reservoirs counts improved drought resilience among their cited benefits, and the compiler of a Cambodian on-farm pond sheet states the pond provides enough water even during drought [ev_drought_hazard_brito07_10, ev_drought_hazard_iegchn07_4, ev_drought_hazard_saru19_1, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_drought_impacts]. The WOCAT compiler for gabions and rock check dams in Somalia likewise judges drought impacts reduced, citing improved soil moisture retention and water infiltration [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_drought_impacts]. In a Kenyan catchment with sand dams the number of people exposed to droughts fell from 420 to 0 while a control catchment stayed at 600 [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. In Brazil, Embrapa describes its barraginhas, small semicircular runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in pastures and croplands, as storing water in the soil by infiltration and easing the effects of droughts on crops in the lowlands [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. A Burkina Faso risk analysis of a farm reservoir used for supplemental irrigation finds that all of the mild dry spells can be mitigated, which explains the more frequent zero-stress seasons under irrigation than in the control, and that severe dry spells late in the season are partly mitigated, turned into mild ones [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_7, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. A conceptual watershed model for the Arvari watershed in Rajasthan showed rainwater harvesting gave a slight buffer in drought years through more reliable groundwater stores (Glendenning and Vervoort, 2011, cited by Glendenning et al.) [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The class is held at moderate because few of the benefit units say how big the effect is. Most of the pool is practitioner judgements and assertions without drought-loss metrics: an expert account from Brazil, a lender evaluation in China, compiler ratings from Cambodia and Somalia, and a review that counts how often small-reservoir studies cite improved drought resilience; only a Kenyan sand-dam catchment table compares people exposed to droughts against a control catchment, and its values are likely interview-derived [ev_drought_hazard_lasage08_1]. Subsurface dams in Brazil tended to dry out in a rainless year and small ones do not withstand long dry spells, which records no benefit when storage is exhausted rather than damage to the works [ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_2, ev_drought_hazard_cirilo03_3]. The barraginha statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measured drought contrast and no normal-year reference [ev_drought_hazard_mira19_8]. The Burkina Faso analysis marks the limit of storage: a drought year, with a probability of 0.1, cannot be mitigated because there is insufficient water to harvest, and the late severe dry spells need at least three irrigation applications while the reservoir supports only two [ev_drought_hazard_fox05_5, ev_drought_hazard_fox05_6]. The Rajasthan buffer is a model result cited second-hand, and the same model showed rainwater harvesting reducing streamflow [ev_drought_hazard_glen12_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are construction costs per structure: village ponds or tanks and dry-stone check dams (per cubic metre of masonry) from a World Bank watershed project in Himachal Pradesh, India, and compiler-reported WOCAT establishment costs for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, a set of check dams and walls in India, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The project figures are self-reported from monitoring in nominal rupees and the WOCAT figures are each compiler's own cost table converted with the sheet's exchange rate; none are market prices. The structures range from a fascine line of a few metres to a haffir of about 5100 square metres, and the per-cubic-metre figure is per volume of masonry built, not water stored, so the cost class should be read with that spread of denominators in mind.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for stone check walls and check dams in India rates fire risk as decreased, but the sheet gives no explanation of how the structures would do this [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk]. Part of any such effect would be off-site, at landscape scale rather than on the adopting farm.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single practitioner rating with no stated mechanism and no measurement, for one Indian technology [ev_fire_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_fire_risk]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, dams and check dams store or slow runoff: users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits, the Kenyan compiler notes a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding, the Ethiopian compiler that the structure and rehabilitated areas reduce the speed and impacts of the flood, and the Somali compiler that stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity and flood-related erosion [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Size can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. The only peak-flow reduction is a secondary citation in a review, the Italian cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting, the Ghana finding is user perception and the rest are compiler ratings or institutional assertions [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, check dams and haffirs store or slow runoff: users of small reservoirs in northern Ghana list limiting rainy-season floods among their benefits, the Kenyan compiler notes a dam or series of dams buffers downstream flooding, the Ethiopian check-dam compiler that the structure and rehabilitated areas reduce the speed and impacts of the flood, and the Somali compiler that stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity and flood-related erosion [ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage during the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The same check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures were ill-designed and not maintained [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3]. Size can reverse the effect: larger sand dams increase the risk of flooding, erosion and seepage [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. The only peak-flow reduction is a secondary citation in a review, the Italian cases are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting, the Ghana finding is user perception and the rest are compiler ratings or institutional assertions [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Dams, check dams and gabions slow runoff and buffer peak flows: WOCAT compilers in Kenya, Ethiopia and Somalia rate flooding as reduced, the Kenyan sheet because a dam or series of dams creates a buffer downstream, the Ethiopian because the structure and rehabilitated areas reduce the speed of the flood, and the Somali because stone lines, gabions and rock check dams reduced runoff velocity; users of small reservoirs in Ghana perceive fewer rainy-season floods [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_1537_2012_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_flood_impacts, ev_flood_hazard_veno12_1]. A check-dam review cites check dams mitigating flooding and significantly reducing peak flow in Iran and check-dam sequences proving effective against strong floods in Italian torrents, and small hill dams in Morocco are credited with damping damage in the serious 2002-2003 floods [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2, ev_flood_hazard_roos10_1]. Embrapa credits its barraginhas, small runoff-retention basins dug along runoff paths in Brazil, with easing floods as well [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Nearly all units are practitioner judgements, user perceptions or secondary citations, not measurements. Size can reverse the effect: a review notes larger sand dams raise flooding, erosion and seepage risk [ev_flood_hazard_ritc21_1]. The check-dam review finds a minimal effect against extreme floods, especially where structures are ill-designed or poorly maintained; its supporting cases are secondary citations, and the Italian ones are mountain torrent control in a high-income setting [ev_flood_hazard_luca21_3, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_1, ev_flood_hazard_luca21_2]. The barraginha flood statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, unmeasured, and a landscape-scale effect rather than one on the adopting farm [ev_flood_hazard_mira19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Ponds, cisterns, subsurface dams and gully check dams store runoff for gardens, crops and livestock, widening diets and carrying households through the lean season. In Brazil, subsurface dams gave families more fruit and vegetables and more food overall, production cisterns allow daily garden irrigation, and adopters of small catchment basins rated food security as the technology's largest impact [ev_food_security_cirilo03_6, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_mira19_2]. In Burkina Faso, runoff cisterns irrigate gardens and water livestock in the lean season, and adopters of rainwater-harvesting ponds showed statistically significant improvements in food-security indicators [ev_food_security_roose94_1, ev_food_security_silv26_1]; Biazin et al. cite Desta (2004) for Ethiopian farmers who adopted rainwater-harvesting irrigation properly having improved their dietary status [ev_food_security_biaz12_26], and a review counts 15 citations for improved food security [ev_food_security_saru19_1]. WOCAT compilers add that farm ponds in Cambodia keep enough water for irrigation during drought, gully check dams in Ethiopia open more rangeland for pastoralists' livestock, and gully rehabilitation in Somalia improved household food availability [ev_food_security_wocat_2844_2017_risk_of_production_failure, ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_7778_2026_food_security_selfsufficiency].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The literature is mostly qualitative, cited in reviews or vote counts, and gives no size of effect; much of it comes from upper-middle-income Brazil, including Embrapa's own assessment and programme reviews, so transfer to low-income settings is adjacent rather than direct [ev_food_security_mira19_2, ev_food_security_arsky20_6, ev_food_security_saru19_1, ev_food_security_silv26_1]. The Ethiopian dietary finding is a secondary citation, and the rainwater-harvesting irrigation it describes uses stored water to irrigate, at the boundary between water harvesting and irrigation [ev_food_security_biaz12_26]. The WOCAT units are practitioner judgements, and the Ethiopian gully sheet rates only a slight gain, which works through more rangeland for grazing rather than crop supply [ev_food_security_wocat_6716_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, small reservoirs, subsurface dams, farm ponds, check dams and haffirs store runoff that farmers use to irrigate more land and take a second or dry-season crop, while sediment trapped behind check dams can be planted with fodder; in Kenya sand-dam water lets farmers irrigate more crops and raise production, and in Brazil soil management in subsurface dams raised crop productivity [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_crop_yield_brito07_5, ev_crop_yield_wocat_2844_2017_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6716_2023_fodder_production]. WOCAT compilers in Somalia describe reliable irrigation from a haffir improving tomato and watermelon, grasses regenerating around the dam, and better water and fodder raising animal production, while a second Somali sheet credits stone lines, rock check dams and gabions with better moisture retention on farmland and more grazing [ev_crop_yield_wocat_7777_2026_crop_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_7777_2026_animal_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_7778_2026_crop_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_7778_2026_animal_production]. Sand dams in Kenya cut crop failure against a control catchment, and in Zimbabwe improved water availability improved livestock health where cattle had been driven up to 20 km to water [ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1, ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1]. Stored water also stabilises output: Indian farmers reported crop-failure chances falling from 20% to 6% in the rainy season and from 100% to 5–10% in winter with a farm pond, reviews report rainwater harvesting systems stabilising production under intra-seasonal rainfall variability and supplemental irrigation of 50–200 mm bridging critical dry spells, wheat output in Pakistan rose from 450 to 815 kg over seven years after small reservoirs were built, a bundle of moisture conservation, rainwater harvesting and micro-irrigation in India raised system productivity by 25%, and silt farmland behind check dams on China's Loess Plateau yields 6–10 times more than sloping farmland [ev_yield_stability_pals23_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2, ev_yield_stability_silv26_1, ev_yield_stability_rock10_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_silv26_1, ev_crop_yield_luca21_1]. In Rwanda, runoff from the terrace waterways collected in a dug, lined pond and applied to maize by a gravity drip kit as supplementary irrigation gave 11982 kg per hectare against 4755 on flat rainfed plots [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. Trials of supplemental irrigation from stored runoff now measure the gain directly. In Burkina Faso, sorghum under the farmer's normal practice averaged 455 kg per hectare over 3 years, against 712 with supplemental irrigation alone and 1403 with irrigation plus fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_1, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_2]; a model of the same kind of system puts the long-term average gain from supplemental irrigation at 150%, or 450 kg per hectare [ev_crop_yield_fox05_1]. In Kenya, maize with supplemental irrigation from a runoff dam plus fertiliser averaged 1796 kg per hectare against 1375 without irrigation, with the steadiest yields (a coefficient of variation of 5% against 11% for the farmers' control) and more grain per mm of rain and irrigation (4.1 against 2.1 kg per mm per hectare) [ev_crop_yield_barr05_1, ev_yield_stability_barr05_8, ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9]. In Pakistan, supplemental irrigation from harvested rainwater raised yields over adjacent rainfed fields by 146% for wheat, 101% for mustard, 118% for maize and 101% for pearl millet [ev_crop_yield_waqa25_1, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_2, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_3, ev_crop_yield_waqa25_4]. On China's Loess Plateau, cropland formed behind silted check dams is reported to produce 2 to 3 times more food than terraced cropland and 6 to 10 times more than sloping cropland (Jin et al. 2012; Wang et al. 2011) [ev_crop_yield_shi19_5], and in semi-arid Zimbabwe supplementary irrigation from ex-situ water harvesting raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In a Burkina Faso farm-pond trial, sorghum given supplemental irrigation from the harvested runoff yielded 680 against 443 kg per hectare in 1999 and 1138 against 634 kg per hectare in 2000, both seasons with serious dry spells [ev_crop_yield_foxr03_4, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_5]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial (Barron and Okwach), supplemental irrigation from a runoff-fed earth dam plus fertiliser raised maize yields over fertilised plots without irrigation in low-rainfall seasons (<300 mm) but not in seasons above 300 mm, and in a dry long-rains season only the irrigated plots produced any grain at all [ev_crop_yield_barr05_3, ev_crop_yield_barr05_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings from technology sheets, and the literature units are largely reviews citing earlier studies, an expert's personal communication on livestock, and Brazilian case accounts from an upper-middle-income setting [ev_crop_yield_ritc21_1, ev_livestock_productivity_veno12_1, ev_crop_yield_cirilo03_4]. A Brazilian subsurface dam produced no harvest in a year of adverse weather [ev_crop_yield_brito07_6]; fodder and livestock outcomes enter only as components of the production gap. The Kenyan and Zimbabwean sand-dam findings come from interviews and respondent statements [ev_crop_yield_lasage08_1, ev_livestock_productivity_lazurko24_1]. Soil salinisation may appear on check-dam farmland, the Pakistani wheat figure has no area denominator, the Indian productivity gain bundles micro-irrigation, and the pond figures come from a farmer survey reported in a preprint [ev_crop_yield_luca21_1, ev_crop_yield_silv26_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_silv26_1, ev_yield_stability_pals23_2]. The Rwandan pond result is a bundle — terrace runoff capture, a lined storage pond and drip irrigation — so the yield is delivered through irrigation hardware and cannot be read as a pure capture effect; it is one season of a randomised trial in which every plot received farmyard manure and mineral fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_uwiz18h1_3]. The irrigation gain depends on inputs and the season. Supplemental irrigation without fertiliser did not raise Kenyan maize yields, and in the first Burkina Faso season, with good rainfall distribution, irrigated and non-irrigated plots did not differ significantly, fertiliser being the main reason for higher yields that year [ev_crop_yield_barr05_2, ev_crop_yield_foxr03_3]. In good-rainfall Kenyan seasons (>350 mm) irrigation had no or slightly adverse effects on final yields [ev_crop_yield_barr05_7], and overall water-use efficiency of rain plus irrigation did not rise with irrigation in Burkina Faso [ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6]. In Tigray, irrigation chiefly from water-harvesting schemes raised output risk when used alone and lowered it only in combination with improved seed and fertiliser [ev_yield_stability_kato11_8]. The Burkina Faso model adds that the yield gain from supplemental irrigation alone does not pay back the labour and capital invested [ev_crop_yield_fox05_1]. The Pakistani gains compare irrigated with adjacent rainfed fields rather than a randomised control, and the Loess Plateau multipliers are second-hand, with no baseline yield [ev_crop_yield_waqa25_1, ev_crop_yield_shi19_5]. In the Kenyan dam trial's drought season the catchment yielded no runoff to irrigate with, both biomass and grain were strongly hit by the lack of water, and no treatment differed from another [ev_crop_yield_barr05_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are compiler-reported annual maintenance costs from WOCAT technology sheets: per structure for a farm pond with irrigation system in Cambodia, check dams and walls in India, a fascine line in Madagascar and a haffir in Somalia, and per hectare for sheets in India and Somalia (the Somalia sheet spreading its total over 160 ha).
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class is set from the per-structure figures while the value range is per hectare, and structures range from a short fascine line to a large haffir, so neither summary is a comparable unit cost.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Small reservoirs, sand dams, farm ponds, runoff cisterns and subsurface dams provide water for dry-season irrigation of vegetables and fruit and for livestock, shifting cropping towards higher-value crops and raising household income [ev_household_income_veno12_2, ev_household_income_ritc21_3]. In Kenya, farmers living near sand dams saw average income rise by 60% as more water in dry periods raised farm yields [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]. Reviews add that rainwater-harvesting ponds brought statistically significant gains in household income in Burkina Faso, water storage gave Ethiopian smallholders greater income security, harvested water used with precision irrigation in Ethiopia reached a net water value of up to 1.53 USD per cubic metre, and benefit-cost ratios reached up to 3.38 with payback periods of 6.8 to 12 years; Indian farms with a farm pond reported net returns of 857 USD per hectare against 586 without [ev_household_income_silv26_1, ev_household_income_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_silv26_1, ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1]. In Brazil, an Embrapa survey of some communities found small-farm incomes rose by about half a minimum wage per month after the second filling of the barraginhas [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. The Cambodian pond compiler rates farm income up because every crop yielded well once there was enough irrigation water [ev_household_income_wocat_2844_2017_farm_income]. Returns on stored runoff can be high: farm-pond supplemental irrigation of maize in Kenya gave net seasonal revenue of US$ 150 and could raise the annual return by 150% (Ngigi et al. 2005), road-catchment harvesting for paddy in Tanzania returned more than US$ 12 per person-day against US$ 3.7 for rainfed sorghum (Hatibu et al. 2006), and a Peruvian programme building 31 cochas returned 1.96 soles per sol invested (Tafur, cited in a programme review) [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_biaz12_21, ev_economic_return_card22_1]. A Burkina Faso and Kenya model puts net profit from water harvesting with supplemental irrigation, fertiliser and an off-season tomato crop at 151–626 USD per hectare a year in Burkina Faso and 109–477 in Kenya, against at most 15 and 40–130 under current practice [ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_fox05_4]. In Pakistan, maize irrigated from harvested rainwater earned 0.28 US$ net per cubic metre in the first year, with a cumulative benefit-cost ratio projected at 2.02 by the second year and 3.53 by the third, and fish farming in a farm pond earned US$ 1799 net on average, about US$ 2951 in mini-dams [ev_economic_return_waqa25_5, ev_household_income_waqa25_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Most literature magnitudes are secondary citations in reviews or vote counts [ev_household_income_saru19_3, ev_household_income_veno12_3]. Sand dams are judged likely not cost-efficient for water supply, Brazilian subsurface dams produced little cash income where electricity, investment capital or an irrigation tradition were missing, and the high Brazilian benefit-cost ratios come from an upper-middle-income context [ev_economic_return_ritc21_1, ev_household_income_cirilo03_7, ev_economic_return_cirilo03_10]. The Kenyan sand-dam income rise compares a small sample of households with a control catchment [ev_household_income_lasage08_1]; the reviewed figures are reported at their upper end, the Indian pond returns come from a cross-sectional survey confounded by farm size and assets [ev_economic_return_silv26_2, ev_economic_return_pals23_1], and the barraginha income finding is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology from an informal survey [ev_household_income_mira19_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty.
