The returns hinge on what the water is used for and on inputs: in the Burkina Faso model the yield gain from supplemental irrigation alone does not compensate for the labour and capital invested [ev_economic_return_fox05_2], and in Pakistan pearl millet irrigated from harvested rainwater lost 0.27 US$ per cubic metre in the first year and stayed below break-even by the third [ev_economic_return_waqa25_6]. The Kenyan, Tanzanian and Peruvian returns are second-hand citations, the model profits rely on a high-value tomato crop and vary with the cost put on labour, and the Pakistani figures are projections assuming constant prices and water productivity [ev_economic_return_biaz12_20, ev_economic_return_card22_1, ev_economic_return_fox05_3, ev_economic_return_waqa25_5].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines and gully plugs trap sediment in gullies and channels, reducing catchment sediment export, and hill reservoirs reduce outlet flows [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_roose06_4]. WOCAT compilers describe masonry check dams in Ethiopia slowing runoff so soil accumulates upstream, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia cutting runoff speed and gully expansion, controlled runoff reducing erosion close to a Somali haffir, and a Cambodian pond allowing crops in all seasons as vegetation cover [ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7778_2026_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7777_2026_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_2844_2017_soil_loss]. Check dams on China's Loess Plateau reduced erosion rates from more than 200 to 20–25 t per hectare a year and cut regional runoff and sediment by about 15% and 85%, check dams at the outlets of five Chinese catchments accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction over 26 years, vegetated check dams in northern Ethiopia significantly reduced peak flow and runoff volume, loose-rock check dams on USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of sediment yield, and small ponds in Germany and Belgium trapped 54-85% and 68% of incoming sediment [ev_erosion_hazard_luca21_1, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_runoff_reduction_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. In Brazil, barraginhas dispersed across farms capture runoff water, which Embrapa says prevents erosion, siltation and the carrying of pollutants [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5]. Well-designed concrete or masonry check dams reduce stream power, sediment transport and channel erosion (Liu 1992, cited in a review) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_11]. On China's Loess Plateau, a watershed model found check-dam construction cut runoff by 12% and sediment by 11.7%, check dams in the Yanhe watershed cut rainy-season runoff by 15.5%–28.9% (Xu et al. 2013), and check dams cut the sediment load of the Huangfuchuan catchment by 51.9% in a sediment delivery model (Zhao et al. 2017) [ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_6, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings; the pooled sediment figures come from a single check-dam synthesis, so the independent literature base is narrow [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_fran21_3]. Check dams can cause downstream channel incision through the clear-water effect (documented in Spain, a high-income setting), gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising to keep working, and the Ethiopian compiler notes that the visible siltation held back has not been quantified [ev_erosion_hazard_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. USA check dams had no significant effect on the runoff volume of major storms and their reduction of outlet sediment was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_2, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]; the Chinese, Ethiopian and European figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA and European sites are high-income [ev_runoff_reduction_poly14_1]. The barraginha erosion statement is Embrapa's self-assessment of its own technology, with no measurement [ev_runoff_reduction_mira19_4, ev_erosion_hazard_mira19_5]. Structures that are abandoned or collapse can turn into erosion sources: decades after channel runoff-control structures on Arizona rangelands were abandoned, a large share had failed and some accelerated headcut retreat and scouring, and failed stone terraces across dry channels in the Israeli Negev induced rill and gully erosion [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_12, ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_13]. The Loess Plateau figures are model results, partly cited second-hand [ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_1, ev_runoff_reduction_shi19_6, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Check dams, gabions and ponds store sediment in channels, reducing catchment sediment yield and the topsoil washed downstream [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. WOCAT compilers rate downstream siltation as reduced for gabions and check dams in Somalia that trap sediment upstream, and for a masonry check dam in Ethiopia that holds back visible siltation [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. In the literature check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1], and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Modelling on the Loess Plateau gives a similar picture: a SWAT simulation found check dam construction decreased sediment by 11.7%, and studies cited in the same paper attribute a 79.4%–85.5% sediment decrease in the Yanhe watershed (Xu et al., 2013) and a 51.9% cut in sediment load in the Huangfuchuan catchment (Zhao et al., 2017) to check dams [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, and nothing on downstream water chemistry is measured; the pooled check-dam magnitudes come from a single synthesis, the Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified, and gabions in Morocco have filled up and need raising to keep trapping sediment [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. The other figures are mostly secondary citations in reviews, the USA, German and Belgian sites are high-income, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment at the USA sites was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. The Loess Plateau figures are all model estimates, and the range between them (from 11.7% to over 79.4%) shows how much the result depends on the catchment and on how many dams are modelled [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sand dams, check dams, subsurface dams, ponds and production cisterns store water in sand, soil or tanks and recharge local groundwater, extending the months of water access and keeping livestock watered when other sources dry up. WOCAT compilers judge sand dams in Kenya, an on-farm pond in Cambodia and a haffir, gabions and check dams in Somalia to improve water collection, quantity or availability: sand dams capture excess flood flows, the pond collects rainwater and groundwater, and the Somali structures slow runoff and improve infiltration [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare against the farmers' control [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9], and supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season, and only part of assessed dams would hold enough water for reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3, ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. Several literature units are review citations, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Somali haffir compiler itself records improved local water availability with little benefit downstream [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence for these structures now sits in the catchment water yield rows, which also answer what upstream capture does to water downstream. In Burkina Faso, overall water-use efficiency of rain plus irrigation did not rise with supplemental irrigation, so the extra yield came with extra water [ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6]; the Kenyan efficiency gain also carries fertiliser, and the Zimbabwe figure is a survey-and-modelling estimate cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9, ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for gully plugging with check dams in Nepal, stone check walls and check dams in India and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6716_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no stated reasoning or measurement, and the Chinese check-dam and Indian farm-pond sheets rate drainage as unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for check dams in India and for stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, the Somali compiler noting the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no measurement, and the storm ratings concern rain-storm runoff damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with drought, and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1013_2011_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1333_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6715_2023_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no observed damage data; spate systems depend on flood flows, so drought is more likely to cut their water supply than to damage the structures.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local rainstorms, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as coping moderately, and marab agriculture in Jordan as coping very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1013_2011_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1333_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6715_2023_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_5770_2020_local_rainstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Large floods could wash out traditional spate diversion structures in Yemen, making it hard to get floodwater onto the land, and the WOCAT compiler for jessour in Tunisia rates them as not coping well with river floods [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1013_2011_general_river_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statement refers to diversions before project improvements, and compilers for water spreading in Sudan and spate irrigation in Eritrea rate coping as good, water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia as moderate and marab agriculture in Jordan as very good [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_3, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1292_2015_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1333_2010_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6715_2023_flash_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_5770_2020_flash_flood]. All ratings are practitioner judgements without damage records.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate jessour in Tunisia and spate irrigation in Eritrea as coping well with local windstorms [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1013_2011_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1333_2010_local_windstorm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without observed damage or stated reasoning.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The compiler of a WOCAT sheet on water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judged habitat and plant diversity slightly increased; no mechanism is described.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: A single technology sheet supplies all units and it rated animal diversity unchanged; these are practitioner judgements, not measurements.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets for marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan, water spreading in Sudan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate soil organic matter increased under these flood-spreading systems, and the Ethiopian sheet also rates emissions reduced; the sheets give no mechanism for these ratings.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner judgements with no compiler comment, not measurements; the Jordan sheet rates the gain strongly while the Sudan and Ethiopia sheets rate it as slight, and soil organic matter and emission ratings stand in for sequestration.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: In Yemen, groundwater tables downstream of spate and conservation structures were maintained or increased, and although the main purpose of the spate irrigation systems was to capture floodwater, a large number of the beneficiary farmers interviewed indicated that groundwater levels increased considerably [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. Groundwater is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units come from one World Bank completion report — a results-framework comment and farmer interviews — so the evidence is self-reported, from one country, with no figure for recharge or flow [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_yem12_2]. No unit measures flow below the diversions.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are the up-front investment in floodwater-diversion systems: compiler-reported establishment costs per hectare from WOCAT sheets for Tunisia and Jordan (the Jordan sheet's total spread over 10 ha), and the average investment cost of spate systems under a World Bank project in Yemen, reported at USD 800-1200 per hectare with farmers contributing a 15-20% share.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT figures are the compiler's own cost tables for the documented technology, summed and converted to USD with the sheet's own exchange rate; they are not market prices. The cost class rests on the Tunisian sheet alone, because the Yemen completion-report range has no single value and the Jordan sheet is an upper-middle-income case; the Yemen report itself calls the farmer contribution comparatively high, and none of these is a cost per hectare restored.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for a floodplain marab system in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drought impacts as reduced [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are compiler ratings with no comment or measurement behind them, and the Jordanian sheet is from an upper-middle-income country outside the target band [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Compilers of WOCAT sheets on marab floodplain water harvesting in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia judge drought impacts reduced, without describing the mechanism.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Only practitioner judgements from technology sheets, with no measurement; the Jordan sheet comes from an upper-middle-income context adjacent to the target.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and diversion structures slow and spread flood flows: Bank reporting from Yemen says they reduce soil erosion and control floods while distributing water more evenly to downstream farmers, and the WOCAT compiler for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rates downstream flooding as reduced, noting the structure reduces the speed and volume of downstream flooding [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen statement is an assertion in a Bank completion report and the Ethiopian unit is a compiler rating; neither measures flood peaks or damage, and much of the effect is downstream of the structures rather than on the farm that builds them [ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Water-spreading weirs and spate diversion structures slow and spread flood flows: the Ethiopian weir compiler states the structure reduces the speed and volume of downstream flooding, and the Yemen completion report says spate and diversion structures control floods and distribute water more evenly to downstream farmers [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The pool is a practitioner judgement from an Ethiopian technology sheet plus a lender self-reported assertion from Yemen; neither measures flood peaks or volumes [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_yem12_4].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: A single WOCAT compiler, for water spreading weirs in Ethiopia, rates the risk of production failure as lowered and attributes this to improved crop resilience from better soil moisture [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: it rests on a single practitioner judgement from a documented technology sheet, with no household survey or measured change in food security [ev_food_security_wocat_6715_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. A second independent source or a measured food-security outcome for spate or floodwater-spreading systems is needed before a class can be stated.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, spate irrigation in Eritrea and marab floodplain farming in Jordan divert and spread floodwater over fields: the Ethiopian compiler states it is the expert's conviction that crop production increased with water harvested and spread over the farm as spate or supplementary irrigation to the seasonal rainfall [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. Much of the gain goes to livestock: in Jordan the barley is mostly used to feed animals and the stubble is grazed, in Eritrea residues are fed to livestock, and in Ethiopia fodder rises with the soil and moisture conserved behind the structure, with animal production increasing as feed becomes more available [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_fodder_production, ev_livestock_productivity_wocat_6715_2023_animal_production].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT technology sheet; there is no literature measurement in this cell, and the Ethiopian crop rating is stated as the expert's conviction rather than a yield comparison [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6715_2023_crop_production]. Most of the remaining support is for fodder and animal production rather than food crops, which is why the class is only slight [ev_forage_productivity_wocat_5770_2020_fodder_production, ev_forage_productivity_wocat_1333_2010_fodder_production].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The spate family's recurrent cost is the compiler's yearly maintenance table for a Jordanian marab floodplain system, costed over 10 ha and expressed per hectare per year [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one practitioner-reported figure from an upper-middle-income country, outside the target band [ev_project_cost_wocat_5770_2020_maintenance]. A second independent cost source, ideally from a low- or lower-middle-income country, is needed.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Floodwater-diverting systems are judged to pay back over time: compilers of WOCAT sheets for jessour in Tunisia, water spreading in Sudan, marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate the long-term returns on establishment as favourable or very favourable, and those for Tunisia, Jordan and Ethiopia rate long-term returns on maintenance the same way [ev_economic_return_wocat_1013_2011_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1292_2015_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_6715_2023_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_1013_2011_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_maintenance_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_6715_2023_costbenefit_maintenance_long].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner benefit-versus-cost judgement from a documented technology sheet, with no comment attached, not a household survey or measured income change, and poverty is reached only through a return proxy. The ratings are long-term; none speaks to the up-front cost of the works, and the Jordanian sheet comes from an upper-middle-income setting [ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_establishment_long, ev_economic_return_wocat_5770_2020_costbenefit_maintenance_long].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading structures control flood flows on the land: in Yemen spate development reduces damage to wadi banks and lets areas re-green, with 64% of the farmers interviewed emphasising the reduced erosion, and the Ethiopian compiler for water-spreading weirs says the physical barriers stop soil and water loss [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Yemen figure is a share of farmers who perceived the benefit, reported in a lender completion report, not a measured soil loss, and the Ethiopian unit is a practitioner rating from a WOCAT sheet [ev_erosion_hazard_yem12_5, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_soil_loss]. Neither gives the size of the reduction in soil loss, so the class rests on direction and rating rather than on a measured effect.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Sheets for jessour in Tunisia, marab floodplain farming in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate downstream siltation as reduced, as floodwater and its sediment are spread and held on the fields [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_1013_2011_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6715_2023_downstream_siltation].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation, a component proxy for water quality, and the Jordan comment states reduced siltation as a desired rather than an observed outcome [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_5770_2020_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Spate and water-spreading systems divert floodwater onto fields, and water productivity, the grain produced per unit of water, is the route by which that capture would ease water stress; the WOCAT guideline authors rate improving water productivity for the floodwater harvesting group as a gain, at the lowest step of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: its single unit is a group-level judgement in the WOCAT water-harvesting guidelines, direction only, with no measurement of water availability or water productivity for spate systems [ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_2]. A second independent source, or any measured result on water access or water productivity under spate or water spreading, would let the cell state a class. The Yemeni groundwater reports sit in the spate catchment water yield row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan and water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Both units are practitioner ratings without stated reasoning or measurement, from technologies built to spread floodwater over fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the WOCAT compiler rating for water-spreading weirs in Ethiopia, which records no change in the impacts of cyclones and rain storms, so no mechanism is evidenced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: a single compiler rating from one technology sheet, with no comment or measurement, neither supports nor rules out an effect [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6715_2023_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source or one measured finding is needed before this row can state a direction or size.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate terraces, stone lines and stone bunds in China, Rwanda, Yemen, Cabo Verde, Uganda, Niger, Haiti and Tunisia as coping well with drought, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately [ev_asset_drought_wocat_1522_2010_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_1553_2012_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_6610_2022_drought, ev_asset_drought_wocat_4284_2018_drought].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings of coping, with no observed damage or failure data.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Storms cause extensive damage to terraces on China's Loess Plateau, with few local funds to repair it, poorly structured vineyard terraces in Spain suffered severe landslides after a single rainstorm, and in Algeria a poorly maintained banquette network fails in a chain reaction during torrential and prolonged rains, the smallest unrepaired breach spreading sliding through the whole network [ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda, stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with local rainstorms [ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7, ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1553_2012_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1573_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1616_2014_local_rainstorm]. A review of terraced landscapes describes the mechanism: soil saturation on terraces in very heavy storms, or runoff accumulating behind the walls, is a determining factor in the failure and movement of terrace risers, and under heavy rainfall landslides normally confined to small parts of a terrace can become debris flows across the whole terraced hillside [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Other compilers judge progressive bench terraces in China, stone-covered bench terraces in Yemen, stone lines in Uganda, vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti and bench terraces in Bangladesh to cope well with rainstorms, and a continuous bench terrace for tea in Thailand to cope very well [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1522_2010_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1560_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_1589_2013_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_3223_2017_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_rainstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4281_2018_local_rainstorm]; thunderstorms are rated as coping moderately for Bangladesh terraces and vegetated stone bunds in Burkina Faso, while Bangladesh terraces cope very well with hailstorms [ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_6729_2023_local_thunderstorm, ev_asset_extreme_rainfall_wocat_4284_2018_local_hailstorm]. Damage in the literature follows poor construction or maintenance (poorly structured terraces in Spain, poorly maintained banquettes in Algeria) and the Loess Plateau evaluation gives no measure of damage, so apart from the terrace review the rest of the evidence is compiler ratings [ev_climate_shock_wei16_2_av, ev_climate_shock_arab04_1_av, ev_climate_shock_iegchn07_7]. The review statements describe how failure happens, not how often, and give no magnitude [ev_climate_shock_arna15_8_av, ev_climate_shock_arna15_9_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh records that the technology copes moderately with forest fire and well with land fire [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The evidence is too thin to state a sensitivity: both units come from one technology sheet and are practitioner ratings, with no observed damage or fire event described, and coping moderately itself implies some damage [ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_forest_fire, ev_asset_fire_wocat_4284_2018_land_fire]. What is missing is a second independent source or one observed account of how terraces fared in a fire.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Banquettes lack the capacity to absorb runoff from erosive rains and overflow, diversion channels fill with eroded soil and overflow in the heaviest storms, and torrential rain collapses terrace walls or carries small terraces away in mass movements [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. WOCAT compilers judge radical terraces in Rwanda and contour stone bunds in Niger not to cope well with river floods, while stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde, stone lines in Tunisia and gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan are judged to cope well [ev_asset_flood_wocat_1553_2012_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1616_2014_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_1573_2013_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_6610_2022_general_river_flood, ev_asset_flood_wocat_7553_2025_flash_flood].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Failure is tied to maintenance and setting: rarely maintained diversion systems generally fail after 4 to 10 years, terrace collapse is linked to abandonment, and the Rwandan mass movement happened on terraces without trees [ev_flood_hazard_roose94_2, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_5]. The literature hazards are erosive rains, torrential rain and mass movements mapped to flood and come as expert and modelled statements without failure rates, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than records of damage [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Slope failure damages terraces where slopes are unstable or terraces are abandoned: in the Tizi Ouzou region of Algeria 19% of banquettes on marls and clays were damaged by landslides and as many by gullying, and in Mediterranean regions over 50% of abandoned terraces were vulnerable to gully erosion and landslides that collapse the dry-stone walls [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: WOCAT compilers judge stone lines in Tunisia and a continuous bench terrace for tea in a high sloping area of Thailand to cope well with landslides, and vetiver-hedge bench terraces with trees in Haiti and bench terraces on hilly slopes in Bangladesh to cope very well [ev_asset_landslide_wocat_6610_2022_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4281_2018_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_3223_2017_landslide, ev_asset_landslide_wocat_4284_2018_landslide]. The damage figures are secondary citations tied to marl and clay substrates and to abandonment rather than to maintained terraces, and the ratings are practitioner judgements [ev_climate_shock_arab04_2_av, ev_climate_shock_wei16_1_av].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers rate stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and contour stone bunds in Niger as coping well with local windstorms, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti as coping well with tropical storms, and bench terraces in Bangladesh as coping moderately with both [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1573_2013_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1616_2014_local_windstorm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_3223_2017_tropical_storm, ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_4284_2018_tropical_storm].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings without observed damage, and the progressive bench terrace in China is rated as not coping well with local windstorms, with no reason given [ev_asset_wind_cyclone_wocat_1522_2010_local_windstorm].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The sources point in opposite directions for different kinds of terrace and different kinds of diversity. The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan rates plant diversity as greatly increased, linking it to the soil becoming suitable for more diverse crops [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity]. A rangeland-restoration review cites Stavi et al. (2015) from Israel suggesting that earthen contour bench terraces built by heavy machinery, which strip the soil's A-horizon from the hillslope, reduce the species richness of herbaceous vegetation, with Stavi and Argaman (2016) adding that the topsoil removal degrades soil quality [ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Studies disagree, and what separates them is how the terrace is built and what is counted: hand-built stone bunds on cropland are credited with more crop diversity, while bulldozed earthen terraces on rangeland are linked to fewer wild herbaceous species [ev_biodiversity_outcome_wocat_6891_2023_plant_diversity, ev_biodiversity_outcome_stav20_9]. Neither side is a measured species or habitat comparison: the Bhutan unit is a compiler rating and the Israeli unit a cited suggestion in a review, and neither comes from the target low-income contexts. A measured biodiversity outcome on terraced land, with the construction method stated, is needed before a direction can be given.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces store carbon in the soil: a preprint meta-analysis of Chinese soil and water conservation measures finds terracing raised soil organic carbon by 27%, 17.94% and 26.62% in three Chinese regions, with increases of 14.11% to 60.96% in regional subsets 11 to 30 years after construction [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_5, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_6, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_7, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_9, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_11]. The compiler for gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan expects the expanding root system to increase below-ground soil organic matter and carbon [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The preprint sets the strength of this row: it has not been peer reviewed, it is from an upper-middle-income country, and its duration figures are the windows with obvious increases, overlapping the regional estimates [ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_8, ev_soil_organic_carbon_zhang26h2_10]. The WOCAT units are practitioner ratings, not measured carbon stocks; the Bhutan stone-bund sheet says organic matter falls at the upper part of the terrace and rises at the lower part, a redistribution within the field rather than a net removal [ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_6891_2023_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C, ev_soil_organic_carbon_wocat_7553_2025_soil_organic_matter_below_ground_C].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour ridges retain rainfall on slopes so part of it recharges groundwater: in Cameroon terraces would cause a groundwater recharge of 15 to 25% of rainfall, with drainage through rock fissures that could reach the piedmonts [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1], and hydrological modelling of contour ridges in Morocco, structures that promote the slow formation of terraces by sediment accumulation, estimates a 50% increase in recharge [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. Recharge is used here as a component of catchment water yield.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Recharge stands in for catchment yield; no unit measures flow leaving the catchment. The Cameroonian figure is a conditional estimate and the Moroccan figure a modelling result, both cited secondarily [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_willem21_1]. The Cameroonian source flags that the drainage could reach the unterraced piedmonts, a much more fragile environment [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_roose06_1]. On-slope supply evidence for terraces is in the terracing water stress row.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Pooled costs are establishment costs per hectare for terraces: in Ethiopia the initial investment cost of terracing was US$ 46.51 per hectare in the first year of construction, with about US$ 48.8 per hectare more to maintain over the first three years [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8]; the WOCAT sheet for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan gives 2000 USD per hectare (a total of 3200 USD spread over 1.6 ha) [ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment]; rehabilitating pre-Columbian terraces (andenes) in Peru, a heavy earth- and stone-moving intervention, cost USD 2,200 per hectare in a 1994 assessment [ev_project_cost_fao13c_1]; and a review tabulates terracing costs from China of 1918 to 4045 USD per hectare (mechanisation, labour and socioeconomic costs), rising with the original slope from 5 to 25 degrees [ev_project_cost_wei16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The spread is wide and reflects what is built: the Ethiopian figure is a first-year construction cost, the Uzbek figure is the compiler's own cost table converted with the sheet's exchange rate rather than a market price, the Peru figure is a rehabilitation cost cited second-hand, and the Chinese costs are a secondary table for mechanised terracing. The Peru and Chinese units come from upper-middle-income settings, so the value range rests on the Ethiopian and Uzbek units [ev_project_cost_adgo13_8, ev_project_cost_wocat_7553_2025_establishment, ev_project_cost_fao13c_1, ev_project_cost_wei16_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: When rainfall is erratic, stone bunds conserve more moisture in the soil and ease crop water stress during dry spells, and crops behind stone bunds in Burkina Faso could yield two to three times more than control plots in dry years [ev_soil_water_retention_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. Rwandan land-husbandry project households showed greater resilience than controls to the 2016 drought and recovered faster, and the WOCAT compiler for orchard terraces in Uzbekistan rates drought impacts as reduced, noting that more water is captured and infiltrated, making the land less susceptible to droughts [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. A terracing study citing De Graaff (2005) states that terracing reduces the risk of crop failure during dry spells in the rainy season through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Stone bunds in Burkina Faso gave no yield benefit in the driest year (1985) and so did not reduce famine risk then, which bounds the cited dry-year gain [ev_crop_yield_roose94_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. The Rwandan finding comes from a bundled package whose terrace share is unknown, and the Uzbek unit is a compiler rating rather than a measurement [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6, ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces capture and infiltrate more water so the land is less susceptible to drought, as the compiler for gradoni orchard terraces in Uzbekistan puts it [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts]. Adgo et al. cite Posthumus and De Graaff (2005), a Peruvian bench-terrace study, for terracing reducing the risk of crop failure during rainy-season dry spells through its water-conserving effect [ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13]. Households in a Rwandan land husbandry and water harvesting project proved more resilient than controls to the 2016 drought [ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The gain is slight and the evidence thin: the Uzbek unit is a practitioner judgement from a technology sheet, the Peruvian finding is a secondary citation about dry spells within the rainy season rather than a failed season, and the Rwanda result is an impact evaluation against controls reported second-hand in a completion report, without a magnitude or outcome metric and for a programme that bundles terracing with other land husbandry and water harvesting works [ev_drought_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_drought_impacts, ev_drought_hazard_adgo13_13, ev_drought_hazard_rwa18_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler-reported establishment cost of one 200m vetiver line forming progressive bench terraces in Haiti, from a single WOCAT technology sheet's cost table converted to USD with the sheet's exchange rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_establishment].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one compiler-reported figure for one structure type, not a market price or a measured project cost; a vetiver hedge line is a light, vegetative structure and is not representative of stone or earth terrace construction [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_establishment]. A second independent cost source is needed before the row can say whether terracing is cheap or costly to establish.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: On intensively tended terraces all crop residues are grazed off as soon as harvests end, so bush fires have little fuel, and the WOCAT compiler for bench terraces in Bangladesh rates fire risk as reduced [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The terrace statement is an expert estimate its authors say has no experimental basis on terraces, and the Bangladesh unit is a practitioner rating with no stated reasoning [ev_fire_hazard_roose06_1, ev_fire_hazard_wocat_4284_2018_fire_risk]. The effect depends on residues being removed by grazing.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and contour stone bunds slow and spread runoff on slopes: terraces lowered mean runoff and flood peaks on small mountain plots, stone bunds lower hillslope peak discharges and in high-rainfall years protect land from rapid flow in heavy rain, and a combined treatment in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment reduced flood runoff volume, clipped peaks and lengthened flood duration [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_2, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s]. Compacted hill terraces with retention walls in Uttarakhand, India are credited with mitigating flood and landslide impact, and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia and Uzbekistan rate flooding as reduced, the Tunisian compiler noting stone lines and walls reduce peak flows during heavy rainfall and the Uzbek compiler that more water is trapped in the catchment [ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Diversion banquettes and ditches, filed in this family, do the opposite: in Niger they raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion systems accelerate concentration time with serious gullying risk if the dikes break [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-level peak-flow evidence for terraces is scarce, the Tunisian result bundles rangeland closure and gully stone-filling with the bunds, the Uttarakhand claim is a Bank self-report, and the Tunisian and Uzbek units are compiler ratings [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts]. The studies disagree because they cover different structures: slope terraces and contour bunds that slow runoff in place, against diversion works that move it faster downslope.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, stone lines and contour stone bunds detain and spread runoff on slopes, lowering peak discharges and making flows last longer after rain; in a semi-arid Tunisian catchment a combined treatment cut the runoff volume of 71 single-peak floods by 50% [ev_flood_hazard_roose06_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s], and WOCAT compilers in Tunisia and Uzbekistan judge flooding reduced, the Tunisian stone-lines sheet citing lower peak flows during heavy rainfall [ev_flood_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_downstream_flooding, ev_flood_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_flood_impacts].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The studies disagree because they cover different structures: diversion banquettes in Niger raised peak discharges, and runoff-diversion dikes speed up concentration time and risk gullying if they break, so design decides the sign [ev_flood_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose94_3]. Catchment-scale evidence is scarce, with a review calling the terrace effect on peak flow uncertain; the Tunisian treatment also included rangeland closure, the Uttarakhand flood-mitigation claim is lender self-reported, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_flood_hazard_willem21_1, ev_flood_hazard_roose06_2_s, ev_flood_hazard_utk22_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone bunds raise yields, enlarge cultivable area and allow more diverse crops, reducing food shortfall. Household food security improves in proportion to the area of a farm improved with bunds [ev_food_security_zoug14_1], and beneficiaries of Rwanda's terracing project saw drastically improved food consumption scores against a comparison group [ev_food_security_rwa18_5]. The WOCAT compiler for contour stone bunds in Bhutan writes that the larger cultivable area ensured food self-sufficiency and that clearing stones from the soil lets land users grow diverse crops throughout the year [ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_food_security_selfsufficiency, ev_food_security_wocat_6891_2023_risk_of_production_failure]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, farmers recalled that before terracing the community was highly food insecure and migrated in search of food even in minor droughts, and that terraces improved crop production and reduced seasonal migration [ev_food_security_adgo13_11].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Gains are slow on degraded land: the compiler for vetiver-hedge terraces in Haiti records no change in food security yet, because on very degraded land users have to wait for the soil to recover, though food security is expected to increase in the long run [ev_food_security_wocat_3223_2017_food_security_selfsufficiency]. The Bhutan and Haiti units are practitioner ratings; the Rwandan evaluation gives no magnitude, and the bund statement is an author's assertion rather than a measured result [ev_food_security_rwa18_5, ev_food_security_zoug14_1]. The Anjene account rests on farmer recall and group discussions rather than a measured comparison [ev_food_security_adgo13_11].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces, fanya juu and contour stone bunds or lines level slopes and slow runoff so more water and soil stay on the field; yields of maize, barley, millet and sorghum rose on terraced or bunded land, especially in dry years. Stone bunds raised sorghum yields by 33% to 55% in Burkina Faso and by about 142% with compost, and millet yields in Niger rose by more than 40% up to 15 years after the bunds were built [ev_crop_yield_zoug14_2, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_1_s]. WOCAT compilers add that stone lines in Tunisia protect farmland from degradation and contour stone bunds in Bhutan enlarge the cultivable area as stones are removed [ev_crop_yield_wocat_6610_2022_crop_production, ev_crop_yield_wocat_6891_2023_crop_production]. Meta-analyses support the gain: a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds a 48% yield increase for terraces, an Ethiopian synthesis a mean gain of 322 kg per hectare for stone bunds with soil total nitrogen up from 0.16 to 0.20%, and a terracing meta-analysis finds biomass on terraces about 1.94 times that on slopes [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1], and 2 to 4-year old bench terraces in Peru gave 20% greater yields than adjacent sloping fields [ev_crop_yield_wei16_4]; reviewed studies also report maize yields up nearly 50% on fanya juu terraces in semi-arid Kenya, wheat yields 6–7 times higher on stone-wall terraces than on slopes under the same input costs, and land productivity over 19% higher on bench terraces [ev_crop_yield_tefe24_5, ev_crop_yield_adim16_1, ev_soil_nitrogen_adim16_1, ev_crop_yield_ngur26_4, ev_crop_yield_wei16_3, ev_agricultural_production_value_wei16_1]. In Burkina Faso, crop yields in years of average rainfall rose by 63–74 per cent on farms using rock bunds [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2]. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. New primaries from Ethiopia add measured contrasts: terraced fields in the Anjene catchment gave 0.95, 1.86 and 1.73 t of teff, barley and maize per hectare against 0.49, 0.61 and 0.77 t on un-terraced farms, and improved water productivity by at least 100% [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_2, ev_crop_yield_adgo13_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]; plot-level econometrics found a yield premium for conserved plots in low-rainfall Tigray of ETB 412 or 299 per hectare depending on the estimator, and robust impacts of all the soil and water conservation technologies studied on crop output in low-rainfall areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_1, ev_agricultural_production_value_kato11_1]. Bunds also steady output: soil bunds reduced production risk in low-rainfall areas, stone bunds did so when combined with inorganic fertilizer, and all the technologies studied reduced risk in high-rainfall areas [ev_yield_stability_kato11_3, ev_yield_stability_kato11_7, ev_yield_stability_kato11_5]. Reviews cite sorghum straw and grain yields doubled on plots with stone lines in Burkina Faso (Zougmore et al., 2000; Zougmoré et al., 2003) and stone bunds and terraces raising crop yield in Ethiopia by up to 53% (Nyssen et al., 2007; Gebremichael et al., 2005), with a survey in Dogu'a Tembien giving 0.65 t per hectare after physical conservation against 0.58 before (Nyssen et al., 2007) [ev_crop_yield_biaz12_13, ev_crop_yield_dile13_4, ev_crop_yield_gebr18_2, ev_crop_yield_gebr18_12].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Some literature figures are lender self-reports (Rwanda before/after yields, Indian with/without models bundled with crop packages); the Rwanda value-of-harvest gain is from an independent DIME evaluation, and the Burkina Faso and Niger gains are cited from earlier studies, the largest bundled with compost [ev_crop_yield_rwa18_7, ev_crop_yield_utk22_8, ev_agricultural_production_value_rwa18_3, ev_crop_yield_zoug14_4]. Diversion banquettes in Niger reduced yields, progressive terraces on poor soils in Rwanda gave no yield increase, bench terraces need heavy fertility restoration before yields rise, and a Haitian compiler notes that on very degraded land farmers must wait for the soil to recover [ev_crop_yield_heusch95_1, ev_crop_yield_roose06_3, ev_crop_yield_roose94_4, ev_crop_yield_wocat_3223_2017_crop_production]. The Tunisian, Bhutanese and Haitian units are practitioner ratings from WOCAT sheets rather than measurements. Stone bunds in semi-arid Tanzania reduced maize yield by 13% [ev_crop_yield_adim16_9], and in Algeria farmers lost 5 to 15% of their cropped area to banquettes without seeing yields improve, legume yields between banquettes showed no significant gain, and a Moroccan farmer saw no yield improvement between banquettes imposed by technicians [ev_crop_yield_arab04_1, ev_crop_yield_arab04_2, ev_crop_yield_roos10_2]. The terracing meta-analysis pools unweighted ratios and some of the largest multiples are single studies cited in reviews [ev_crop_yield_wei16_1, ev_crop_yield_wei16_3]. The Burkina Faso rock-bund gain is for years the authors call average rainfall, with compost on the bunded fields [ev_crop_yield_sawa11h1_2]. That is a compiler judgement for a group spanning earth bunds, stone lines, vegetative strips and fanya juu terraces, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The same Ethiopian studies show the limit in wetter highlands: in high-rainfall Amhara conserved plots showed no significant yield difference, the point estimate lying ETB 179 or 145 per hectare below non-conserved plots, and only waterways and trees had robust impacts on output in high-rainfall areas [ev_agricultural_production_value_kass08_2, ev_agricultural_production_value_kato11_2]. Earlier studies found fanya juu, soil and stone bunds and grass strips did not increase crop yield and biomass in the highlands of Ethiopia and Eritrea (Herweg and Ludi, 1999; Kassie et al., 2008) [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_12]. Stone bunds alone had no independent risk-reducing effect in low-rainfall areas, and soil bunds raised production risk in Tigray, the driest region studied [ev_yield_stability_kato11_4, ev_yield_stability_kato11_6]. Rodents sheltering in narrowly spaced stone bunds can damage up to 225 kg of crop per hectare (Meheretu et al., 2014) [ev_crop_yield_gebr18_4]. The Anjene terraces have been maintained for decades and farmers there also apply fertiliser on cereals, so the gap is not the structures alone [ev_crop_yield_adgo13_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: The only unit is the compiler-reported annual maintenance cost of one 200m vetiver line forming progressive bench terraces in Haiti, from a single WOCAT sheet's cost table converted to USD at the sheet's exchange rate [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_maintenance].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: This row is data deficient: one compiler-reported figure for one vegetative structure type, from the sheet's own cost table rather than a market price or a measured project cost, and not representative of stone or earth terrace upkeep [ev_project_cost_wocat_3223_2017_maintenance]. A second independent cost source is needed before the row can say whether terrace upkeep is cheap or costly.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing raises yields and enables higher-value crops on former hillsides, which drives modelled returns per hectare above cost; terrace investments are judged to pay off over long lifetimes, mainly where they carry high-value crops such as vegetables [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_economic_return_willem21_1, ev_economic_return_fao13c_1]. WOCAT compilers report income from diverse crops behind contour stone bunds in Bhutan [ev_household_income_wocat_6891_2023_farm_income]. An Ethiopian synthesis reports net present values of 3486.2 Birr per hectare for stone bunds, 2794.0 for bench terraces and 5283.4 for level fanya juu [ev_economic_return_adim16_1, ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_economic_return_adim16_3], and modelled bench-terrace gains in Peru could raise per capita incomes by up to 15% [ev_household_income_wei16_1]. A review cites soil and water conservation measures, including level bunds and fanya juu terraces, boosting farmer income by increasing soil fertility, yield and water [ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. Field data from Ethiopia's Anjene catchment now measure the gain directly: teff, barley and maize grown on terraces earned an incremental income advantage of US$ 159, 275 and 141 per hectare per year over un-terraced farms, and at a 10% discount rate the average net present value of terrace investment for barley over 50 years was US$ 1542, and net present values were above zero across the catchment [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4, ev_economic_return_adgo13_5, ev_economic_return_adgo13_6, ev_economic_return_adgo13_10]. A review cites stone bunds giving a return rate of 50% in terms of farm profit (Gebremedhin et al., 1999) [ev_economic_return_gebr18_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Several of the literature returns are lender crop-budget models for Rwanda and India [ev_economic_return_rwa18_8, ev_household_income_utk22_9]. Not every return is large: banquette profitability in Niger was of the order of 1% [ev_economic_return_heusch95_1]. The Ethiopian net present values are unweighted means from a small set of studies, the Peruvian income gain is a modelled potential cited in a review, and the Ethiopian income claim is cited from a study the citing review itself describes as methodologically weak [ev_economic_return_adim16_2, ev_household_income_wei16_1, ev_household_income_tade23h1_1]. Income and returns are proxies for poverty. The Anjene income figures exclude family labour and come from terraces that the community has maintained for decades, so they show what long-lived, maintained terraces return rather than the first years after building [ev_economic_return_adgo13_4]; the stone-bund return rate is cited second-hand [ev_economic_return_gebr18_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Bench and progressive terraces, contour stone bunds and lines and banquettes shorten slope length and slow runoff, so soil losses on steep plots fall sharply and sediment loads drop where terracing is widespread. Terraces cut soil losses on small mountain plots on 20 to 60% slopes from more than 200 to under 2 t/ha a year, a contour banquette in Niger divided erosion by 150 against traditional cropping, and stone bunds with compost cut total soil loss by 79% [ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_zoug14_1]. WOCAT compilers for bench terraces in Thailand, contour stone bunds in Bhutan and Gradoni terraces in Uzbekistan rate soil loss or runoff as reduced, the Uzbek compiler noting that soil eroded from the inter-spaces is trapped by the terraces [ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_4281_2018_surface_runoff, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_6891_2023_soil_loss, ev_erosion_hazard_wocat_7553_2025_soil_loss, ev_runoff_reduction_wocat_7553_2025_surface_runoff]. Meta-analyses agree: a terracing meta-analysis finds erosion control on terraces 11.46 times that of controls and runoff reduction 2.6 times [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_1], a meta-analysis of traditional in-situ water harvesting finds terraces cut soil loss by 60.21% and runoff by 56.5%, and an Ethiopian synthesis reports stone bunds cutting soil loss by 38% and runoff by 34.4% [ev_erosion_hazard_tefe24_5, ev_runoff_reduction_tefe24_3, ev_erosion_hazard_adim16_3, ev_runoff_reduction_adim16_3]. Reviews also report terracing reducing runoff by 92.6% and 80% in sub-humid and humid regions, stone lines and terraces reducing runoff and erosion by 30 to 50%, sediment accumulating behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, and fanya juu trapping 64% of sediment, rising to 80% with vetiver grass [ev_runoff_reduction_wei16_2, ev_runoff_reduction_roos10_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6]. Reviews add further cited contrasts: runoff and erosion in non-terraced catchments 2.7 and 15.3 times higher than in terraced ones under the same cultivation (Lal, 1982), stone-terraced hillslopes reducing runoff by 65–85% and soil erosion by 58–69% (Al-Seekh and Mohammad, 2009), stone bunds reducing soil erosion by 68% (Nyssen et al., 2007), soil loss in Dogu'a Tembien falling from 57 to 20 t per hectare a year after physical conservation (Gebremichael et al., 2005), and modelled net erosion of 25.04 t per hectare a year on terrace farmland against 28.97 on slope farmland in China's Dingjiagou catchment (Zhang and Li, 2014) [ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_1, ev_runoff_reduction_stav20_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_1, ev_erosion_hazard_gebr18_13, ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3]. A review of farming terraces explains why: terraces increase infiltration rates, reduce sediment transport and interrupt the flows that feed runoff contribution areas and peak discharges [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_4, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: Alignment decides the sign: diversion banquettes in Niger doubled runoff coefficients and increased gully erosion, while contour banquettes in the same region cut erosion; ditches with downslope banks cause rill erosion, many Maghreb banquettes were erased or unmaintained, and abandoned terraces increase erosion [ev_runoff_reduction_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_1, ev_erosion_hazard_heusch95_2_s, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_3, ev_erosion_hazard_roose06_4, ev_erosion_hazard_willem21_2]. The Rwanda sediment reductions are lender-monitored before/after figures without a control, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements rather than measurements [ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_1_s, ev_erosion_hazard_rwa18_2]. Bench terracing alone reduced runoff by only 9% in a small USA watershed, gullied area on Tunisian banquette land grew by 12% between 1963 and 1973, poorly maintained Algerian banquettes accelerate erosion, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on downstream dam sedimentation [ev_runoff_reduction_meko14_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_1, ev_erosion_hazard_arab04_2, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The meta-analytic ratios are unweighted, and the Ethiopian stone-bund sediment figure comes with a total soil loss of 77 t per hectare, so bunds trap most but not all eroded soil [ev_erosion_hazard_wei16_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1]. Construction can also cause harm: in cropland fields, excessive removal of stones to build terraces has been linked to a threefold increase in sheet and rill erosion (Nyssen et al., 2007, cited by Stavi et al.) [ev_erosion_hazard_stav20_3]. Terraces do not hold everything: the review puts the delivery ratio at approximately 20%–30% for sediment and 50%–60% for runoff, and in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel; in a Spanish catchment, terrace maintenance slowed runoff only for events with a return period shorter than 8–10 years (Bellin et al., 2009) [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6, ev_runoff_reduction_arna15_5]. The Dingjiagou difference is modelled and small, and the review contrasts are cited second-hand [ev_erosion_hazard_arna15_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terracing and retaining walls hold soil on slopes, which an evaluation in Morocco expects to reduce siltation of downstream rivers and dam storage [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. Reviews add that sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]. A terracing review finds terraces reasonably effective at reducing sediment transport, though about 20%–30% of sediment may still be delivered [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Morocco unit is an evaluator assertion; nothing on water chemistry is measured, and siltation is a component proxy [ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. The added sediment figures are secondary citations in reviews, in extreme rainfall the sediment accumulated on terraces can reach the channel [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6], the bench-terrace figure comes from a high-income watershed, and Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5, ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Terraces and stone lines capture and retain rainwater on slopes, and stone lines contribute to increased infiltration of rainwater into the soil, thereby replenishing water resources [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability]. Measured soil moisture supports this: a meta-analysis gives terraces an SMD of 40.5% for soil moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6], a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. The FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. In Ethiopia's Anjene catchment, terraces improved the water productivity of teff, barley and maize by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7]. A review of farming terraces notes that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that a very flat terrace bed lets rain pond, reducing runoff and increasing infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The Tunisian stone-line units are practitioner judgements, and catchment modelling in Peru found no difference in crop water distribution with partial terracing [ev_water_regulation_willem21_1]. Abandoned or degraded terraces worsen water regulation [ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The recharge estimates for terraces and contour ridges now sit in the terracing catchment water yield row. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases from mixed-income countries [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1], and the Chinese finding comes from an independent World Bank evaluation reporting project monitoring with no control [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. That is a compiler judgement for a group spanning earth bunds, stone lines, vegetative strips and fanya juu terraces, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The same review cites work finding that the infiltration capacity of the soil is not particularly affected by terracing (Posthumus and Stroosnijder, 2010), so the gain comes from water held longer on the flat bed rather than a change in the soil [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. The Anjene figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also use fertiliser [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: Stone bunds hold runoff in the field, and in wet years this can waterlog parts of the field and harm crop production; millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: The harm is confined to wet years or very wet months and neither unit gives a magnitude or the share of the field affected; both are cited statements from Burkina Faso rather than measurements, so they mark a risk to watch where stone bunds are placed on soils or in seasons that already hold excess water [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for radical terraces in Rwanda, vetiver bench terraces in Haiti and stone lines in Tunisia rate the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_1553_2012_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms, ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_6610_2022_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_har.conditionality: All units are compiler ratings concerning rain-storm damage rather than wind, and the Haiti compiler says the impact is not yet measured [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_3223_2017_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Check dams, gabions, fascines, terraces and bunds trap sediment that would otherwise reach streams, canals and reservoirs, lowering catchment sediment export and downstream siltation [ev_sediment_retention_fran21_1, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_3]. WOCAT compilers describe gabion walls and check dams in Somalia trapping sediment upstream so less travels downstream, and a masonry check dam in Ethiopia holding back visible siltation [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_7778_2026_downstream_siltation, ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation]. Measured retention now spans scales: check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, studies cited by Shi et al. report check dams cutting sediment by 79.4%–85.5% in the Yanhe watershed and the sediment load by 51.9% in the Huangfuchuan catchment, and a watershed model attributes an 11.7% sediment reduction to the main check dams [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2]; loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1]; sediment accumulates behind Ethiopian stone bunds at 59 t per hectare a year, fanya juu trapped 64% of sediment (80% with vetiver grass), and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_6, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5]; and small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3]. Holding soil also holds nutrients: an Ethiopian synthesis finds graded soil bunds reduced total nitrogen lost in runoff and sediment by up to 48% [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result. The in-field row holds the strongest result, strong, but it rests on the Ethiopian graded-bund nitrogen synthesis [ev_nutrient_removal_adim16_1]. The rows that carry the measured trapping studies — check dams and ponds (runoff catchment) and terraces and bunds (terracing) — hold moderate, and the cross-family row, a single modelled Chinese programme figure, holds slight [ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5]. The vote gives moderate, below the pooled strong. Water quality is inferred almost entirely from sediment retention, a component proxy, plus nutrient losses in runoff from a single synthesis; nothing on water chemistry downstream is measured, and the WOCAT units are practitioner ratings of downstream siltation. Retention is partial: a terracing review puts the delivery ratio at about 20%–30% for sediment, and in extreme rainfall the sediment held on terraces can reach the channel [ev_sediment_retention_arna15_6]. Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of a downstream dam over 1947-1968, and the twofold decline in outlet sediment yield with USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Much of the literature is secondary citations in reviews, several from high-income settings (USA, Germany, Belgium), the China programme figure and the Loess Plateau watershed results are modelled [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7], and gabions in Morocco have filled and need raising [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_iegchn07_5, ev_sediment_retention_iegmar09_1]. The Ethiopian compiler notes the trapped sediment has not been quantified [ev_sediment_retention_wocat_6716_2023_downstream_siltation].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In semi-arid catchments check dams on China's Loess Plateau are credited with cutting regional sediment export by about 85% and accounted for 37.2% to 72.2% of sediment reduction at the outlets of five catchments over 26 years, and loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The USA check dams produced a twofold decline in outlet sediment per unit of peak runoff, but this was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, the Chinese figures are secondary citations in reviews, and the USA site is high-income rangeland rather than smallholder farmland [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: In high-income settings loose-rock check dams on semi-arid USA rangeland retained 48.4% and 82.4% of watershed sediment yield, small ponds trapped 54-85% of incoming sediment over 8 years in southern Germany and 68% over the long term in Belgium, and bench terracing cut sediment yield by 58% in a small USA watershed [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_3, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_5].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: The twofold decline in outlet sediment by the USA check dams was significant only at α = 0.2 [ev_sediment_retention_poly14_2]. Sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality, most figures are secondary citations in a review, and rangeland and arable-field ponds in high-income countries transfer only loosely to smallholder water harvesting [ev_sediment_retention_meko14_2].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.mechanism: Check dams trap sediment before it reaches rivers and reservoirs: on China's Loess Plateau a check-dam campaign to retain floodwater and intercept soil sediments is credited with reducing sediment by about 85%, and at the outlets of five Chinese catchments check dams accounted for sediment reductions of 37.2% to 72.2% over 26 years compared with other soil and water conservation measures [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4]. Further Loess Plateau studies agree: check dams in the Yanhe watershed cut sediment by 79.4%–85.5% (Xu et al. 2013), a sediment delivery model credits check dams with removing 51.9% of the Huangfuchuan sediment load (Zhao et al. 2017), and a watershed model found the main check dams cut sediment by 11.7% [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_8, ev_sediment_retention_shi19_2].
