water_harvesting_conservation__water_qua.conditionality: Not every work cuts downstream sediment: Algerian banquettes had no influence on the sedimentation rate of the Oued Fodda dam over 1947-1968 [ev_sediment_retention_arab04_1]. The Chinese figures are secondary citations in reviews, sediment retention is a component proxy for water quality with no water chemistry measured, and the row covers upper-middle-income settings only [ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1, ev_sediment_retention_meko14_4]. The added figures are model results or citations in a single check-dam study, and the Yanhe figure may restate work behind the Loess Plateau review figure [ev_sediment_retention_shi19_7, ev_sediment_retention_luca21_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Bunds, stone lines, micro-basins and check dams capture and retain rainwater so that it infiltrates, and compilers and local people report raised well levels; sand dams and subsurface dams store water that extends the months of water access or backs up wells when other sources dry up, production cisterns keep livestock watered, and participating villages in India reduced water transport by tanker. WOCAT compilers for the Vallerani system in Burkina Faso, a sand dam in Kenya, a farm pond in Cambodia, stone lines in Tunisia and haffir and gabion works in Somalia judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1537_2012_harvesting_collection_of_water, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_2844_2017_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_6610_2022_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7777_2026_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_quantity]. In Zimbabwe the months per year water could be collected at sand-dam sites rose from 6.5 to 10.9 after construction, and from 5.8 to 9.7 in a drought year, while in Kenya the average distance to a water source fell from 3 to 1 km [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2, ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_1, ev_water_access_deficit_lasage08_1]. A check-dam review reports that check dams storing seasonal runoff solve local supply scarcity; traditional rainwater ponds in South Korea reduced the occurrence of water deficit from 30 to 20% [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. In India, discharge of springs and streams rose in treated watersheds: a sample study in Himachal Pradesh reports a 40 percent increase in water discharge in spring and stream sources [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1], and the Uttarakhand project achieved an average 21 percent increase in water discharge from perennial water sources in sampled micro-watersheds, against a target of 25 percent [ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. Measured soil moisture adds a field-level route: capture structures hold rain in the root zone. A meta-analysis of in-situ practices finds they improve soil moisture retention by 59%, with infiltration pits highest at an SMD of 114.4%, soil/stone bunds 76.4%, tied ridging 48.9% and terraces 40.5% [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_1, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_2, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_3, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_5, ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_6]; a global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at conserving soil water, with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]; and conversion of slopeland to leveled fields in China increased moisture retention [ev_soil_water_retention_iegchn07_2]. In Burkina Faso, zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9], and in Ethiopia hand-dug planting basins held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at flowering and maturity [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_6]. Mulching, the soil-cover form of in-situ water harvesting, improves soil moisture retention with an SMD of 54.0% in the meta-analysis, and maize-stalk mulch in Ethiopia held more topsoil water than unmulched plots at Ziway at all three stages [ev_soil_water_retention_tefe24_4, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_1, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_3, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_5]. Indian project watersheds showed an increase in soil moisture content by 30.5 percent compared to the IWMP sites [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2]. Water productivity, the grain produced per unit of rain, is a route by which capture eases water stress. Grain per unit of rain rises with capture in a set of East and Southern African trials: the best conservation-farming practice per site gave yield increases ranging from 20 to 120% over conventional tillage whilst rain water productivity improved with 10–50% [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. In an on-farm trial at Houndé, Burkina Faso, stone rows with zaï pits, every arm also receiving manure, lifted maize rain water productivity from 3.10 kg per hectare per mm under the farmers' practice of oxen ploughing with NPK and urea to 6.61 [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. A review reports that contour tied-ridging in eastern Sudan gave the highest water use efficiency of the treatments compared [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. The water-productivity evidence points the same way: FAO compilers list improved water use efficiency among the main benefits of rainwater harvesting, the WOCAT guideline authors find that all water harvesting groups indicate improved water use efficiency, mostly high to medium, through reduced evaporation loss and better soil water availability, and a review sentence, citing earlier work, says capture approaches often lead also to higher water productivity because denser canopies shade the soil [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. FAO compilers rate improving water productivity for the cross-slope barrier group at the middle mark of their scale [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. Trials and reviews add to the soil-moisture route: micro-catchments in Ethiopia raised mean soil moisture by 31% in the wet season and 24% in the dry season (cited in a review), tied ridging, open ridging and sub-soiling raised root-zone water by 24%, 15% and 3% over traditional tillage in drought-stricken Wollo (McHugh et al. 2007), tied ridges in northern Ethiopia cut runoff by about 60% and raised rooting-zone water by at least 13% (Araya and Stroosnijder 2010), terraces stay humid longer than sloping fields (Posthumus and Stroosnijder 2010), and 20–25 cm deep contour furrows in Iran raised soil moisture and shrub productivity (Jahantigh and Pessarakli 2009) [ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_6, ev_soil_moisture_dile13_1, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_8, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7, ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6]. On water productivity, terraces in Ethiopia improved the water productivity of three crops by at least 100% against un-terraced plots [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7], tied ridging with a wood-shavings mulch raised rainfall water-use efficiency of sorghum in Nigeria [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9], and supplemental irrigation from a Kenyan runoff dam with fertiliser raised rain and irrigation water-use efficiency from 2.1 to 4.1 kg of grain per mm per hectare [ev_rain_water_productivity_barr05_9]; supplementary irrigation in semi-arid Zimbabwe raised water productivity from 1.75 to 2.3 kg per cubic metre (Kahinda et al. 2007) [ev_rain_water_productivity_dile13_6, ev_rain_water_productivity_biaz12_5]. In Burkina Faso, water-harvesting reservoirs are used for livestock and household needs during periods of domestic water scarcity [ev_water_access_deficit_foxr03_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The class follows the sub-practice vote, not the pooled result: the storage and cross-family rows hold strong results and the in-field, micro-catchment and terracing rows moderate ones, so the roll-up is moderate rather than the pooled strong. Most literature units are narrative, perception or lender-reported, the pooled percentages mix spring-discharge, water-deficit and tanker-use metrics, and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets rather than measurements [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1528_2012_water_quantity, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_7778_2026_water_availability]. Groundwater-recharge evidence, with its limits, now sits in the catchment water yield rows. Many sand dams cannot supply a household through the dry season [ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3]. The Zimbabwean sand-dam figures rely on recall of conditions before construction [ev_water_access_deficit_lazurko24_2]. The check-dam and pond findings are secondary citations in reviews, and the Korean result is modelled in a high-income setting [ev_water_access_deficit_silv26_1]. The Indian spring and stream discharge figures come from World Bank completion reports, the lender's own evaluation, measured before and after without untreated comparison sites, for catchment treatment that bundles plantations, trenches, ponds and check dams with water-harvesting structures, so the gain cannot be credited to water harvesting alone [ev_water_regulation_hp17_1, ev_water_regulation_utk22_6]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The measured soil-moisture evidence has its own limits. Tillage alone is not water harvesting: in the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone, scored as high as the tied furrows, so that treatment does not speak for the practice [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. The Ethiopian basins did not differ from unmulched plots at planting at Ziway or at any stage at Melkassa [ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_2, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_8, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_10, ev_soil_water_retention_sime15h2_12]. Under meteorological drought and dry spells in Kenya, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient in soil moisture conservation since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]: structures store rain, they cannot make it. A review found no significant effect of infiltration trenches on soil moisture because only four studies provided sufficient statistical data [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1]. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8], the Indian watershed comparison is a project-commissioned study of a package of soil and water conservation structures [ev_soil_water_retention_kar20_2], and the Brazilian tied-furrow trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. Soil moisture is read as a component of water stress, not water stress itself. Those best-practice arms are bundled: planting pits, basins or ripper-with-ridging (the capture element, which is the practice here) come with reduced tillage and mostly with fertiliser, and tillage alone is not water harvesting [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_1]. The trial-level readings are weaker: the authors find no clear tillage effect on rain water productivity in Kenya, no clear effects of tillage in Ethiopia (where the gains that do show come with fertilised treatments), and only a tendency of improvement in semi-arid Tanzania [ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_5, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock09_4]. The Burkina Faso trial covers a single season, and every conservation arm also received manure, so its gain belongs to the package rather than to the structures alone [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_1]. At Houndé, grass strips with zaï (4.84 against 3.10) were not significantly different from the control, and at Péni neither grass strips with zaï (4.51) nor earth bunds with contour ploughing (4.31) differed significantly from the control (3.53), the authors stating that water was not limiting at Péni, which had more rain than Houndé that season [ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_2, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_3, ev_rain_water_productivity_koro17_4]. The Sudan comparison ranks treatments without a no-practice value [ev_rain_water_productivity_ngur26_3]. These are compiler and author judgements across groups, direction only, and the review sentence is second-hand; the WOCAT authors also note that some case studies indicate little to no improvement in water use efficiency [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_wocwh13_1, ev_rain_water_productivity_rock10_1]. The FAO cross-slope barrier mark is a compiler judgement, direction only [ev_rain_water_productivity_faoslm11_3]. The water-productivity and moisture gains are not universal: ridging without a mulch did not consistently raise water-use efficiency in Nigeria, overall rain-plus-irrigation water-use efficiency did not rise with supplemental irrigation in Burkina Faso, and Nigerian ridges stored a few per cent more soil water each year but significantly so on only a single measurement date out of nine [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_8, ev_rain_water_productivity_foxr03_6, ev_soil_moisture_chir06_7]. The Nigerian water-use gain is bundled with mulch, and most of the Ethiopian, Iranian and terrace moisture figures are cited second-hand [ev_rain_water_productivity_chir06_9, ev_soil_moisture_biaz12_1].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terraces hold rainfall on the slope so more of it reaches the crop: in the Ethiopian highlands, fanya juu terraces improved the water productivity of the three crops studied (teff, barley and maize) by at least 100% over un-terraced plots, which the authors read as clear evidence of more efficient use of rainwater [ev_rain_water_productivity_adgo13_7].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The gain depends on there being rain to hold. In a Kenyan trial, tied ridging without organic inputs was insufficient for soil moisture conservation during meteorological drought and dry spells, since there was little or no rainwater to be held in the basins [ev_soil_water_retention_ndun23_1]. The Ethiopian figure compares long-maintained terraces with un-terraced plots at a single catchment where farmers also apply fertiliser, and the Kenyan result is for tied ridges rather than terraces, so the row rests on few sites and differing practices.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Storage and recharge structures ease water stress in semi-arid areas: production cisterns in semi-arid Brazil keep livestock watered while clay tanks are dry, an agency review credits consumption and production cisterns with a large drop in rural establishments without any water source, and subsurface dams raise water levels in existing wells used when other sources dry up [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. In the field, pits and furrows keep rain in the root zone: in Burkina Faso zaï of 30–40 cm diameter and 1-m half-moons retained moisture for 2-3 weeks through dry spells, and zaï can retain moisture in the soil for seven to ten days after rainfall; in semi-arid Brazil tied furrows kept more soil moisture than the traditional flat system at all crop stages and depths [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8, ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Supply is bounded by storage: 57% of Kenyan sand dams would hold 4 months of water for their reported beneficiaries [ev_water_access_deficit_neuf17_1]. The Brazilian units are implementer or agency assessments, interviews or census inference from an upper-middle-income context rather than the low-income target [ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5]. Well-level evidence for semi-arid bunds and zaï now sits in the catchment water yield rows. What upstream capture does to water downstream is a separate question, answered in the catchment water yield rows. The zaï and half-moon results come with compost in the pits, so the moisture gain cannot be credited to the pit alone [ev_soil_water_retention_zour25h1_7, ev_soil_water_retention_sawa11h1_8]. In the Brazilian trial deep ploughing, which is tillage alone and not a capture structure, scored as high as the tied furrows, and the trial ran a single season at a station of the agency that promotes the technology [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, pits, bunds, terraces and check dams increase infiltration and groundwater recharge, raising well levels and spring discharge, and sand dams store water that extends the months of water access. WOCAT compilers for jessour, spate and water-spreading systems, bunds, terraces, check dams, sand dams, ponds and haffirs from Tunisia, Niger, Ethiopia, Kenya, India, Somalia and elsewhere judge them to improve water harvesting, water quantity or water availability.
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Many literature units are lender-reported or community perceptions and the WOCAT units are practitioner judgements from technology sheets; compilers judge no change in water availability for water spreading in Sudan and semi-circular bunds in Niger [ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1292_2015_water_availability, ev_water_access_deficit_wocat_1614_2014_water_availability]. Groundwater gains in India could be wiped out by increased pumping, year-round wells did not increase in Burkina Faso, and many Kenyan sand dams lack capacity to supply even one household through the dry season [ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_iegind11_4, ev_groundwater_recharge_potential_kabo04_2, ev_water_access_deficit_ritc21_3].

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: Terraces and check dams hold water where it is needed. A global terracing synthesis finds terraced sites more efficient than slopes at reducing runoff and conserving soil water (e.g., soil moisture recharge), with a mean δsm of 1.2 [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. A terracing review cites Posthumus and Stroosnijder (2010) finding that the soil stays humid for longer on terraces than on sloping fields, and that ponding on very flat terrace beds increases infiltration [ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7], and a check-dam review reports that check dams that store seasonal runoff solve local scarcity in supply [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: Both sources pool cases from high- and lower-income countries, so the cell does not isolate the low-income target [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1, ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1]. The terracing ratio is an unweighted mean across extracted cases, and soil moisture is read as a component of water stress rather than water stress itself [ev_soil_water_retention_wei16_1]. The check-dam and terrace-moisture findings are secondary citations within reviews, and the same terrace study reports infiltration capacity itself not particularly affected by terracing [ev_water_access_deficit_luca21_1, ev_soil_moisture_arna15_7]. What upstream capture does to water downstream is answered in the catchment water yield rows.

water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.mechanism: In semi-arid Brazil, stored rain covers gaps in supply: a production cistern keeps animals drinking while a family's clay tanks are dry and lets it manage an intermittent piped supply, subsurface dams raise the water level in wells that families draw on mainly when other sources dry up, and more than 1 million cisterns are credited with cutting the number of rural establishments without any water source [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1]. In the field, deep ploughing and tied furrows kept soil moisture higher than traditional flat planting at every crop stage and depth [ev_soil_water_retention_brito07_9]. In Iran's Sistan-Baluchistan rangelands, 20–25 cm deep contour furrows raised soil moisture and the productivity of shrubs (Jahantigh and Pessarakli 2009, cited in a review) [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__water_str.conditionality: The benefit is real but its size is not stated, hence the slight class. The cistern evidence is an interview account and a census-based inference with no counterfactual, and the subsurface-dam supply is intermittent [ev_water_access_deficit_arsky20_5, ev_water_access_deficit_castro22_1, ev_water_access_deficit_cirilo03_1]. Catchment and soil effects are weak or unproven: a trench review found no significant effect on soil moisture because only four studies gave enough data, terracing 20% of cropland made no difference in a Peruvian catchment model, and abandoned or degraded terraces can harm water regulation [ev_soil_water_retention_locat20_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_1, ev_water_regulation_willem21_2]. The Iranian furrow finding is second-hand, gives no magnitude and concerns rangeland shrubs rather than crops [ev_soil_moisture_stav20_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water on the cropped field backfire in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In southern Africa an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. Biazin et al. cite Jensen et al. (2003) from Tanzania: tied ridges helped maize in years of near-normal (500–600 mm) rainfall, but in wet years (700–900 mm) the maize showed waterlogging effects [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit in the row points the same way, so the practice is rated as worsening waterlogging, but none states how large the loss is or what share of a field is affected, so the strength is not quantified. The harm is tied to wet years, high-rainfall zones or sub-humid sites: it comes from using in-field water-holding practices (pits, basins, mulch, ridges, stone bunds) outside their rainfall window, and says nothing about storage or diversion structures, which have no waterlogging evidence left in this row. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, and the Burkina Faso statements and the Tanzanian tied-ridge result are cited from earlier studies [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15]. The Ethiopian finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the sub-humid conclusion covers conservation agriculture bundled with reduced tillage [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8, ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6]. The Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Kenyan losses are held out of the production classes as performance caveats and counted here as waterlogging evidence.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In low and lower-middle-income settings, stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and sorghum in zaï pits in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields; WOCAT compilers for pits and stone lines in Niger and conservation tillage in Kenya also rate drainage of excess water as worse [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1100_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_940_2010_excess_water_drainage]. Compilers for check dams in Nepal and India, bench terraces in Yemen, water-spreading weirs and check dams in Ethiopia, ripper tillage in Zambia and composted planting pits in Burkina Faso rate drainage as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1493_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5210_2019_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_959_2010_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Harm appears in wet years or high-rainfall zones and is not quantified, and the units that report it are cited statements or an unpublished observation, while the opposing units are practitioner ratings; the Indian farm-pond sheet rates drainage as unchanged [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1474_2011_excess_water_drainage]. The direction depends on whether a practice ponds water in the field or channels it away.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: WOCAT compilers for the rehabilitation of ancient terraces in Peru, reinforced stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde and marab floodplain agriculture in Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: All units are practitioner ratings with no measurement; the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage as worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Under rainfed cropping the harm comes where water is held on the cropped field in wet conditions: in wet years stone bunds in Burkina Faso may cause waterlogging in some parts of the field, millet production can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the Sudanian zone of Cameroon, where rainfall exceeds 80 mm per day and 1 200 mm per year, sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields because of frequent soil waterlogging and the risk of nutrient leaching [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In southern Africa, an FAO study shows by a water-balance calculation that planting basins can depress yields when too much water concentrates in them under high rainfall or in seasons with abnormally high rainfall, citing extension reports and farmer testimony of farmers scooping water from the basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8], and concludes that in sub-humid environments yields could be affected by water-logging in years with adequate rainfall [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. Tied ridges behave the same way: in Tanzania they benefited maize in years of near-normal rainfall (500–600 mm), but in wet years (700–900 mm) waterlogging effects were observed (Jensen et al., 2003, cited by Biazin et al.) [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit in the row points the same way, so the practice is rated as worsening waterlogging, but none of the harm sources gives a magnitude or the share of a field affected, so the strength is not quantified. The harm comes from practices that keep water on the cropped field (pits, basins, mulch, stone bunds) used outside their rainfall window, in wet years or high-rainfall zones; the row holds no evidence on storage or diversion structures. The Cameroon zaï and Burkina Faso millet losses are held out of the production classes as performance caveats and counted here as waterlogging hazard evidence [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors, and the Burkina Faso statements are cited from earlier studies [ev_crop_yield_roose93_4, ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3]. The southern African basin finding rests on a theoretical water balance plus extension reports and farmer testimony, and the author notes there are currently few published data to substantiate it [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_8]; the sub-humid conclusion goes beyond what the crop model simulates and covers conservation agriculture as basins or ripping with residue retention, so it is bundled with reduced tillage; neither gives a magnitude [ev_waterlogging_hazard_faocr11_7]. The Tanzanian tied-ridge observation is cited second-hand and gives no yield loss [ev_waterlogging_hazard_biaz12_15].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income countries the only evidence is WOCAT compiler ratings, and most say the practice improves drainage of excess water: compilers for terraces in Peru and Cabo Verde and for marab floodplain farming in Jordan rate drainage as improved, the Peruvian sheet at the top of the scale [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: The ratings split by sub-practice: the Philippine conservation-tillage sheet rates drainage worse and the Chinese check-dam sheet rates it unchanged [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage], so the improvement belongs to structures that terrace or spread runoff, not to tillage that holds water in the field. No unit is measured; these are compiler judgements without a magnitude, and none covers severe or extreme waterlogging. The measured and cited harm results under rainfed cropping come from low and lower-middle income countries and are outside this scope.

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: Practices that hold water in the field can backfire in wet conditions: stone bunds can waterlog parts of the field in wet years, millet behind stone bunds can suffer waterlogging when monthly rainfall exceeds 200 mm, and in the humid Sudanian zone of Cameroon sorghum in zaï pits yielded less than on flat-cultivated fields [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. In an Ethiopian Rift Valley trial, waterlogging lasting 3–5 days during early maize growth also affected the mulching and basin treatments, whose waterlogged plants had yellow leaves and stunted growth [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. In a Kenyan on-farm trial, ridged plots with fertiliser at the relatively wetter sub-humid Rachuonyo site gave the lowest yields, slightly below conventional practice, which the authors say can probably be explained by waterlogging caused by ridging [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit points the same way, but the harm is tied to wet years, very wet months or high-rainfall zones, and none gives the size of the yield loss or the share of field affected, so this is a warning about placing water-holding practices where water is already in excess rather than a measured penalty [ev_waterlogging_hazard_zoug14_1, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The Burkina Faso statements are cited rather than measured, and the Cameroon observation is unpublished work cited by the authors [ev_crop_yield_roose94_3, ev_crop_yield_roose93_4]. The Ethiopian waterlogging finding is a field observation with no measured yield loss, and the source names a tillage treatment as the one particularly affected, so only part of the harm can be put on mulch and basins [ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_1, ev_waterlogging_hazard_sime15h2_2]. The Kenyan ridging loss is the authors' probable explanation rather than a measured waterlogging contrast, and the ridging is bundled with fertiliser; because it comes from using the practice at a wetter site than it suits, it is held out of the production classes as an envelope misfit (a suitability caveat) and counted here as waterlogging evidence [ev_crop_yield_rock09_6].

water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.mechanism: In upper-middle-income settings, WOCAT compilers for water-harvesting works in Peru, Cabo Verde and Jordan rate drainage of excess water as improved, the Philippine conservation-tillage compiler rates it worse, and the Chinese check-dam sheet records no change [ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1506_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1573_2013_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_5770_2020_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1021_2011_excess_water_drainage, ev_waterlogging_hazard_wocat_1455_2011_excess_water_drainage].
water_harvesting_conservation__waterlogg.conditionality: Every unit is a practitioner rating of drainage on a technology sheet, with no comment and no measured waterlogging or yield loss. The measured harm in the wider pool, in-field capture that waterlogged crops in wet years or high-rainfall zones, comes mostly from low- and lower-middle-income settings and is not in this scope, so this row says only that these structures were judged to drain well where they were documented.

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: A single WOCAT compiler, for stone lines, gabions and rock check dams in Somalia, rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced, saying the structures stabilised the landscape and reduced damage from intense rainfall and stormwater runoff [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This cell is data deficient, not a finding of no effect: it rests on a single compiler rating with no measurement, and that rating concerns rain-storm damage rather than wind [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_7778_2026_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms]. A second independent source, or any measured finding on how the practice fares under cyclones or wind storms, is needed before a class can be stated.

water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.mechanism: The WOCAT compiler for mechanised Vallerani micro water harvesting in Jordan rates the impacts of cyclones and rain storms as reduced [ev_wind_cyclone_hazard_wocat_5860_2021_impacts_of_cyclones_rain_storms].
water_harvesting_conservation__wind_cycl.conditionality: This rests on a single practitioner rating with no stated reasoning, and the compilers for conservation tillage in the Philippines and stone-wall terraces in Cabo Verde rate wind velocity as unchanged [ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1021_2011_wind_velocity, ev_windbreak_protection_wocat_1573_2013_wind_velocity].
